interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, President of the Commission, Commissioners, Members, next Thursday and Friday, leaders will meet in Brussels for the European Council. At the heart of the discussions are two major strands of the EU's work this year: competitiveness and the next multiannual financial framework.

Ukraine and the Middle East will, as ever, remain important priorities. Leaders will also review progress on defence readiness and hold strategic discussions on migration and the way forward on enlargement and reforms.

Against a challenging geoeconomic backdrop, discussions will start with competitiveness. Together with Presidents Metsola and von der Leyen, leaders will review progress on the One Europe, One Market agenda. It is important to inject urgency into this work and accelerate delivery, while preserving the overall level of ambition.
This is a key message for me as Irish Presidency: we need to work together across our institutions to make sure we deliver the roadmap to enhance European competitiveness.

Leaders will also discuss the impact of the current geopolitical situation on global energy prices, and provide guidance on the way forward, given the implications for Europe's competitiveness and the cost of living.
Following their discussion in June, the leaders will return to global macroeconomic imbalances and hear from the Commission about its ongoing work to complement the EU's trade policy toolbox.
This brings me to the second key topic on the European Council agenda, which is the multiannual financial framework. We are entering a decisive phase in the negotiations.
The October European Council will be an important milestone, as the presidency this week presents its revision of the negotiating box.

Our work builds on the many exchanges and discussions held so far during our presidency. We are confident that our negotiating box will bring Member States closer to agreement by bridging Member States' positions and will prepare the ground for the final phase of negotiations, which will be under the leadership of the President of the European Council.

The discussion among leaders next week will be a pivotal moment in identifying the key elements of a balanced compromise. This will provide the necessary guidance to the President of the European Council, should he consider it appropriate to take negotiations forward, with the aim of reaching agreement by the end of the year.

On Ukraine, recent months have seen Russia step up its brutal, systematic and large-scale missile and drone attacks against civilian and critical infrastructure. Russia's latest attacks continue to kill and injure Ukrainians going about their daily lives, with more civilians killed in the first eight months this year than the whole of last year. This has put Ukraine under enormous pressure. Yet, thanks to the resilience of the Ukrainian people, Russia has failed to achieve its military and strategic objectives. Europe's solidarity with Ukraine remains steadfast in response.

Against this backdrop, the focus will be on further strengthening the EU's support for Ukraine and keeping up pressure on Russia to halt its brutal war. Key priorities ahead of winter include strengthening Ukraine's air and missile defence, protecting its critical energy infrastructure and addressing its immediate needs. The situation in the Black Sea remains another concern, with implications for grain exports and global food security.

The Middle East will also remain high on the agenda, against the backdrop of continued instability across the region. Leaders will take stock of the latest developments regarding Iran and their wider regional implications.

The situation in Gaza remains disastrous. The priorities include securing a lasting ceasefire, ensuring the full implementation of the UN Security Council Resolution 2803 by all parties, and securing unimpeded and sustained humanitarian assistance at scale into and throughout the Gaza Strip.

The situation in the West Bank also requires urgent action, in light of Israel's continuing military operations, the expansion of settlement activity, including the tender for the E1 settlement, which would have fundamental implications for the viability of the two-state solution, and continuing settler violence against Palestinians.

In Lebanon, the focus is on supporting the Lebanese state and people, and efforts to strengthen stability and security in the country. This includes preparations for the period following the end of UNIFIL's mandate and the EU's contribution in this regard.

Turning to defence readiness, it's important to maintain momentum across all strands of work. Recent hybrid attacks and acts of sabotage in Member States have only added to the urgency of making progress. These attacks have also highlighted the need to strengthen resilience and preparedness against hybrid threats. Leaders' discussions will be informed by the first annual defence readiness report, published last week.
As agreed in June, the European Council will also hold a strategic discussion on migration. Leaders will discuss the way forward, building on the results achieved.

As the Irish Presidency seeks to seize upon the recent momentum on enlargement, and seeks to make progress on the candidacies of the frontrunners of Montenegro, Albania, Moldova and Ukraine, another strategic discussion will focus on enlargement and reforms. This will be an opportunity to take stock of progress and look more broadly at how best to prepare the Union for future enlargements.

Leaders will discuss the enlargement process, the possibilities for gradual integration, and transitional measures and safeguards in future accession treaties. Indeed, the Commission's communication on these issues will be an important input into the discussion.
The objective is clear for this meeting of the leaders: to make Europe stronger, more resilient and better able to act in a rapidly changing world.

interventions.speaker_label: Ursula von der Leyen, President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Roberta, Minister, honourable Members, let me start directly with a topic that affects all of us: the high energy costs. Families and industries are paying the cost of a crisis far beyond our borders. Since the end of February, gas prices have risen by 140 %. Diesel prices have doubled. Altogether, if we look at imported fossil fuels, their costs for Europe are EUR 100 billion extra – without a single molecule of energy in addition.

We are all feeling these higher costs. Businesses are under high pressure; people struggle to pay their bills. And this could, of course, intensify as we head into the winter. We need to act now to protect those most in need, and to make sure we come out of this crisis stronger than we entered it – that we address the structural problems that are underlying this crisis.

Honourable Members, we have gone through that before. Four years ago, Russia tried to blackmail us. At that time, 45 % of our gas imports came from Russia. You will remember that almost overnight, almost everything was cut. But Europe stood together and we came out stronger. We diversified our supplies and we massively accelerated investment in home-grown clean energy. Today, our imports of Russian gas have fallen from 45 % to 12 %. And we will reduce that to zero by the end of the year.

In addition, more than 70 % of our electricity today comes from home-grown and clean sources, that is, renewables and nuclear. Because of these decisions that we took in 2022, today we are less vulnerable and in a better position. Therefore, the decisions we take today must follow the same logic. In the short term, we need to support Member States to respond to the immediate pressure. But for the mid and long term, we need to continue to address the structural issues that leave us exposed to volatile foreign fossil fuel markets. So we need to invest in our resilience.

Let me start with the short-term response. We know that energy challenges are not the same across the European Union, because every single Member State has a different energy mix. Let me give you some figures. In one Member State, for example, a megawatt hour of electricity costs around EUR 145. Here, the price is set mostly by gas. In another Member State, the same megawatt hour of electricity costs only EUR 70. Here, nuclear and renewables are setting the price.

So there is no silver bullet for the whole of the European Union. Different Member States have different energy mixes and they face different pressures. Our role is to give Member States the tools and the flexibility to respond. This is why – you will remember – in April, right at the beginning of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, we presented AccelerateEU. We introduced a temporary state aid framework for the industrial sectors most exposed, which we will prolong. And we set out options to help the households most in need.

What is very important here is that the support has to be targeted: there should be no blanket handouts, because that would only increase the demand, it would actually favour higher incomes and it entails enormous costs. So we need tailor-made support and there are good examples of this: in France and Romania, for example, energy voucher schemes provide support to low-income families. This is the right approach – very targeted, effective support for those who truly need it.

So that is for the demand side. At the same time, we are working with our partners on the supply side. Last week, G7 members agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil. This will help stabilise global prices. We will give flexibility to exporters for one more year on methane. This saves additional costs at a moment of crisis. And we will launch a strategic dialogue on European refineries. The aim here is to bring down costs and to ensure we have the supplies that we need – actually, also the supplies that we need for defence. Therefore, the strategic dialogue will be chaired by Commissioner Jørgensen and Commissioner Kubilius.

Finally, we will launch a new task force to bundle energy demand. As I said, there is a different energy mix in every Member State. Therefore, we have quite a fragmented demand side. We have done this before: when Russia tried to blackmail us, we brought together European buyers. We pooled the demand. We helped secure the supplies that Europe needed. So it is a model that works. But now we have to bring it to the next level. We want to move from simple matchmaking to aggregating demand, and then task a market operator to do the joint procurement for all of us.

So that's for the short term. As I said, most important are also the investments in the mid and long term. Honourable Members, it is one thing to respond to the immediate threat, but as long as Europe depends on oil and gas, our prosperity remains exposed to events that are beyond our control. When we import fossil fuels, we import the shocks and crises that come with them. So we must transform the way we consume energy. We need to make strategic choices today to secure our energy independence tomorrow. And that means replacing fossil fuels with clean electricity made here in Europe.

On production, we have already made real progress. Last year, for the first time, wind and solar produced more electricity than all fossil fuels combined. But we need the infrastructure to get this clean electricity to where it is needed. Here again, one figure: last year, we installed more than 80 GW of renewable capacity. That is good, but six times more is still waiting to be connected. So it is wasted. And that is why we need our grids package so urgently. You will recall, it's in your hands now to have it agreed by the end of the year. And I know that Europe can count on you.

Honourable Members, producing clean energy and getting it where it is needed is only half the job. We also need to use more of it. Today, electricity accounts for less than a quarter of our final energy consumption. Therefore, our Electrification Action Plan sets out clear targets to double that by 2040. And if we manage this, just imagine: that could help cut our fossil fuel imports by EUR 260 billion every year. Therefore, in the coming months, we will come forward with the measures to deliver on this – because every electron of clean energy we produce and use here in the European Union is energy we do not need to import from volatile global markets.

Honourable Members, the energy challenge we are facing is another reminder that our next long-term budget needs to rise to the many challenges Europe is facing. We need to step up our investments: just as a reminder, in defence and security, in competitiveness, in artificial intelligence, in energy infrastructures – we just spoke about it – in raw materials, in research, in innovation, in skills, in enlargement, in international partnerships. I could go on and on.

The priorities for the next MFF, including the need to safeguard food security and cohesion, are not challenged. We have all agreed on them. The question is one of ambition. We have proposed an MFF that preserves the current level of funding for financial support to agriculture and cohesion. At the same time, our proposal significantly boosts the financing for priorities that are currently underfunded in our budget. Some of these areas will be covered by the future competitiveness fund – but also beyond, for example, for energy infrastructure or the topic of military mobility.

Our proposal also addresses the new reality we live in and increases the funding for crises. This is the case for the agricultural reserve, for example – completely depleted now – or for natural disasters – also completely depleted – or for additional funding to tackle illegal migration. This summer, honourable Members, reminded us how critical such instruments and, of course, their funding are.

Finally, we have proposed boosting financing in areas where spending at the European level is delivering more and better results than spending nationally. Think of large-scale projects such as space. It's self-explanatory. And it is also needed for projects that simply would not be possible without European funding, for example, energy interconnection or other cross-border projects.

Honourable Members, we sometimes hear that this is not possible. Allow me to recall that we are talking about a budget of 1.26 % of the European Union's GNI. I am aware that balancing all of the constraints is not easy. I am also aware of the difficult budgetary situation in Member States. But I would like to caution against large cuts. They would risk cutting deep into critical priorities that we have all agreed on together.

This is why we have proposed a significant package of new own resources. I know that this House will support me in this. I believe that the priorities we proposed in the MFF are the right ones. If we want to preserve our priorities and the level of ambition we have for Europe, we have to do the hard work on the revenue side.
Thank you very much and long live Europe!

At the same time, our proposal significantly boosts the financing for priorities that are currently underfunded in our budget. Some of these areas will be covered by the future competitiveness fund – but also beyond, for example, for energy infrastructure or the topic of military mobility.

Our proposal also addresses the new reality we live in and increases the funding for crises. This is the case for the agricultural reserve, for example – completely depleted now – or for natural disasters – also completely depleted – or for additional funding to tackle illegal migration. This summer, honourable Members, reminded us how critical such instruments and, of course, their funding are.

Finally, we have proposed boosting financing in areas where spending at the European level is delivering more and better results than spending nationally. Think of large-scale projects such as space. It's self-explanatory. And it is also needed for projects that simply would not be possible without European funding, for example, energy interconnection or other cross-border projects.

Honourable Members, we sometimes hear that this is not possible. Allow me to recall that we are talking about a budget of 1.26 % of the European Union's GNI. I am aware that balancing all of the constraints is not easy. I am also aware of the difficult budgetary situation in Member States. But I would like to caution against large cuts. They would risk cutting deep into critical priorities that we have all agreed on together.

This is why we have proposed a significant package of new own resources. I know that this House will support me in this. I believe that the priorities we proposed in the MFF are the right ones. If we want to preserve our priorities and the level of ambition we have for Europe, we have to do the hard work on the revenue side.

Thank you very much and long live Europe!

interventions.speaker_label: Siegfried Mureşan, on behalf of the PPE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, good morning, dear colleagues. Just three weeks ago, from this plenary of the European Parliament, we gave a very important signal to the outside world by inviting Canada to strengthen its ties with the European Union. Canada is a NATO founding member. It is a G7 nation, and it is an important trading partner for the European Union. Together as liberal democracies we are also defending the values that we share. With that decision, we gave a very clear signal to the outside world that the European Union can be, for the years and decades to come, the global centre of gravity for liberal democracies, and because we have this unique opportunity, now people are looking at us.

The next European Council will be important, and the message that we have to transmit is that we have our house in order, that we know exactly what we want to do over the course of the next years: a union that is safe and secure; a union that protects its citizens and that protects its enterprises; a union that invests in innovation, that wants to become more competitive, that wants to put technology to work for the citizens; and a European Union that defends human rights, the rule of law; a European Union that is based on values, on rules and on laws.

To be sure that we can do this, indeed, Madam President, the budget of the European Union, the multiannual financial framework that we are supposed to decide together in the upcoming months, will be important. We, as a European Parliament, agree that we have to invest more in the security, in the competitiveness of the Union, continuing to provide support to our regions, to our farmers. The European Parliament does have a position on this file – it is high time that the European Council also agreed on the position on the multiannual financial framework, so that we can have negotiations between Parliament and the Council as soon as possible.

We need a budget which is sufficient, because, if the budget is insufficient, the challenges that we are facing are not disappearing. Member States will have to tackle them at national level. It will be more expensive. This is why this European Parliament will in no way be in a position to approve a budget which is insufficient, which contains unjustified cuts, because it would weaken Europe. It would only be fuel for the populists. This being said, every prime minister coming to the European Council and wanting to pay as little as possible to the European Union and benefit as much as possible – that is not European.

So our task, together, will be to defend a budget which is good for every Member State of the Union, but also good and sufficient for the European Union. That will also be key to the image that we are going to project in the next years to our citizens, to our enterprises, but also to the outside world.

interventions.speaker_label: Iratxe García Pérez, en nombre del Grupo S&D.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, hay una pregunta que deberíamos hacernos antes de hablar del próximo presupuesto europeo, y es ¿qué Europa queremos construir?

Porque hoy hay dos Europas en disputa. Está la Europa que recorta, que enfrenta la cohesión con la competitividad, la agricultura con la defensa, la inversión social con la seguridad. Es la Europa que finge hacer más con menos, pero es imposible hacer más con menos. ¿Cómo vamos a recortar el presupuesto cuando las guerras de Trump, Putin y Netanyahu están encareciendo el precio de la energía y haciendo la vida más difícil a millones de europeos? ¿Cuando los agricultores pierden sus cosechas por los incendios, las sequías y las inundaciones? ¿Cuando nuestras familias no pueden pagar una vivienda?

Nosotros defendemos otra Europa: la Europa de la cohesión que construye hospitales, escuelas, carreteras y empleo en nuestras regiones; la Europa de nuestros agricultores, que alimentan a los ciudadanos, protegen nuestro territorio y merecen una renta digna; la Europa competitiva, que sabe que nuestra industria solo será fuerte si aceleramos el Pacto Verde; la Europa que se defiende frente a las amenazas de Trump y frente a la guerra híbrida de Putin; y, sobre todo, la Europa social, la que pone la vivienda en el centro. Porque una unión que habla de prosperidad mientras una generación entera no puede acceder a una casa está fallando a sus ciudadanos.

Y lo hemos visto en países como España, cuando hay fuerzas políticas que prefieren ponerse del lado de los grandes grupos de inversión y de los fondos buitre antes que del lado de la gente que de verdad necesita una política digna.

Y por eso necesitamos una Europa que se atreva; que se atreva con los poderosos y los grandes beneficiarios del mercado único con recursos propios procedentes de las grandes plataformas digitales, del juego en línea y de las criptomonedas. Y una Europa justa que haga pagar a las compañías energéticas por sus beneficios extraordinarios para crear un bono social que ayude a las familias con la luz, la calefacción, la gasolina y la cesta de la compra.

Presidenta Von der Leyen, se lo pido directamente: proponga un impuesto sobre los beneficios extraordinarios de las compañías energéticas, porque es inaceptable que se enriquezcan con los beneficios de las guerras mientras nuestros ciudadanos no llegan a fin de mes. Y presione a los Estados: no permita que este presupuesto nazca mutilado por los recortes.

El presupuesto europeo no es una hoja de Excel, es una decisión política sobre quién queremos ser. Nosotros queremos una Europa que esté al lado de la gente cuando más lo necesita, porque esa Europa no solo es posible: es la única Europa que merece la pena construir y defender.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Elnök Asszonyok, Miniszter Úr! Kollégák! A jövő heti uniós csúcs előtt elismételhetném újra, mi nincs rendben Európában. Beszélhetnénk a magas energiaárakról, az illegális migráció miatt romló közbiztonságról, az MFF hibás prioritásairól, a gazdákat és kohéziót érintő pénzelvonásokról, újabb adókról.

Mi, Patrióták, évek óta hiába kongatjuk a vészharangokat, hogy az Unió rossz irányba halad, és hogy gyökeres irányváltás kell. Mit tesz közben a Bizottság? A hibáktól nem okulva, valódi megoldások helyett továbbra is központosít, bürokráciát épít, és ideológiai célok mentén akarja meghatározni Európa jövőjét.

Az elmúlt másfél évtizedben Önök állandóan farkast kiáltottak, számonkérve a jogállamiságot az előző patrióta magyar kormányon, most az új magyar kormány önkényt épít. Ellenzéki politikusokat zárnak ki a politikai versenyből, politikailag motivált büntetőeljárásokat indítanak ellenük, és aránytalan kényszerintézkedéseket alkalmaznak megfélemlítés céljából.

Mindez a kommunista időket idézi számunkra, de az uniós intézmények részéről néma csend van. A hallgatás csak egyet jelenthet: annak a nyilvánvaló beismerését, hogy a TISZA-kormány demokráciát korlátozó lépései a Bizottság és a Tanács támogató hallgatásával, sőt ösztönzésére történnek. Beigazolódott, hogy a jogállamiság itt csak addig számít, ameddig azt patrióta kormányok zsarolására, büntetésére lehet használni.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signora Presidente von der Leyen, il prossimo Consiglio europeo si riunisce mentre fuori la realtà continua a bussare con molta forza. Con l'aumento del costo dei carburanti, la fiammata inflazionistica sta di nuovo travolgendo le famiglie e soffocando le imprese.

Io non mi stancherò mai di ripeterlo: è sbagliato dividersi in due squadre, quella delle fonti rinnovabili e quella delle fonti fossili. Lo scopo della partita è un altro: dobbiamo essere più autonomi nell'autoproduzione di energia, qualunque ne sia la fonte, anziché essere costretti a comprarla da fuori, da altri. Invece, qui dentro tutto continua a girare sempre intorno al feticcio della decarbonizzazione.

L'autonomia strategica è l'unica strada per essere resilienti di fronte agli shock geopolitici che possono sopraggiungere da un momento all'altro. Vale per l'energia come per la difesa militare. Non è certo un caso se il primo nucleo fondativo dell'Unione si sia coagulato proprio intorno al carbone e all'acciaio. Sovranità energetica e sicurezza sono le due facce della stessa medaglia.

A tal proposito, due notizie importanti sono arrivate dalla Lettonia. La prima riguarda il rischio di fallimento di Air Baltic. Dai suoi libri contabili abbiamo saputo che il suo principale creditore è lo Stato lettone, o meglio l'Unione europea, a cui la compagnia europea deve versare oltre quaranta milioni di euro di quote ETS. Una tassa mostruosa, che crea un mostruoso svantaggio competitivo tra le aziende europee e il resto del mondo, senza aiutare l'ambiente.

Il CEO di Lufthansa ha messo in fila due numeri impressionanti: l'Unione europea produce appena il 5 % delle emissioni mondiali di gas serra, ma contribuisce con oltre l'80 % alle entrate mondiali derivanti dai sistemi di scambio delle emissioni.

La seconda notizia che arriva dalla Lettonia è la grande vittoria del premier Kulbergs e della famiglia politica dei conservatori. I cittadini chiedono fermezza sui confini, sicurezza, rispetto della propria identità nazionale e un drastico ritorno al buon senso in economia.
Il Consiglio europeo ascolti finalmente questa voce prima che siano le crisi a travolgere l'Europa.

interventions.speaker_label: Valérie Hayer, au nom du groupe Renew.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Ministre, chers collègues, à quelques jours de ce sommet européen, je voudrais commencer par un chiffre: 360 milliards. 360 milliards d'euros, c'est le déficit commercial de l'Union européenne avec la Chine en 2025. Près d'un milliard d'euros par jour. Ce que révèle ce chiffre, c'est qu'on ne lutte pas à armes égales. La Chine organise le déséquilibre commercial avec l'Union européenne. Alors, Madame la Présidente, nous devons durcir notre doctrine commerciale, justement parce que nous soutenons un commerce international basé sur des règles claires. Ce sont ces règles qui protègent nos emplois et nos entreprises et qui nous permettent de renforcer notre compétitivité. L'ouverture de notre marché reste évidemment un atout, mais il ne peut pas se faire sans la mise en œuvre d'une sécurité économique européenne réellement efficace. À cet égard, les positions évoluent et je m'en félicite. Alors, Madame la Présidente, nous attendons vos annonces prochaines sur ces questions fondamentales pour l'avenir de notre économie européenne.

Deuxième point que je souhaite aborder, cela a déjà été évoqué par mes prédécesseurs, le budget européen. On va dire les choses franchement: on sait tous aujourd'hui les tensions qu'il y a autour de la sortie de la "nego-box". Mais la réalité, c'est qu'il n'y a qu'un seul budget qui vaille. Pas de coupes drastiques. Et c'est aussi une proposition ambitieuse sur les ressources propres. Monsieur le Ministre, cher Thomas, vous savez que vous avez tout notre soutien. Vous savez aussi quelles sont nos exigences. Vous les connaissez parfaitement. Pas d'accord du Parlement sans avancer sur les ressources propres. Et là aussi, on sait quels sont les freins. Alors il faut qu'on soit créatifs ensemble.

Dernier point – et je m'adresse ici directement au Conseil, bien au-delà de la présidence irlandaise –, sur ce sujet comme sur beaucoup d'autres, vous êtes trop lents. Le Parlement européen, il fait son travail législatif sur l'élargissement, sur le budget, sur l'Ukraine, sur la défense européenne, sur la mise en œuvre du rapport Draghi. Mais que font les États? Cela fait plus de deux ans maintenant qu'on attend que nos dirigeants se mettent d'accord sur ces sujets comme sur d'autres. Et sur toutes ces priorités: des blocages, des tergiversations, du temps perdu, de l'inertie. Alors il faut y aller, maintenant. Chers collègues, on le sait tous: les Européens nous regardent. Ce n'est pas demain qu'il faut agir, c'est maintenant.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Minister, dear colleagues, this EUCO is absolutely crucial for the MFF, and I have two messages to the European leaders.

First, if you think for one second that this Parliament is like previous Parliaments and that you can basically just present us with a fait accompli at the end of the negotiations and then we are going to swallow it, we are heading for disaster and you will be responsible for it. Building majorities is very, very difficult in this House and we managed to do it in the interim report. So let that be your guiding light when you are negotiating on where you want to head with the MFF.

Secondly, without own resources, we will simply not make it work. You want to pay less in national contributions? Well, there is a way to do that: stop blocking sensible ways of financing the European budget.

On enlargement, colleagues, yes, we absolutely need a positive story. I want the European Union to grow, enabling more people to become EU citizens. But, Commission President, if you go to a candidate country that has seen mass protests for more than 130 days, and not just on anything – because the Flamingo Revolution is largely about EU values, it is about upholding EU law – and you do not even mention that, we have a problem. Albania is the prime example. People outside the European Union are not looking for accession just for the sake of accession. They want to have rights as EU citizens, they want to be protected from corruption and they want to have better lives.

That is the vision, colleagues, that we have to give to people in candidate countries. We need to have a merit-based process, a strong focus on rule of law, and we need clear commitments from the European side, and we also need to stand up to those commitments, even if some Member States are making it difficult.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! In Berlin gewinnt die Linke die Wahlen, weil meine Partei glaubwürdig das zentrale Problem dieser Stadt angehen wird. Die Menschen können sich die Mieten nicht mehr leisten. Und meine Genossin Elif Eralp, bald Bürgermeisterin von Berlin, wird das ändern. In Spanien geht eine halbe Million Menschen auf die Straße für bezahlbaren Wohnraum. Auslöser war die Zwangsräumung der 87-jährigen Maricarmen aus ihrer Wohnung, in der sie fast ihr gesamtes Leben verbracht hat. Skrupellose Miethaie hatten die Miete von Maricarmen von 500 EUR auf 2 650 EUR im Monat erhöht. Sie darf jetzt in ihrer Wohnung bleiben. Der Widerstand hat sich gelohnt.

Doch der Kampf um ein bezahlbares Leben geht weiter. Basta! Es reicht! Wohnen ist ein Menschenrecht. Die Mieten müssen runter. In Berlin, in Madrid, in Paris, in Athen, in vielen europäischen Städten. In den Metropolen brennt die Luft. Die Spritpreise explodieren. Menschen können ihre Tankfüllung und ihren Weg zur Arbeit kaum noch bezahlen. Die Lebensmittelpreise explodieren. Familien müssen jeden Euro und Cent zusammenhalten, damit sie den Wocheneinkauf gestemmt kriegen.

Die Menschen können sich das Leben nicht mehr leisten, aber damit will sich der EU-Rat nicht befassen. In Frankreich streiken genau jetzt und heute wieder Schüler und Studierende für ihre Zukunft und gegen den Sparhammer. Keine Regierung, die noch bei Verstand ist, kürzt an der Bildung der jungen Menschen und damit bei denjenigen, die unsere Zukunft sind. Die Regierung Macron hat abgewirtschaftet. Frankreich braucht eine klare soziale und antifaschistische Perspektive. Bald stehen Wahlen in Spanien, in Frankreich, in Italien, in Polen, in Griechenland, in Finnland an und die Linke ist bereit für diesen Kampf, weil wir mit den Menschen für ein bezahlbares Leben kämpfen, weil wir die Zukunft unserer Jugend sichern wollen.

interventions.speaker_label: René Aust, im Namen der ESN-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Zwei deutsche Forscher haben den Nobelpreis für Medizin erhalten. Herzlichen Glückwunsch! Ich finde, dieser Nobelpreis zeigt noch mehr, nämlich, was in unserem Land und auf unserem Kontinent mit unseren Kulturen, unserer Wissenschaftstradition und unserer Forschungsinfrastruktur noch immer möglich ist.

So stellen wir uns Deutschland und Europa im Jahr 2050 vor: ein Land und Kontinent, in dem wir Krankheiten heilen können, die heute noch als unheilbar gelten, weil die besten Forscher der Welt bei uns arbeiten, in dem neue Kernkraftwerke zuverlässig Energie liefern und Strom für unsere Industrie und unsere Familien wieder bezahlbar ist. Umso bemerkenswerter, dass Frau von der Leyen auch heute wieder die Kernkraft lobend hervorgehoben hat. Als CDU-Mitglied hat sie in der Regierung den beschleunigten Ausstieg mit beschlossen, und die CSU in Bayern, die baut den Rückbau von Kernkraftwerken voran, was den Wiedereinstieg schwieriger macht in der Zukunft. Kernkraft und Zukunft gibt es eben nur mit der AfD.

Stellen wir uns vor: Roboter in Fabriken der Zukunft, die unsere Fabriken produktiver machen und Millionen von Mechatronikern, Technikern, Ingenieuren Arbeit geben, weil sie diese Maschinen und Roboter bauen, programmieren und warten. All das ist möglich, wenn Schluss ist mit dem Glauben, dass Politik aus Brüssel unsere Zukunft besser gestalten könne als wir selbst. Es muss Schluss sein mit den Fesseln aus Bürokratie, übervorsichtigen Vorschriften und Verboten, damit die Bürger wieder selbstständig tätig sein können als Forscher, als Erfinder, mit Investitionen, und mutig sein können, um die Zukunft zu erreichen. Im Übrigen, Frau von der Leyen, Sie sagten gerade eben: Long live Europe! Ich möchte das ergänzen: Lang leben die Völker Europas!

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, los objetivos y el presupuesto deben ser ambiciosos. Son la única vía para ser competitivos. Ganar en innovación; tener un mix energético para garantizar nuestra soberanía y el futuro de los jóvenes con empleo de calidad y vivienda, sin olvidar la PAC, la pesca y la cohesión; celebrar nuevos acuerdos comerciales, y completar la gran asignatura pendiente, el mercado único, son nuestras herramientas geopolíticas en un mundo cada vez más hostil.

Avancemos hacia la Unión de Ahorro e Inversiones para que las empresas autónomas y familias se financien y escalen sin trabas. Eliminemos burocracia a todos los niveles, porque simplificar en Europa, mientras los Gobiernos nacionales regulan más, es trasladar la burocracia de una mesa a otra. Si Europa quiere ser una superpotencia, debe competir como tal, no fragmentada en veintisiete mercados, sino unida. Esta unidad que hemos logrado, por ejemplo, en el pacto migratorio y en el Reglamento de retornos.

Europa ha entendido que no hay soberanía sin fronteras seguras y que solo Europa decide quién entra en Europa. Por eso Ceuta no está sola y por eso fracasan los autócratas como Sánchez. Todo va a cambiar el 29 de noviembre. España dejará atrás por fin ocho años de fracasos, de corrupción y de alianzas con nuestros enemigos para volver al lugar que nunca debió abandonar en el corazón de Europa, con un Gobierno digno y con un presidente decente y con todos los españoles votando en las urnas.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, you would almost forget, Council, that enlargement is on your agenda.

And, dear colleagues, enlargement is not just a nice thing to have or a tick-the-box exercise. It's essential for the future of our continent and our European Union. And it is time for us in Europe to deliver.
Keeping countries endlessly in the waiting room weakens democratic forces. It undermines the trust in the EU and it creates space for Russia and other anti-democratic forces.

We need four things. A credible timeline, so no endless waiting. No unanimity for every step. A faster, gradual integration – if you meet conditions, you should already benefit from closer integration and gradually from full membership. And fourth, Europe must uphold its social model as a guarantee of prosperity.
And there is one red line for our political group, and that is no compromise on the rule of law, democracy and European values.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Jetzt einmal ehrlich: Ist es Ihnen nicht zu dämlich, hier rauszugehen und sich selbst zu beweihräuchern, während den Menschen draußen das Geld zum Leben fehlt, während die Preise explodieren, die Energiekosten ins Unermessliche gehen, Arbeitslosigkeit und Konkurse immer weiter nach oben gehen? Sie kommen hier heraus, geben noch ein Bussibussi zur Kommissionspräsidentin, lassen Weinflaschen für die Kommissionspräsidentin da. Das ist ein klägliches Scheitern Ihrer Politik. Das ist ein Totalversagen, das Sie hier dokumentieren.

Wenn Sie die Ratssitzung jetzt hier im Auge haben und das diskutieren und debattieren, was seit Jahr und Tag debattiert wird, und es immer und immer schlechter wird, von der Wettbewerbsfähigkeit bis zur Migration, kann ich nur sagen, das einzig Richtige wäre: Demissionieren Sie, machen Sie Platz für eine Politik, die eine andere ist als die Ihre. 27 Kommissare haben Sie – völlig aufgeblasen. 18 sollten und dürften es sein nach Lissabon. Jetzt wollen Sie weitere zwei Kommissare machen, das Ganze noch mehr aufblasen. Das ist der falsche Weg. Und der Kurs, den Sie fahren, da ist die Titanic noch ein sicheres Schiff dagegen und ein guter Kurs. Das, was Sie tun, führt diesen Kontinent in den Abgrund. Hören Sie auf damit und machen Sie eine Schubumkehr.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Wieloletnie ramy finansowe mają, wnioskując z wypowiedzi Pani Przewodniczącej von der Leyen, po raz kolejny stać się po prostu narzędziem do wprowadzania zielonego szaleństwa, ideologizacji Unii Europejskiej. No tak nie może być, jeżeli one mają działać, jeżeli te pieniądze mają sensownie być wydawane, a dzisiaj Europa potrzebuje inwestycji, potrzebują rodziny europejskie wsparcia, to te pieniądze muszą być wydawane mądrze i nie można powielać błędów, które robiło się przez tyle lat. Przecież to nic innego, tylko Zielony Ład i ETS wykończył europejski przemysł.

Dzisiaj tworzycie Państwo fundusz konkurencyjności, który ma wspierać upadające przedsiębiorstwa europejskie. Ale dlaczego one mają problem? Mają problem przez błędną politykę Unii Europejskiej i można tak wymieniać w nieskończoność. Co oznacza nowe zasoby finansowe, o których mówi tutaj Pani Przewodnicząca. No nic innego, tylko podatki. Kto za to płaci? Kto za to zapłaci? Europejczycy. Tą drogą naprawdę nie wyjdziemy z kryzysu, w którym tkwi Unia Europejska.

paragraphs.text: (Start of speech off mic) ... Council welcome this debate. Security and defence are a priority. Energy independence, enlargement and ensuring that we remain competitive or build our competitiveness back – these are all key important factors for the European Union.

However, a lot of threats to the European Union come from within the Council, and that is an area that we have to address through the multiannual financial framework. We have to ensure that there is a budget that delivers for citizens. We simply cannot have a situation where we are trying to explain to citizens over the next number of years that Europe simply doesn't have the capacity to deliver in real, tangible terms. So I would urge the Council to come forward with a proposal that is meaningful in terms of underpinning the values of the European Union not just in words but in actions and with support and finance.

We talk about cohesion funding. We talk about the common agricultural policy. But clearly, if we can't fund schemes that have underpinned the cohesion of the European Union for the last 40 years, well, then we will politically undermine it. So I urge that a budget is brought forward that will at least allow us to support citizens and underpin the values of the European Union through financial measures.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Council, colleagues, imagine a comet heading to Earth. Instead of trying to stop it, leaders say, 'Nah, it's not a priority this quarter.' Isn't there a chance it could destroy Earth? Maybe. But it's full of gold and diamonds. 'If we don't get it,' say the Americans, 'the Chinese will get it first.' This doesn't only resemble the movie Don't Look Up; it also sums up the sad state of the current AI debate.

Even if the end of humanity claims are overblown, and I believe they are, there's still plenty to worry about: increased cybercrime, climate change, democratic erosion, autonomous warfare, lost jobs, a market crash when the AI bubble bursts, and our dependence on foreign tech. This desperately needs a new voice, and Europe can become that voice, but it's not even on the agenda of the next Council summit. We urge the Council to look up, organise a dedicated summit and make a plan around one single question: how does Europe make AI that benefits humanity?

paragraphs.text: A Uachtaráin, agus fáilte a Aire Byrne.

I want to begin by sending solidarity to the residents and the community of the Garvaghy Road in the north of Ireland. Their courage and determination in standing up for and protecting their community has prevented a sectarian and hateful Orange Order march from proceeding down the Garvaghy Road.

But let us be very clear: this situation should never have arisen in the first place. Twenty-eight years of peace was not a problem that needed to be solved. And we are not going back to the past in the north of Ireland. The days of second-class citizenship for nationalists are over.

It is now time for this Parliament, and particularly I urge the Council in their upcoming meeting, to send a strong and unequivocal message to the north's Secretary of State: this march cannot and should not go ahead.

This Parliament should stand resolutely with the residents and the community of the Garvaghy Road, with their right to live in peace and with the principles that have underpinned the peace process for the past 28 years.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Mają Państwo niezwykły talent. Najpierw uchwalacie przepisy, które dławią przedsiębiorców, a potem debatujecie, dlaczego gospodarka traci konkurencyjność.

Nawet przy kilku zamówieniach rocznie to koszt tysięcy euro rocznie. Efekty? Żaglownia z Giżycka po 35 latach zapowiada zawieszenie działalności. paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, je propose de renommer le Conseil européen, l'Assemblée de nos chefs d'État et de gouvernement, en «Conseil ukrainien» et de remplacer son président, M. Costa, par M. Zelensky. En effet, le Conseil européen se fiche visiblement des citoyens européens et de leurs problèmes. Dans son projet de conclusions, il consacre exactement douze lignes à la compétitivité et une ligne à la crise migratoire. L'Ukraine, en revanche, a droit à 104 lignes, plus 64 au titre de la défense. En résumé, 168 lignes de soutien inconditionnel à M. Zelensky, et treize lignes pour les soucis quotidiens de nos citoyens.

Comme nous n'avons plus les moyens pour financer cette guerre, il faut enfin parler de diplomatie et négocier avec la Russie. Malheureusement, le Conseil européen préfère encore négliger les problèmes des Européens au profit du régime corrompu de M. Zelensky. Dans beaucoup de nos pays, on entend réduire les prestations sociales ou les pensions. Il n'en saurait être question.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, hybrid attacks across Europe have unfortunately become the new normal. We face sabotage, cyber attacks, foreign interference and disinformation campaigns on a daily basis. Hostile actors like Russia and Iran seek to undermine our security and democracy. The message from the European Council must, therefore, be clear: Europe cannot continue to be reactive. We must counter hybrid threats.
First, we need stronger cooperation at European level. Europol has a crucial role to play in supporting Member States. This must be reflected in the agency's updated mandate.

Secondly, we must strengthen our defence. This means, of course, continue supporting Ukraine, but it also means strengthening Europe's military capabilities. We need a strong European pillar of defence.

Thirdly, we also must make sure that we have a proper and strong response when it comes to protecting our democracy. We need a European democracy shield that actually means that we are protecting our elections and our democratic systems.
This House has demanded a strong response to hybrid threats. Now it's time for the Council to step up and protect Europe.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señor presidente, señor comisario, señorías, a los llamados países frugales —o mejor dicho, a sus respectivos Gobiernos— los socialistas españoles les decimos que tenemos hambre de más Europa, que no podemos hacer más política europea con menos recursos.

Los frugales marcan como sus prioridades la seguridad y la defensa, la competitividad, la innovación y la lucha contra la inmigración irregular; los socialistas queremos, además, responder a las expectativas de la ciudadanía y a los nuevos desafíos, manteniendo la cohesión social y territorial, las políticas tradicionales como la PAC —que son los pilares de la construcción europea— y defendiendo la migración regular, que es necesaria y positiva.

Y si hemos decidido avanzar hacia un destino común no podemos pensar en términos nacionales: debemos, más que nunca, mancomunar recursos y apostar por los recursos propios, como el gravamen sobre las grandes plataformas digitales, los juegos de azar en línea o los criptoactivos.

Señorías, sin voluntad política ni ambición presupuestaria la Unión puede quedarse fuera del mapa mundial, con unas sociedades cada vez más desiguales, empobrecidas y polarizadas. Son tiempos de valentía política y presupuestaria.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, se la signora von der Leyen fosse rimasta in Aula, le avrei detto che siamo alle solite: chi crea i problemi dopo viene in quest'Aula anche a spiegarci come risolverli.
Dobbiamo riconoscere che c'è un immobilismo, nell'attuale crisi energetica dell'Unione, nella gestione della crisi del gas.
Va fatta anche una riflessione su quello che è lo scarso peso, la scarsa capacità dell'Unione, nel ridisegnare le geografie degli shock energetici e nelle dinamiche delle relazioni tra gli Stati.

Guardiamo ad esempio gli Stati Uniti: abbiamo un sistema energetico che una volta era importatore di energia e che invece adesso funziona, è diventato esportatore e ha anche la capacità di resistere a tutti questi shock esterni.

Avrei voluto anche ricordare alla signora von der Leyen che una volta c'era uno uno spread, un differenziale del 30 %, tra il prezzo del petrolio greggio e quello che si pagava alla pompa. Invece adesso, a causa del fatto che l'Unione ha depresso gli investimenti sulle raffinerie, noi ci troviamo che questo spread è il doppio, e quindi si paga praticamente il doppio la benzina rispetto a quello che è il prezzo del greggio.
Pensiamo agli Stati Uniti e pensiamo alle altre economie e avremo un quadro chiaro. Gli altri galoppano e in Europa, come sempre, si passeggia.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, en avril dernier, ce Parlement a adopté le rapport de mon collègue Carlo Fidanza sur l'élevage: réduction de notre dépendance aux protéines importées, défense des paiements directs aux agriculteurs, accès au foncier et au crédit. Mais depuis, qu'a fait madame von der Leyen de ces recommandations? Dans cette institution, la souveraineté agricole est un slogan, ça n'est pas une politique réelle. Après le Mercosur et les contraintes intenables du Pacte vert, elle envisage aujourd'hui de réduire de 87 milliards d'euros le budget garanti à notre agriculture, en passant de 387 à 300 milliards. Pire, elle proposerait d'instaurer une PAC mise en concurrence avec d'autres politiques nationales. En France, l'été 2026 a été dévastateur: des pertes de rendement atteignant 50 % dans certains territoires et un déficit de 40 % de la pousse des prairies. La récolte de maïs pourrait être la plus faible depuis 1980; dans les Deux-Sèvres et en Charente-Maritime, 64 % des agriculteurs interrogés envisagent d'arrêter leur activité. Alors, combien de chiffres faudra-t-il encore à la Commission pour écouter la détresse de nos paysans?

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, Council, the last time we met in this chamber, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney was among us. He talked about Europe and Canada being much stronger together, together with the other middle powers, to preserve a world order based on our values – an order that served us so well and gave us prosperity.

Mark Carney emphasised the strength of togetherness, not what could divide us. And what a contrast with the European Council. On the future budget, on enlargement and reforms, on competitiveness, our Member States seem to focus more on their differences than on their common strength.

We all know the EU needs a more modern and bigger budget. So get it done. We all know we need to take new Member States up and we need institutional reforms. So get it done. And we all know that only a truly European approach will make our economy stronger. So get it done.

paragraphs.text: Gospod predsednik! Pred zasedanjem želim sporočiti dve temeljni opozorili.

Prvič, kohezijska politika ne sme biti predmet pogajanj. Zmanjšanje sredstev za kohezijo, da bi z njimi financirali nove prednostne naloge, kot je obramba, bi pomenilo, da bodo revnejši plačali za varnost bogatejših. Že danes je razmerje med razvitimi in nerazvitimi regijami ena proti pet, zato številni upravičeno menijo, da jih je Evropska unija preprosto pozabila. Zato nevarnost za Evropsko unijo ni zunaj nje, ampak v evroskepticizmu znotraj nje.

Drugič, pripravite se za širitev Evropske unije. Če bomo še naprej odlašali, bomo Zahodni Balkan dokončno izgubili. Medtem ko oklevamo, se Srbija, Bosna in Hercegovina in Severna Makedonija oddaljujejo od nas. Črni gori je potrebno določiti kristalno jasen datum za širitev in pristop.
Brez širitve Evropske unije na Zahodnem Balkanu imamo samo še več nacionalizma. Če Evropska unija ne bo zapolnila tega prostora, bodo to praznino zapolnili drugi.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, so the energy crisis is here again, and we warned that this would be one of the consequences of Trump's illegal attack on Iran.

Now Giorgia Meloni is pushing for new exemptions to the EU fiscal rules, asking the question of why defence investments get differential treatment, while energy crisis measures do not. It is a fair question, but she is a perfect example of how it is the same politicians who want to weaken our climate policies and maintain our fossil fuel dependency that now want to pour more public money into fossil fuel subsidies.

Multinational oil majors' profits have doubled since the start of the Iran war. They must be made to pay a part of the bill and help address the fundamental problem, which is our dependency on imported fossil energy.

So, yes, please decide to change the fiscal rules, but do it to enable investment in renewable energy and in electrification, so we do not have to encounter the same energy crisis over and over again.

Multinational oil majors' profits have doubled since the start of the Iran war. They must be made to pay a part of the bill and help address the fundamental problem, which is our dependency on imported fossil energy.

So, yes, please decide to change the fiscal rules, but do it to enable investment in renewable energy and in electrification, so we do not have to encounter the same energy crisis over and over again.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhor Comissário e Senhor Ministro, 45 % é a tarifa equivalente que as empresas europeias pagam todos os dias, não em Washington, não em Pequim, mas dentro das nossas próprias fronteiras, e, nos serviços, esse número ultrapassa os 100 %. 45 %. Passámos meses a negociar com Washington um teto de 15 % e esquecemo‑nos de que as maiores barreiras ao comércio europeu fomos nós a construí‑las.

O nosso maior adversário na competitividade chama‑se mercado interno incompleto. O EU Inc. é um passo concreto para as derrubar. Mas transformar o 28.º regime numa diretiva é voltar ao ponto de partida, é criar 27 versões de uma solução pensada para resolver 27 versões.

Queremos um regime único, opcional para quem empreende, obrigatório para quem governa. Em março, os chefes de Governo e de Estado fizeram dele uma prioridade. Portanto, eu peço‑lhes agora que levem essa ambição até ao fim, até ao final do ano. Mas sejamos claros, Senhor Comissário, se o EU Inc. for esvaziado do seu propósito, se deixar de ser um regime verdadeiramente europeu, igual em Coimbra ou em Copenhaga, então mais vale retirar a proposta.

Um vigésimo oitavo regime que se transforma num 28.º labirinto não serve nenhuma empresa. Serve apenas para fingirmos que fizemos alguma coisa, porque na corrida pela competitividade a Europa não perde para os Estados Unidos nem para a China, perde‑se para si própria.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Deputada, Lídia Pereira, falando de competitividade, a pergunta que lhe faço é: não acha que era tempo de a União Europeia e os governos nacionais intervirem nos preços da energia e dos combustíveis, controlando os preços e enfrentando as multinacionais que estão a procurar acumular lucros utilizando a guerra como pretexto? É que a senhora presidente da Comissão Europeia já reconheceu que o aumento dos preços em consequência da guerra dos Estados Unidos contra o Irão já significou 90 mil milhões de euros pagos pelos povos no aumento dos preços. Não acha que era tempo de se intervir nessa matéria? E, particularmente, o Conselho Europeu devia fazer disso uma prioridade que está completamente ausente da agenda da próxima reunião?

paragraphs.text: Senhor Deputado, eu sou uma insuspeita defensora da transição energética, tenho defendido neste plenário, nos últimos sete anos, que é essencial que nós transitemos para um mercado que não esteja dependente de outros mercados para funcionar e que não ponha em causa a competitividade europeia.

Se há coisa que mais defendo é a proatividade do presidente do Conselho Europeu e que passe a trabalhar como um verdadeiro presidente e não como um secretário‑geral. Portanto, se não está na agenda, é uma coisa que o Senhor Presidente António Costa deveria de facto empreender, e colocar à consideração dos chefes de Estado.

Precisamos mesmo de resolver o problema que temos do mercado energético europeu, não é um verdadeiro mercado, é um mercado fragmentado, e é um problema que só podemos resolver se empreendermos a transição energética e, como a senhora presidente da Comissão aqui disse, se não nos desviarmos do caminho que temos percorrido até hoje.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, in un paese dell'Appennino la scuola ha un tetto nuovo grazie ai fondi europei, un Comune potrebbe avere le case popolari grazie ai fondi europei e un agricoltore potrebbe avere un trattore grazie ai fondi europei.

Ora i governi di destra ci dicono che dobbiamo tagliare il bilancio e dobbiamo scegliere quali dei tre tagliamo. Noi diciamo no! La domanda è sbagliata. Perché dovremmo scegliere? Perché dovremo scegliere di tagliare qualcosa di queste tre opportunità?
Quelle stesse destre, poi, bloccano ogni nuova entrata europea. Sovranisti con tutti, eccetto che con i giganti del web.

Noi diciamo debito comune e contribuisca chi oggi non lo fa: grandi piattaforme digitali, gioco d'azzardo online, crypto-attività, fino a 32 miliardi di euro ogni anno. Così non si sceglie tra la casa, la scuola e il trattore, ma si tengono tutte e tre. Così non si uccide la speranza di farcela, ma si ridà fiducia nei confronti di chi la fiducia l'ha persa.
Commissione, dovete avere coraggio! Ai governi diciamo che si può fare, si può avere coraggio e dobbiamo farlo.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, Nexit is de enige optie voor Nederland. Mijn partij, de Partij voor de Vrijheid, heeft even gehoopt dat hervormingen binnen de Europese Unie mogelijk waren. Het tegenovergestelde bleek waar te zijn. Nederland lijdt immers onder het wanbeleid van andere lidstaten. Zo beloont de socialistische regering in Madrid op grote schaal illegalen met een verblijfsvergunning, die daardoor zonder onze instemming naar Nederland kunnen afreizen. Het wanbeleid van de andere lidstaten raakt tevens aan onze welvaart. Terwijl Nederland bezuinigt om de pensioenen en sociale zekerheid betaalbaar te houden, weigeren andere lidstaten hetzelfde te doen. En draait de Nederlandse belastingbetaler op voor de schulden en risico's van andere eurolanden. Ondertussen holt de levensstandaard van de Nederlander hard achteruit en blijven de bodemloze utopieën van de EU ons miljarden kosten. Dit is waarom wij de zeggenschap over onze grenzen, ons geld en ons beleid willen terugnemen en waarom de Partij voor de Vrijheid terugkeert naar haar Nexit-standpunt. De bevolking van IJsland had gelijk toen zij de EU afwees. Ook Nederlanders moeten die keuze kunnen maken.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, commissaris, minister, waar het in de State of the Union aan ontbrak, hoop ik dat de Raad de focus voluit teruglegt op productiviteit en concurrentievermogen. Dat wil zeggen: deregulering die daadwerkelijk regels schrapt; een kapitaalmarktunie die tot echte marktintegratie leidt; structureel lagere energieprijzen en meer ruimte voor investeringen, innovatie en groei. Maar al die inspanningen zijn een maat voor niets als onze bedrijven niet op een gelijk speelveld kunnen spelen. Europa is wat dat betreft veel te lang naïef geweest ten aanzien van China. China verstoort het speelveld grondig, en wel via vier structurele elementen: massale overheidssubsidies, afscherming van de eigen markt, een kunstmatig ondergewaardeerde munt en grootschalige diefstal van intellectuele eigendom. Wordt het geen tijd om eens ernstig na te denken over een heffing van 10 % of meer op alle Chinese import? Moeten we daarbij rekening houden met forse tegenreacties? Waarschijnlijk wel, maar de prijs die we vandaag betalen voor passiviteit is zo mogelijk nog hoger.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, dear representative of the Council, dear Thomas, next week, the European Council will try to sort out all the problems on the agenda, so let me save you some time.
The source of all the problems is sitting around the table. Maybe you don't agree, so let me explain to you why.
On competitiveness, everybody praises Draghi, Letta and all that, but then Germany and France and others insist on reducing the scope of EU Inc. or dragging their feet on a capital markets union.
On Ukraine, we all stand with Ukraine, whatever it takes and all that. But then France and Luxembourg unashamedly used a veto power to remove Russian oligarchs from the sanctions list.
On the MFF, everyone agrees that Europe is lagging, that we must do much more, spend more and all that. But then many countries, including my own, refuse to budge on the budget.
On defence, yes, of course, Europe's defence and security must be autonomous and all that, as long as each national defence industry benefits most from this effort.
On enlargement and reforms, the need is recognised unanimously, but it's that same unanimity that often blocks and delays these reforms and therefore hurts Europe.
Ladies and gentlemen, it is said that the European Council is where ambition and reforms go to die. It's up to you to change that starting next week.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Gerade diese Tage, wo auch der Europäische Rat stattfindet, sind für Europa entscheidend. Denken wir nur an die Meldung der deutschen Nachrichtendienste, die von einer massiven russischen Bedrohung gesprochen haben. Das heißt, wir müssen unsere europäischen Werte entschlossen verteidigen, und die sind Demokratie, Rechtsstaatlichkeit, Freiheit und Solidarität. Und gerade deshalb müssen wir auch der Ukraine weiter zur Seite stehen und den russischen Angriffskrieg, der sich ja nicht nur gegen die Ukraine richtet, sondern auch gegen die europäische Friedensordnung, endlich verstehen.

Und wir erleben diese russische hybride Kriegsführung – Desinformation, Cyberangriffe, Einflussnahme auf Wahlen in den EU-Mitgliedstaaten und in den Ländern, die auf dem Weg in die Europäische Union sind. Deshalb ist die EU-Erweiterung auch eine Frage unserer Sicherheit. Denn wenn wir Ländern des Westbalkans und anderen Beitrittskandidaten eine klare europäische Perspektive geben, dann stärken wir die Demokratie und die Stabilität. Die Erweiterung ist eine Erfolgsgeschichte, und sie soll es bleiben. Wir wollen ein starkes, demokratisches und solidarisches Europa und eine Erweiterung, die Europa stärker und sicherer macht.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! To prawda, jesteśmy w bardzo ważnym punkcie negocjacji wieloletniego budżetu. Zwiększenie budżetu ponad dotychczasowy poziom i spłata pożyczki NextGenerationEU powoduje, że Unia Europejska szuka nowych źródeł dochodu.

Po pierwsze, jak nie ma pieniędzy, to trzeba ciąć wydatki, a nie tworzyć nowe zasoby własne. Po drugie, nie ma naszej zgody na unijne podatki. Po trzecie, nie ma naszej zgody na przekazywanie kolejnych kompetencji Unii, w tym przypadku kompetencji fiskalnych i ograniczania suwerenności finansowej państw członkowskich. Po czwarte, nie ma zgody na mechanizm warunkowości, czyli pieniądze za praworządność, bo to nic innego jak finansowy szantaż wobec rządów, które nie zgadzają się z obecnym kursem Unii.

Negocjacje budżetu powinny zakończyć się po przyszłorocznych wyborach we Francji czy w Polsce, bo dopiero nowe rządy będą miały właściwy mandat. Trzeba powiedzieć to z całą mocą – ten budżet to kolejny etap federalizacji Unii Europejskiej i na to też nie ma naszej zgody.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, they say that beauty is in the eyes of the beholder, and we will talk about the enlargements this week, and we will have presented the enlargement strategy.

In Bosnia and Herzegovina, we had clear historic elections and, finally, legitimate representation in the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. They're a bit slow on progress, because this position was occupied four times by somebody who was breaking the Dayton Peace Agreement.

So, please, Irish Presidency – you who know power-sharing agreements – you must help Bosnia and Herzegovina. You must help now Darijana Filipović, the Croat member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to put in order a middle way between the two extremes. We must seize this moment to help the country overcome the obstacles that have blocked progress for too long.
Reform of the electoral law remains essential. A roadmap for Bosnia and Herzegovina must include guarantees of legitimate representation and equality for all three constituent peoples.

If the Council recognises enlargement as a strategic and security interest, it must urgently open accession negotiations with Bosnia and Herzegovina. Our message must be clear: turn geopolitical commitments into concrete decisions and give Bosnia and Herzegovina a credible path forward. Don't make a difference, because in history, if you make a difference, it pays dearly.

paragraphs.text: Poštovani predsjedavajući, povjereniče, kolegice i kolege, svjesni smo da nam treba ambiciozniji proračun, pogotovo za konkurentnost, priuštivo stanovanje i razvoj naših regija. No, nije važno samo koliko novca imamo, nego i koliko brzo on dolazi do ljudi.

Novi Europski fond za konkurentnost s predloženih 450 milijardi eura jedinstvena je prilika za snažnija ulaganja u istraživanje, inovacije i kvalitetne projekte diljem naše Unije. No, konkurentnost moramo graditi i u svim državama članicama. Iskustvo Obzora Europa u kojem šest država koristi čak 70 % sredstava upozorava na neravnoteže koje novi fond mora izbjeći.

Kao izvjestiteljica EPP-a za taj fond, Odbor za regionalni razvoj traži geografsku ravnotežu i ravnomjerniji pristup svim sredstvima. Europa može ostvariti svoj puni potencijal samo ako kvalitetni projekti iz svih njezinih regija dobiju priliku.

Kao izvjestiteljica EPP-a za taj fond, Odbor za regionalni razvoj traži geografsku ravnotežu i ravnomjerniji pristup svim sredstvima. Europa može ostvariti svoj puni potencijal samo ako kvalitetni projekti iz svih njezinih regija dobiju priliku.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor ministro Byrne, señor comisario Šefčovič, desde la Declaración de Granada adoptada durante la Presidencia española en noviembre de 2023, la Unión Europea se ha afanado en su ampliación y, descartada Islandia en su propio referéndum, son nueve los estados que están en la lista de espera. El primero de ellos, Montenegro, que, como ya ha señalado la Presidencia irlandesa, ratificará la adhesión inminentemente. Puede pensarse que Montenegro es asimilable: tiene 600 000 habitantes, su producto interior bruto no producirá un gran seísmo. Pero ¿y los ocho que vienen detrás?

La Unión Europea tiene que estar preparada y es el momento de insistir en que no es posible acometer razonablemente esa ampliación en la que la Unión Europea puede pasar de ser veintisiete a treinta y seis sin una reforma institucional de su proceso de toma de decisiones y de su procedimiento legislativo que permita superar de una vez la regla bloqueadora de la unanimidad para que la Unión Europea tenga una voz audible en lugar de ser simplemente más ancha, y que al mismo tiempo no sea más irrelevante y más impotente por su incapacidad de decidir.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, ζητήσατε περισσότερα για άμυνα και ασφάλεια, αντιμετώπιση της παράνομης μετανάστευσης, στήριξη των ηλεκτρικών διασυνδέσεων για ενεργειακή αυτονομία από ευρωπαϊκές πηγές. Συμφωνούμε απόλυτα. Όσα δηλαδή δεν εφαρμόζονται στο κράτος μέλος της Ανατολικής Μεσογείου.

Σιωπή, όμως, και πάλι για την Κύπρο και την Τουρκία. Διερωτώμαι, κυρία Πρόεδρε, αν μία χώρα κατείχε το μισό Βερολίνο, μοίραζε στη μέση τη Γερμανία και είχατε συγγενείς επί πενήντα δύο χρόνια αγνοούμενους, θα είχατε την ίδια στάση; Δεν χρειάζεται να μου απαντήσετε. Ξέρουμε όλοι πολύ καλά την απάντηση. Αυτό φανερώνει την επιλεκτική ευαισθησία και κυρίως την υποκρισία σας.

Κλείνοντας, πρόσφατα άκουσα δήλωση για τα Σκόπια με αναφορές σε γλώσσα και ταυτότητα μακεδονική. Φαντάζομαι εννοείτε τη βουλγαρική γλώσσα και την κλεμμένη ελληνική ταυτότητα και ιστορία. Ντροπή σε εσάς, κυρία Πρόεδρε, και σε όσους σας έχουν στηρίξει να βρίσκεστε σε αυτή τη θέση. Η ιστορία δεν παραχαράσσεται.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση προωθεί σε όλα τα επίπεδα την κλιμάκωση στα δύο μέτωπα του ιμπεριαλιστικού πολέμου, την Ουκρανία και τη Μέση Ανατολή. Η κλιμάκωση, η πολεμική εμπλοκή απέναντι στην καπιταλιστική Ρωσία, οι πλάτες στο κράτος-κατακτητή Ισραήλ δεν συνιστούν κάποιο εξωγενή παράγοντα, αλλά πηγή μεγάλων κινδύνων και ενεργειακής φτώχειας για τον λαό.

Εκατοντάδες δισεκατομμύρια συγκεντρώνονται στην πολεμική βιομηχανία και τα θηριώδη κέρδη των λεγόμενων πράσινων ενεργειακών ομίλων, που απολαμβάνουν προκλητικά ρήτρες διαφυγής και φοροαπαλλαγές: όσα λείπουν, δηλαδή, από μισθούς, συντάξεις, υγεία και παιδεία.

Αδιανόητες στερήσεις, ακρίβεια για τις εργατικές λαϊκές οικογένειες, που προκλητικά εμφανίζουν ως «ανακούφιση». Πενταροδεκάρες, που δεν βγάζουν κανέναν από τη φτώχεια στη βάση των ευρωενωσιακών δημοσιονομικών οροφών και ματωμένων πλεονασμάτων, την κοστολόγηση κυβέρνησης και αστικών κομμάτων.

Οι λαοί δεν θα αποδεχτούν θυσίες για τον πόλεμο και τα κέρδη των καπιταλιστών. Εκατοντάδες χιλιάδες βγαίνουν στον δρόμο σε όλη την Ευρώπη, στην Ελλάδα και ενάντια στην επίσκεψη του γερακιού του πολέμου Ρούμπιο, δυναμώνοντας τον μόνο δρόμο και τη μόνη διέξοδο, τη συνολική ανατροπή.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, I want to address this directly to the Presidency of the Council. You need to be bold and brave together, and the majority of this House is ready to act together with you.

Times of just talking about security and defence have to be over. We must invest. Times of just talking about our independence of energy supply must be over. We must act to get the basis of our independence correct. This means competitiveness and it means affordable energy for all.
We need to see all countries stepping up together. We are very strong, but only when we act together. This is, of course, why we are under attack.

But we need to see much more courage coming out of the Council. Please let us all remember this. We need our own income stream. We need to build up our own income stream and finances. And finally, as my colleague also alluded to: EU Inc. has to come through.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Bardzo ważna październikowa Rada Europejska przed nami. I trzy tematy: po pierwsze – bezpieczeństwo, po drugie – konkurencyjność, a po trzecie – budżet.

Jeśli chodzi o bezpieczeństwo, zrobiliśmy bardzo wiele, krok milowy, trzy programy finansowe, które zostały uruchomione. Dzięki temu jesteśmy bezpieczniejsi. Ale jako kontrsprawozdawca projektu mobilności wojskowej apeluję do Rady o przyspieszenie prac, bo nie mamy czasu. Musimy wprowadzić wojskowe Schengen tu i teraz.

Jeśli chodzi o konkurencyjność, trwa wyścig technologiczny na całym świecie. Kto będzie miał tańszą energię, wygra ten wyścig. Patrzę na Chiny, patrzę na Stany Zjednoczone. I cieszy oczywiście, że produkcja energii z wiatru i słońca daje już więcej niż z innych źródeł. I to bardzo cieszy. Ale musimy więcej inwestować.

I przechodzę do kwestii budżetu. To nie jest czas na cięcia. My musimy przyspieszyć. Jeśli chcemy wygrać ten wyścig, nawet w kontekście energii, musimy przyspieszyć. Dlatego też apeluję, żeby wycofały się te kraje, które jeszcze myślą o tym, żeby w tym nowym budżecie 2028–2034 ciąć budżet. To nie ten czas.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, domnule comisar, intervenția doamnei președinte Ursula von der Leyen a fost plină de contradicții. Vorbim de un nou exercițiu financiar pe șapte ani și spunea domnia sa că rezerva agricolă este goală, dar în același timp renunță la politica agricolă comună, nu mai avem un buget pentru agricultură, nu ține cont de inflație și ne spunea că e același buget. Nu putem avea competitivitate, despre care tot vorbim, dacă nu avem bugete, dacă nu avem predictibilitate, dacă IMM-urile nu se pot dezvolta, dacă reindustrializarea nu are loc. Și atunci despre ce Europă vorbim? Europa fierbe. Nu mai vrem Europa cu două viteze. Nu mai vrem societate polarizată, nu mai vrem cetățeni săraci. Pentru aceasta ne trebuie, domnule comisar, să acționăm urgent. Există mai departe evaziune? De ce nu impozităm marile companii cu profituri absolut astronomice ca să putem să avem buget pentru a crește la fermieri subvenția, pentru a crește fondurile pentru coeziune, pentru că de coeziune vorbim de când este Uniunea Europeană și totuși nu avem coeziune.

interventions.speaker_label: Maroš Šefčovič, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Minister, honourable Members of the European Parliament, I would like to thank you for all your interventions, many of which would definitely contribute to the final preparation of the next European Council. You highlighted the importance of enlargement, of housing problem across Europe, of the close link between energy and competitiveness and, of course, the perspective for a conclusion of the multiannual financial framework.
As you know, according to the new rules, I was only given two minutes, so let me focus just on on two points.

We all agree on a close link between housing, energy prices, energy supplies and competitiveness of European Union. As you know, there are different proposals on the table, but also many of them in the making. Some of them will be discussed even today in different plenary debates, some of them in the course of this week. Therefore, I just would like to underscore once again that the multiannual financial framework is the absolute top priority, I believe, for all of us. I know how difficult these negotiations always are, but we should not lose the big picture here – because we are talking about 1.26 % of European GNI and which, on top of it, is always bringing much higher added value compared to the similar investments, if they are made only on the national level.

I also would like to highlight that we know how much the Irish Presidency is focused on this priority, and we all know that we have to do our utmost to make sure that we would start the new budgetary period with a budget which fits to the 21st century and which responds to the huge challenges of today.

Tá mé fíorbhuíoch díobh go léir as gach atá ráite sa díospóireacht seo inniu agaibh. Cuirfidh mé gach rud in iúl d'Uachtarán na Comhairle Eorpaí. paragraphs.text: Dear colleagues, with us today is the Prime Minister of Portugal, Luís Montenegro, as part of our 'This is Europe' series of debates. Prime Minister, dear Luís, welcome to the European Parliament. Thank you for being here.

Let me begin by expressing our solidarity with everyone affected by the natural disasters in Portugal, and paying tribute to the bravery and commitment of all emergency workers. This summer, even while facing wildfires at home, Portuguese firefighters crossed the border to walk into fires in neighbouring Member States. They represent the very best of Europe and we thank them.
(Applause)

Dear Prime Minister, this year we celebrate 40 years of Portugal in the European Union – four decades of Portuguese leadership, of Portugal shaping our Union and of our Union shaping Portugal. This Parliament shares your ambition for a more competitive Europe, with less bureaucracy and more room for companies to grow, scale and create jobs. We also share your determination to improve energy connections between Member States – and I know your work on the Iberian Peninsula reflects that. Your energy security is part of international stability, and we welcome your focus on both as Portugal prepares to take its seat on the United Nations Security Council.

Of course, delivering on this agenda means securing a budget that can support it. And that is why reaching an agreement on the next multiannual financial framework is so urgent. Parliament and Portugal share a lot of common ground and, Prime Minister, we know we can rely on you to play a constructive role in the negotiations ahead.

It is fitting that the Treaty that guides our Union bears the name of your capital. Portugal may sit on the western edge of our continent, but its place is at the very heart of our common project. And as we take the next steps on our common European journey, we will need to find our own Portuguese perseverance and persistence. This is how we keep building Europe: step by step; brick by brick; vote by vote.
And here I will quote you when you say:
«Água mole em pedra dura tanto bate até que fura».
So without further ado, dear Prime Minister, dear Luís, the floor is yours.
