political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, muito obrigado a todos os senhores deputados intervenientes. É com muito gosto que partilho aqui alguns pontos de vista sobre as questões que suscitaram. Com o mesmo gosto com que estarei na próxima sexta‑feira na Assembleia da República, no Parlamento português, a responder aos deputados portugueses sobre a concreta realidade da vida do país, como é minha obrigação.

Deixar‑vos quatro reflexões finais. A primeira sobre o quadro financeiro plurianual, as questões da coesão, as questões da política agrícola comum, as questões da competitividade. Para reiterar que a nossa perspetiva não é de estar aqui a pedir nada. A nossa perspetiva é de construir uma Europa onde os cidadãos, as organizações e as empresas tenham as mesmas oportunidades, partilhem um mercado que é comum e um mercado que é comum que valoriza os consumidores daqueles que têm maior capacidade produtiva. A solidariedade hoje, a coesão, hoje são um sinónimo de valorização do mercado interno, de valorização das economias mais fortes também. E mais, a coesão territorial é essencial à promoção da estabilização climática e da luta contra as alterações climáticas. Porque se nós não tivermos a ousadia e o espírito solidário de ajudar aqueles que estão nas regiões menos desenvolvidas, essas regiões vão ficar cada vez mais desertificadas e, portanto, os seus territórios expostos àqueles que são os fenómenos climáticos mais extremos que depois exigem uma resposta de todos nós.

A política de financiamento comunitário é essencial. Àqueles que aqui manifestaram dúvidas sobre a União da Poupança e dos Investimentos ou a União Bancária, eu deixo esta questão: querem uma Europa que continua a alocar grande parte dos seus recursos para financiar aqueles que são, do ponto de vista comercial, os nossos principais concorrentes? Querem uma Europa que continue a depositar, por exemplo, nos mercados de capitais americanos, a sua capacidade financeira, que podia estar disponível para a nossa economia, para as nossas empresas e, por via disso, também para a melhoria das condições de vida dos nossos concidadãos?

Porque financiar as empresas é estimular a inovação, é estimular a produtividade e é estimular o pagamento de melhores salários. É, portanto, dar condições de vida concretas a cada um dos cidadãos. É a primeira reflexão que vos deixo, reiterando aquilo que aqui disse sobre a importância geopolítica não apenas de solidariedade, o que já não era pouco, mas a importância geopolítica do apoio às regiões ultraperiféricas.

A segunda questão, a questão da habitação. Qual é a minha perspetiva? A minha perspetiva é que a Europa pode dar um contributo no respeito por aquelas que são as responsabilidades dos Estados‑Membros, mas pode dar um contributo através de legislação menos complexa, de simplificação e através, também aí, do aumento da capacidade de financiamento. Aproveitar toda a capacidade no perímetro das instituições europeias, talvez de uma forma mais preponderante do Banco Europeu de Investimento, para podermos ter a capacidade de aumentar a oferta.

Àqueles que aqui vêm com lágrimas de crocodilo, falar sobre as consequências sociais da falta de acesso à habitação, eu digo: sem oferta, o preço sobe; quando o preço sobe, o acesso é mais limitado. E aqueles que têm dúvidas disso já experimentaram. Vejam, por exemplo, aquilo que aconteceu numa cidade grande espanhola, em Barcelona, quando se quis conter e limitar o funcionamento do mercado. Mais imediatamente houve algum acréscimo de possibilidade de arrendar, mas quando o mercado respondeu à limitação do seu funcionamento, o número de casas diminuiu e as rendas aumentaram cerca de 80 %. Foi essa a consequência.

Portanto, valorizar a oferta, a oferta pública e a oferta privada. Eu dou o exemplo português. Quando cheguei ao governo, o governo que me antecedeu do Partido Socialista queria construir 26 000 casas. Só deixou dinheiro para 16 000 no perímetro público. Nós aumentámos o objetivo para 59 e neste momento estamos a financiar com o Banco Europeu de Investimento mais 133 000 novas casas reabilitadas ou construídas de novo, para que aqueles que têm mais vulnerabilidade possam ter acesso.

Mas isso não chega. A oferta pública tem de se conciliar com a oferta privada. Por isso, estamos a diminuir os impostos, para que haja mais construção e, por isso, estamos também a estimular, do lado da procura, o acesso à habitação mesmo nos sítios onde há mais pressão e as rendas são mais caras. Sim, em Lisboa há muita gente que paga 2 000 EUR de renda. E estamos a falar de quem? Estamos a falar de médicos, estamos a falar de professores, estamos a falar de polícias. Há menos médicos, professores e polícias em Lisboa porque os preços da habitação são mais altos. E é preciso também, do lado da procura, intervir para garantir que, através da fixação desses profissionais, todos os cidadãos, nomeadamente aqueles que têm mais vulnerabilidade e mais dificuldade, possam ter uma resposta. Porque para haver uma resposta num centro de saúde, num hospital, numa esquadra de polícia, para haver uma resposta numa escola, garantindo uma igualdade de oportunidades a todos, é preciso que os profissionais lá estejam, mesmo nas zonas mais densas do ponto de vista populacional.

Terceira linha, imigração. Sim, imigração. Nós temos a responsabilidade de ser, além do mais, uma fronteira externa da União Europeia. A imigração que nós defendemos é uma imigração regulada e humanista. Vale a pena vir para a Europa trabalhar se se vier por bem, se se vier pelos canais próprios. Vale a pena, já agora, vale a pena contestar e combater as redes ilegais de tráfico de seres humanos. Mas isso só se faz conduzindo as pessoas para o cumprimento das regras, das regras para virem com a garantia de trabalho, das regras para virem com a garantia de ter uma habitação condigna e o acesso a cuidados de saúde. E já agora também para garantir os cuidados de educação aos agregados familiares.

Aquilo que foi muitos anos esquecido, mas que hoje está em funcionamento em Portugal, e que naturalmente pressupõe que aqueles que não cumprem as regras devem retornar aos seus países de origem. A Lei do retorno que o Pacto das Migrações da União Europeia prevê, e que nós estamos a implementar em Portugal, é a garantia de que quem vem por bem, cumpre as regras, fica. Se não vem por bem, não cumpre as regras, vai para o seu local de origem. Só o cumprimento das regras, também do retorno, pode conduzir as pessoas a virem dentro daquilo que é o estabelecido por todos nós.

Uma última palavra sobre os jovens, sobre o futuro, sobre aquilo que nós temos de fazer para fixar na Europa o nosso capital humano. Nenhuma sociedade pode ser desenvolvida, a Europa não pode combater a força dos outros blocos comerciais dos Estados Unidos, da América, da China, dos países emergentes, das economias que têm mais potencial hoje, não pode fazê‑lo se insistir na complexidade das regras. Com certeza, a simplificação é um caminho de melhorar a competitividade, mas eu quero aqui dizer, alto e bom som: se não tivermos a capacidade de ter entre nós os nossos melhores, o nosso talento, os nossos jovens qualificados, e se não tivermos até a capacidade de atrair alguns que venham dos outros blocos comerciais, nós não podemos dar‑nos ao luxo de exportar o nosso talento para que os outros sejam mais competitivos do que nós. Nós temos de apostar na inovação e temos de apostar na valorização dos nossos recursos humanos.

Por isso, em Portugal, hoje paga‑se menos impostos sobre o rendimento do trabalho. Por isso, em Portugal, hoje nós estimulamos a economia baixando os impostos sobre as empresas para que elas possam inovar mais e para que elas possam pagar mais salários. Por isso, para os jovens, em particular até aos 35 anos, nós temos um regime fiscal que lhes dá o acesso a 100 % de desconto dos impostos sobre o rendimento do trabalho no primeiro ano de trabalho, a 75 % no segundo, no terceiro e no quarto, a 50 % de desconto, no quinto, no sexto e no sétimo ano, a 25 % de desconto dos impostos sobre o rendimento do trabalho no oitavo, no nono e no décimo ano de vida ativa. Mas, ao mesmo tempo, damos isenção de impostos para a compra da primeira habitação e damos uma garantia pública para que possam comprar uma casa com 100 % do financiamento, para que os bancos possam emprestar‑lhes aquilo que é necessário.

Também para isso a União Bancária como estímulo à igualdade de oportunidades, a uma sã concorrência, é fundamental. E é por isso, Senhores Deputados, termino, que em 2025, o ano passado, já fizemos regressar 69 000 imigrantes que estão hoje a reforçar os nossos quadros na nossa economia, nas nossas empresas, nas nossas instituições. Assim, a Europa possa seguir também esta linha. Garanto‑vos, se a Europa conseguir seguir esta linha, acho que nós podemos multiplicar os exemplos como aqueles que aqui trouxe, modéstia à parte, são mérito da sociedade portuguesa, das portuguesas e dos portugueses, das instituições portuguesas.

Uma economia que cresce mais, uma economia que gera riqueza, que garante que o Estado Social funciona, uma economia que chega ao final do ano com contas públicas equilibradas e vamos para o quarto superavit consecutivo das nossas contas públicas, não aumentando um único imposto nem pondo na gaveta os investimentos públicos que são necessários à qualidade de vida das pessoas. A nossa dívida vai acabar este ano abaixo dos 90 % do nosso produto e, felizmente, no próximo ano a trajetória vai continuar assim. É com esta resistência e resiliência que nós nos apresentamos para a Europa disponíveis para podermos ter a garantia de termos um espaço que valoriza a paz, que valoriza os direitos das pessoas, que garante a resposta social, que garante a prosperidade. Não há nenhuma sociedade que possa combater a pobreza que aqui muitos quiseram evidenciar se não criar riqueza. O caminho que nós defendemos é criar riqueza para combater a pobreza.

paragraphs.text: Before we move to the votes, which will be presided over by Vice-President Zīle, I would like for you to give me a moment to address an incident that occurred in the European Parliament yesterday evening.

A Member of this House was filmed apparently damaging an exhibition commemorating the victims of the terrorist attack in Israel on 7 October. The person concerned was seen allegedly throwing the flag of Israel to the ground, dropped a flagpole and the European Union flag was knocked down. Both flags were left lying on the ground before the Member left the scene.
I would like to underline that we take this extremely seriously and that all appropriate steps, according to our procedures, are being taken, including the right of the person concerned to be heard.

But I also want to make a wider point today. This House is a place where all of us must feel safe and secure, and we reject, in the strongest possible terms, any action by any person that makes anyone feel less protected here. We cannot have actions like this.

We cannot have actions that could make people fearful of speaking. We cannot have damage to property, and we cannot have attempts to intimidate rather than to debate. So at a time of rising global antisemitism, we owe it to Europe's Jewish community to ensure that when they look to us, they see that this is their House too.
Tomorrow we will mark another anniversary since that black 7 October three years ago. On your behalf, I will speak at the event and we will remember the victims with the dignity that they deserve.
I know some colleagues have asked to take the floor on this point. I ask you to make it very short and very quick so that we go to the vote.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, demain marquera le troisième anniversaire des attentats du 7-Octobre. 1 180 victimes, dont plusieurs dizaines de citoyens européens, et le peuple israélien tout entier, comme le peuple palestinien, entraîné dans l'horreur par les islamistes du Hamas.

Hier, à l'occasion d'un événement organisé par notre collègue Hildegarde Bentele, Rima Hassan – vous l'avez rappelé – s'en est prise au drapeau israélien et au drapeau européen qu'elle a jetés par terre. Et à une personne qui l'interpellait, elle a répondu simplement «Israël n'existe pas». Personne ici ne nie le droit à la sécurité et à la dignité pour le peuple palestinien. Mais il y a une force politique qui a décidé de nier ces droits pour le peuple israélien.

Madame Hassan, nous ne vous laisserons pas faire. Ni vous, ni vos amis. Nous ne vous laisserons pas entraîner l'Europe dans la spirale d'antisémitisme, de haine et de violence où vous cherchez à la pousser.
(Applaudissements)

L'article 10 de notre règlement, Madame la Présidente, impose que chaque élu s'engage à respecter la dignité liée à son mandat. L'histoire de l'Europe a commencé par dire que la dignité, c'est d'abord le respect dû aux morts. Et demain, en commémorant les attentats du 7-Octobre, nous nous engagerons à redire ensemble: «Plus jamais ça, plus jamais ça!».

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, je me réfère à l'article 10, encore, à la lutte contre l'antisémitisme, encore. Hier, dans cet hémicycle, Manon Aubry osait me donner des leçons de lutte contre l'antisémitisme. Hier, le même jour, un membre de son parti, Rima Hassan, mettait à bas un drapeau israélien et, en même temps, un drapeau européen. Alors, les leçons d'antisémitisme de LFI, c'est de l'antisémitisme qu'il pratique.

Hier, dans cet hémicycle, je rappelais que le Rassemblement national est issu d'un parti créé par d'anciens Waffen-SS, a été présidé par Jean-Marie Le Pen, qui a été condamné pour antisémitisme. Me dire que la veille du 7-Octobre, il y a dans ce Parlement deux groupes politiques où l'antisémitisme a servi de colonne vertébrale, c'est insupportable. C'est insupportable pour notre construction européenne qui est née des cendres de la Deuxième Guerre mondiale, qui est née des cendres de la Shoah. Et nous avions dit: «Plus jamais ça!».

Alors, en mémoire des victimes de la Shoah, en mémoire des victimes du 7-Octobre que nous commémorerons demain, je demande à tous les groupes politiques de retrouver de la décence, de se souvenir des valeurs fondamentales de l'Union européenne et de lutter vraiment sérieusement contre l'antisémitisme.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, je vais rappeler de façon très calme et apaisée les faits, parce que vous avez vous-même repris des éléments qui sont factuellement faux.

Ce qui s'est déroulé hier, c'est que j'ai assisté à une exposition, un événement qui est tout d'abord organisé en partenariat avec l'ambassade d'Israël – c'est un élément très important à rappeler. Dans le cadre de ce partenariat avec l'ambassade d'Israël, qui est le porte-parole finalement de l'État israélien, il y a une exposition du drapeau israélien. Personne ici n'accepterait que le drapeau russe soit exposé et il est tout à fait normal de s'y opposer, précisément au regard des crimes qui sont commis par la Russie.

Israël, que vous le vouliez ou non, commet aujourd'hui un génocide, un crime d'apartheid qui est un crime contre l'humanité. Et on peut parfaitement, comme nous l'avons fait avec notre groupe, commémorer les victimes du 7-Octobre sans s'associer à l'État israélien génocidaire.

Je veux également préciser, Madame la Présidente – non, c'est un élément très important –, à l'occasion de cet événement, est également vendue une carte d'Israël, du Grand Israël. Et quand nous avons posé la question aux organisateurs, ils nous ont répondu que le peuple palestinien n'existait pas, que la Palestine n'existait pas. Est-ce que ces propos sont conformes à la politique que vous défendez ici au sein des institutions européennes? Je ne crois pas.
Donc, je veux rappeler un dernier élément, Madame la Présidente, je n'ai pas touché au drapeau européen. Il est simplement tombé après que le drapeau israélien a été…

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, io sarò molto sintetica. Però voglio dire che, a differenza di quello che oggi ha detto la collega, abbiamo assistito a una gravissima, gravissima aggressione alle istituzioni. La signora è già rinviata a giudizio per apologia del terrorismo e anche ieri ha appoggiato il terrorismo di Hamas. Inaccettabile, gravissimo! Sanzioni severe.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, ho sentito le parole della collega Hassan e sono ancora più indignato, perché voler separare le vittime del 7 ottobre dalla loro nazionalità lo trovo ancora più vergognoso e criminale. Quegli uomini e quelle donne erano uomini e donne di Israele e sono stati uccisi sul territorio israeliano.

Mentre vandalizzava la mostra, la collega Hassan urlava frasi senza senso, del tipo che quella mostra sarebbe stata "a senso unico". Evidentemente, secondo la collega, bisognava rappresentare anche il pensiero di coloro che hanno tagliato la gola ad anziani, a ragazze che ballavano, a bambini di pochi mesi. In questo modo, sarebbero stati giustamente rappresentati entrambi i punti di vista.
Io credo che la deriva islamista della sinistra sia ormai evidente e sia un evidente problema in tutta Europa. E noi la contrasteremo, questo è sicuro.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, I am very pleased that, just before the summer break, we reached a political agreement on the programme for agile and rapid defence innovation. Today, we need to adopt it in the plenary.

AGILE is an important pilot programme because it puts Europe's SMEs, start‑ups and scale‑ups at the heart of defence innovation. The agreement maintains the EUR 115‑million budget, SME focus and four‑month time‑to‑grant objectives, while aligning with Member States' capability needs.

The European Parliament has shown again that it can respond quickly and take responsibility to reduce strategic dependencies and strengthen the resilience of our defence, technological and industrial base. I also call on the Commission to present a single market for defence and communication. The defence procurement framework should be modernised too.
Finally, let me thank co‑rapporteur Mr Ijabs, the shadow rapporteurs, our assistants and advisers for the exemplary cooperation on this important file.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, every day of the ongoing Russian aggression in Ukraine shows the urgency of boosting our own defence industries, especially regarding the innovation and new technologies. That is why the adoption of the agile programme is so timely and necessary. Now let me just mention a few things where we were succeeding in reaching an agreement with the Council on this file.

First of all, support for SMEs and start-ups. This is where defence innovation often happens. We want to keep them in Europe and to make Europe attractive to innovators. Second, we have to work productively with Ukrainians to involve them in our defence industrial ecosystem. Third is agility, as the name suggests.

The programme starts already early next year, and I strongly encourage you, dear colleagues, to distribute the information about it among the innovators and SMEs in your Member States to make it truly effective, truly competitive and above all, truly European in its scope. I would like to thank my co-rapporteur, Tonino Picula, and the shadow rapporteurs, for this successful and really intense collaboration. Also, my thanks goes to all advisers and assistants involved in the process.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear colleagues, it is time that the EU becomes a project of hope again. We all need it in these very turbulent times.

Colleagues, preventing people from getting cancer means providing hope. Every year, around 120 000 workers in Europe are diagnosed with work-related cancer. These are people who simply went to work and became seriously ill by it.

I am proud to say that we reached an ambitious but balanced agreement here. We strengthened the protection against dangerous substances on the work floor, but protection also needs to work in practice.

I visited a cobalt refinery in Finland, and I spoke with workers, with trade unions and with employers. I saw that protection and a competitive European industry can go hand in hand. I have seen that social dialogue is so important. It leads to workable solutions on the ground and that matters.
We need our own European critical raw materials, such as cobalt, for our industry, but also for our clean transition. We want to protect the jobs for the people working in those industries.

So the message today is very clear: we do not have to choose between protecting the workers or protecting our industry. We can do both. And with this agreement, we prevent cancer and other serious diseases while giving companies the time, the clarity and the support that they need. Because no one should become seriously ill just by going to work. And that is why I ask you all to support this agreement.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Wir erleben ja gerade sehr anschaulich, dass Fragen der wirtschaftspolitischen Steuerung auf der Tagesordnung stehen. Die Anleihemärkte senden ein klares Signal bei den Staatsanleihen. Bei den Staatsfinanzen in Europa läuft nicht alles rund. Die Kosten für neue Schulden sind so hoch wie lange nicht mehr. In solchen Zeiten braucht Europa klare Regeln, die glaubwürdig, die verlässlich, aber die auch einfach anzuwenden sind.

Genau das ist das, was wir miteinander vereinbart haben – Rat und Parlament –, über was wir heute abstimmen. Unnötige Berichtspflichten werden gestrichen, Verfahren werden gestrafft, der Rahmen wird kohärent. Den fiskalischen Kern lassen wir dabei unberührt. Das heißt, die Sicherheit unserer Währung ist nicht gefährdet. Aber Regeln, und das sage ich auch ganz deutlich, sind nur so gut wie ihre Durchsetzung. Deswegen, sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar, geht es auch darum, dass die Regeln angewandt werden. Das ist Ihre Verantwortung. Bitte liefern Sie.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, começo, naturalmente, por agradecer ao colega Markus Ferber correlator, bem como às equipas técnicas, toda a colaboração neste dossiê. Gostaria de dizer também que este acordo para a simplificação das regras de governação económica mostra que simplificar não significa desregular.

Reduzimos o reporting excessivo, flexibilizámos prazos para os governos entregarem os seus orçamentos e reduzimos as multas, mas não só. Este pacote de simplificação preserva ainda o papel do Parlamento, reforça a dimensão social e dá condições mais favoráveis a investimentos nas áreas do social, clima digital e defesa; e estas são prioridades críticas de investimento para enfrentarmos os desafios de uma Europa mais competitiva, mais justa e mais forte.

A reforma das regras de governação económica é, sem dúvida, um passo na direção certa, mas não resolve tudo. Caras e caros colegas, a Europa tem de se comprometer em ter recursos próprios para financiarmos o futuro orçamento da União à altura dos desafios que enfrentamos e não passarmos meses à volta de décimas e de 1 % do rendimento nacional. A Europa tem de estar à altura da sua própria ambição.

paragraphs.text: - Pirms balsošanas:

interventions.text: - Pirms balsošanas:

paragraphs.text: Mr President, colleagues, we are addicted to fossil fuels. Almost 70 % of Europe's energy is still fossil. If we're going to get rid of that dependency, we need to change. The clothes we're wearing, our transport, the food we eat, the processes that industry is using, what we consume – we have fossil fuels everywhere, and we need a broad transition within our industry.

In order to do so, our industry needs reliable information and faster permits. To do the right thing should be easy. It shouldn't take nine years to get a permit to build a windmill. One individual woodpecker should not be allowed to block a whole decarbonisation of the steel industry, and you should not need a team of experts to understand environment data.

The green transition should have taken place preferably yesterday, and not after decades of waiting for paperwork. One of the first steps we are taking today – this law makes environment data available, accessible and comparable across Europe without unnecessary regulatory burden, without double regulation. This is simplification when simplification is at its best.

Mr President, colleagues, we are addicted to fossil fuels. Almost 70 % of Europe's energy is still fossil. If we're going to get rid of that dependency, we need to change. The clothes we're wearing, our transport, the food we eat, the processes that industry is using, what we consume – we have fossil fuels everywhere, and we need a broad transition within our industry.

In order to do so, our industry needs reliable information and faster permits. To do the right thing should be easy. It shouldn't take nine years to get a permit to build a windmill. One individual woodpecker should not be allowed to block a whole decarbonisation of the steel industry, and you should not need a team of experts to understand environment data.

The green transition should have taken place preferably yesterday, and not after decades of waiting for paperwork. One of the first steps we are taking today – this law makes environment data available, accessible and comparable across Europe without unnecessary regulatory burden, without double regulation. This is simplification when simplification is at its best.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Úr! Az európai vállalkozások azt várják tőlünk, hogy végre lélegezni tudjanak. A túlszabályozás elkerülését, kevesebb adminisztrációs terhet és nagyobb védelmet a tisztességtelen versennyel szemben.

Az adózás terén különösen igazak ezek az elvárások. Ezért az európai adópolitikának egyszerre kell biztosítani a fair adóztatást és Európa versenyképességét. Nem kell választanunk a kettő közül, mindkettőre szükségünk van. A globális minimumadó nagyban hozzájárult ahhoz, hogy ne érje meg pusztán adózási előnyök miatt mozgatni a tevékenységeket és a profitot.

Most itt az ideje, hogy elvégezzük a saját házi feladatunkat. Szüntessük meg az egymást átfedő adójogszabályokat, és célzott, jogszerű adókedvezményekkel tartsuk Európában az innovatív vállalkozásokat. Ez a Bizottság adózási könnyítési csomagja jó irányba tett lépés, de a hatálybaléptetési sebességet gyorsítani kell.

Ahhoz pedig, hogy választ tudjunk adni az olyan égető kihívásokra, mint a digitális szolgáltatások adózása, összehangoltabb és erőteljesebb európai érdekérvényesítése van szükség a nemzetközi fórumokon. Képviselőtársaim! A cél világos: kevesebb, de jobb szabály, tisztességesebb adózás és versenyképesebb Európa. Kérem Önöket, hogy támogassák a jelentést.

interventions.speaker_label: Thomas Byrne, President-in-Office of the Council.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, Commissioner, the housing crisis has become one of the most pressing social and economic challenges facing citizens across Europe.

In October 2025, the European Council recognised the scale and urgency of the challenge, and called on the Commission to swiftly present an ambitious and comprehensive plan for affordable housing. This was an important political signal that housing is no longer confined to being a national issue, but rather it has become a matter of common European concern.

Access to adequate and affordable housing is impacting the lives of our citizens, particularly the young and the vulnerable, and their full participation in society and in our economy. When housing becomes unaffordable, people's ability to find work, to move for employment, to start a family and to access education is affected, as is their capacity to stay in the communities where they have established their lives.

Our Presidency will have an informal meeting of housing ministers this year. We know that there is a housing crisis across Europe, and if we do not address this crisis, it weakens social cohesion, it threatens competitiveness, it weakens labour and social mobility. Ireland's Presidency is determined to do everything we can to work with our EU partners to make a positive contribution on housing.

Indeed, the Council conclusions of June rightly underlined the links between housing and demographics, including ageing, smaller households and urbanisation. Across Europe, the challenge is not just a shortage of homes; it is a shortage of affordable, suitable and accessible homes in the places where people need them. Rising housing costs are having a particularly negative impact on young people, families, low and middle-income households, and essential workers. The conclusions that I mentioned explicitly identify these groups among those disproportionately affected.

Housing affordability is also increasingly impacting EU competitiveness. Businesses need to be able to attract and retain workers. Regions need to be able to attract investment. Young people need to be able to access employment and education without being priced out of the places where the opportunities exist. If housing costs prevent workers from moving where jobs are available, this can restrict labour mobility and exacerbate regional inequalities. So addressing housing affordability is not just about addressing cost; it is also an investment in Europe's economic and social resilience.

It's with that mindset that the Irish Presidency is setting about its work on the new proposal for a regulation establishing a framework for measures in Member States to safeguard housing affordability and availability, published by the Commission on 9 September. The proposal aims to support public authorities in identifying areas of housing stress and to take measures to protect housing affordability in those areas, including in relation to short-term rentals.

The Council has very recently started discussing the proposal at a technical level and a thorough examination of the proposal will continue in the coming months. We look forward to following this debate today in Parliament on the Commission proposal so that when the time comes to start interinstitutional negotiations, we can arrive at a result that meets the expectations of European citizens on such a pressing matter.

interventions.speaker_label: Dan Jørgensen, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, dear friends, what makes a city a city? Is it the buildings? Is it the architecture? Is it the landmarks? No, it is the citizens. There is no Paris without Parisians. There is no Rome without Romans. A city is defined by its citizens, and a city needs its citizens. The sanitation workers who clean our streets. The bus drivers who take us from A to B. The students and young people who bring new life to old neighbourhoods. But today, too many of these people are being pushed out of their communities because homes are not affordable to buy, because housing is not affordable to rent. And let me be clear: short-term rentals, second homes and vacant properties are not the root cause of these problems, but in some parts of Europe, including in some of our biggest cities, they do contribute to this problem. They are a part of the challenge.

Since I took office, this issue has been raised time and time again by many of you here in Parliament. It has also been raised by mayors and ministers from cities, regions and countries across Europe. They have told me that they want to take action, but that they lack the legal certainty and that they fear litigation.

With the Affordable Housing Act, we aim to replace this fear with freedom. We provide legal certainty. We set out common criteria to identify areas under housing stress. We give cities, Member States and regions the opportunities to take the action that they need, which are adequate and proportionate. Brussels will not decide which areas should be targeted or which measures should be introduced. Those decisions will remain local, regional and up to the national authorities. With the support of this act, they can make their decisions with greater confidence and with the best interests of their people in mind.

As I said, short-term rentals, second homes and vacant properties are not the sole cause of Europe's housing crisis, but in some places they are a part of the problem. In the same way, this act is not the whole solution, but it is a part of the solution. Together, we must keep working to boost investments and supply, to address speculation and support the most vulnerable, and to cut red tape.

In the meantime, with this act, we can already support the areas that are suffering the most. We can already make the best use of existing buildings, and we can already make a real difference, in real time, to ensure that housing is used first and foremost for the people to live in, and to ensure that cities belong first and foremost to their citizens.

paragraphs.text: Poštovani predsjedavajući, kolegice i kolege, poštovani povjereniče, u Europskoj uniji nam nedostaje 10 milijuna stambenih jedinica. I zato sam u ad acta o priuštivom stanovanju očekivala puno više. U planu za priuštivo stanovanje 2025. upravo Vi ste najavili ograničavanje kratkoročnog najma i promicanje priuštivosti u područjima pod stambenim pritiskom, upravo kroz pojednostavnjenje administrativnih postupaka kao što su planiranje i izdavanje dozvola.
Nažalost, za brže izdavanje dozvola, više gradnje, za obnovu, prenamjenu postojećih zgrada i mobilizaciju investicija dobili smo neobvezujuću preporuku. Ali još je veće razočarenje uredba.

Prvo, tražili smo da se za ograničavanje kratkoročnog najma uvaži činjenica da je za mnoge naše građane takvo iznajmljivanje važan izvor prihoda i naglasili smo da takve mjere ne smiju odvratiti turizam. Ali daleko najveći problem je da uredba uvodi mogućnost ograničavanja korištenja ili kupnje druge nekretnine. Takva mjera nije bila niti tražena, niti najavljena, niti će biti prihvaćena. Jednostavno ne dolazi u obzir da se kažnjavaju građani koji svoju ušteđevinu su uložili u kupnju druge nekretnine.

Ako je ideja uredbe bila ograničiti špekulacije, onda je to trebalo jasno tako i propisati. U teoriji Akt o priuštivom stanovanju omogućava donošenje mjera koje moraju biti nužne i proporcionalne, a u praksi šta to znači, da ako donesene mjere ne budu takve, na građanima je obveza da sudski dokazuju da smiju raspolagati svojom vlastitom nekretninom. E pa povjereniče, Europska povelja o temeljnim pravima garantira svim našim građanima pravo na vlasništvo nad zakonito stečenom imovinom.

Nažalost, Akt o prištivom stanovanju dovodi u pitanje to temeljno pravo. interventions.speaker_label: Irene Tinagli, on behalf of the S&D Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the S&D Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues, when the Socialists and Democrats first called for action on housing, many, including in this House, did not see it as a significant problem. They said it was not even a European problem. But I think that today nobody would dare to say so because everybody can see it's an emergency, everybody can see it's affecting millions of European citizens, and most importantly, we see that these citizens are asking for concrete answers. That's what we need to deliver.

Of course, European institutions cannot replace Member States. We don't want to replace Member States. We can't. But they can provide tools and actions. That's what the Affordable Housing Act is about. It's a key step in this direction. It does not impose anything on anyone. It respects subsidiarity and autonomy of the cities and regions, but gives mayors possibilities, tools to act. But above all, it affirms a crucial principle: access to housing is like healthcare and education, a common good that is essential in keeping our society and cities functioning, and therefore it must be protected.

paragraphs.text: Pane předsedající, pane komisaři, kolegyně, kolegové, za pár dní nás v České republice čekají komunální volby a lidé se mě logicky ptají: „Paní poslankyně, bydlení je drahé. Je to asi jeden z nejpalčivějších problémů. Bytů je málo. Co pro nás může udělat Evropská unie?“ Ale upřímně, po přečtení návrhu opravdu nevím, co jim odpovědět. Asi to, že pokud obec prokáže, že se nachází v oblasti pod tlakem na bydlení, splní stanovené podmínky a příslušná opatření projdou evropským rámcem proporcionality, pak bude mít větší prostor přijmout některá opatření na místním trhu s bydlením. No tak to se lidem určitě uleví. Jen se obávám, že mladá rodina, která si nemůže dovolit byt, by čekala trochu jinou odpověď. Například, že se postaráme o to, aby se stavělo více bytů, že zjednodušíme evropské fondy, uvolníme pravidla veřejné podpory, přivedeme soukromé investice, zrychlíme výstavbu a podíváme se na evropskou legislativu, která ji prodražuje. Akt o dostupném bydlení nesmí být další případem, kdy na velmi jednoduchou otázku občana odpovíme velmi složitým evropským mechanismem. Lidé se ptají prostě, kde budou bydlet. Neměli bychom jim odpovídat definicí „oblast s napětím na trhu bydlení“. A to ani nemluvě o tom, jak obrovskou administrativní zátěž tím klademe na bedra měst a obcí. Bydlení není potřeba regulovat, pane komisaři, ale podpořit.

interventions.speaker_label: Antonella Sberna, a nome del gruppo ECR.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, la Commissione ha avuto il merito di portare la casa al centro dell'agenda europea. Ha però scelto lo strumento sbagliato. In Europa mancano alloggi e il regolamento risponde limitando l'uso di quelli che ci sono.

Signor Commissario, il vostro testo ammette che le restrizioni non risolvono la carenza di alloggi. Eppure, è l'unica materia su cui il regolamento detta regole vincolanti. Per decidere dove applicarle usa lo stesso indice in tutta Europa, senza distinguere tra una grande città, un centro storico o un'area rurale. Nei nostri borghi si finirebbe per colpire proprio le case che i fondi europei hanno aiutato a recuperare. Così l'Europa scarica le crisi sui sindaci e se ne lava le mani. La casa è competenza degli Stati membri e l'Europa può fare molto per aiutarli.

Proponiamo di rovesciarla questa impostazione. Una ricetta che funziona esiste e, ad esempio, è quella italiana. Il governo guidato da Giorgia Meloni ha messo al centro una cosa semplice: recuperare le case e costruire. Rimette in uso 60 000 alloggi popolari inagibili, investe fino a 10 miliardi per 100 000 alloggi in dieci anni. A chi costruisce offre procedure semplici, con prezzi calmierati, prevede garanzie sui mutui anche per i giovani e governa gli affitti brevi con un codice nazionale e controlli digitali senza divieti. È la ricetta da seguire, perché aumenta l'offerta e dà fiducia a chi investe.

Il nuovo regolamento metta al centro le misure che fanno crescere l'offerta, oggi confinate in una raccomandazione. La priorità sia rimettere in uso le case vuote, a partire da quelle pubbliche, renda operativa la garanzia europea per i giovani oggi allo studio della BEI e conceda più flessibilità di bilancio per gli investimenti in edilizia agevolata. Su questa strada il Parlamento è pronto a lavorare con la Commissione fin da subito.

interventions.speaker_label: Ciaran Mullooly, on behalf of the Renew Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Renew Group

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, Minister, the rising cost of housing has become one of the defining political challenges of a generation.

Minister, in your own county, Hannah Clarke from St Vincent de Paul in Navan in County Meath told me that where once they were asked to help with food and heat, today they are being asked to help with rent and eviction notices. In County Galway, Carina, a mother of seven, tells me that six children still live at home. The eldest is 29. They all have good jobs, but they can't move out because the average price of a house is EUR 400 000.

So, while the aims of the EU Affordable Housing Act to deal with areas under housing stress are admirable, you know, Commissioner, there is more work to be done. Vulture funds: you talked about doing something like this next year. Let's bring it on as quickly as we can to try and get in there and bring down the price of a house – because that is what we must do.

We must act quicker and easier to try and build and renovate homes. How can we do that? Let us try and bring forward legislation in this area. But also at Member State level, let us look at that as well. Let us look at ways in which we can bring down the cost of building our new homes and deal with this serious issue.

interventions.speaker_label: Vicent Marzà Ibáñez, en nombre del Grupo Verts/ALE.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señorías, la paciencia de la gente ha terminado. Escuchen a la gente que está en la calle, escuchen a la gente que está acampando en Valencia, en Alacant, en Madrid: no pueden más. No pueden más de matarse a trabajar para transferir todo su sueldo a los rentistas; no pueden más de matarse a trabajar para acabar alquilando una pequeñísima habitación en un piso compartido minúsculo. La gente joven no puede ni soñar en emanciparse. Hay trabajadores públicos que están renunciando a trabajos porque no se pueden pagar el alquiler en la zona, en el pueblo donde tienen que trabajar. Hay gente mayor a la que se está expulsando de su casa después de estar pagando 50 años religiosamente su alquiler. ¿Por qué? Porque es más rentable poner ese piso y echar a una mujer jubilada, para que se haga negocio con los pisos de alquiler.

Mientras ellos duermen en la calle, ustedes lo que plantean es una serie de actividades legislativas, burocráticas, con muy buena intención, pero que no les resuelven el problema ahora, les piden que esperen. ¿Esperar a qué? ¿A que nadie pueda pagar ya nunca el alquiler? Deben despertar, despertar y prohibir de verdad que los fondos buitre puedan comprar casas; ampliemos de verdad el parque asequible de vivienda y protejamos la vida y no a aquellos que especulan con ella.
Si hacen eso ahora, tendrán nuestros votos y el apoyo de la mayoría de la ciudadanía europea. Si no lo hacen, nos tendrán en la calle con la gente que está luchando por una vivienda digna.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: au nom du groupe The Left

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, il y a 20 ans, jour pour jour, avec des galériens du logement, nous fondions le collectif Jeudi Noir pour faire baisser les loyers en éclatant la bulle immobilière. Nous occupions des immeubles vides, accaparés par des banques et des compagnies d'assurances. Et pour nous faire entendre, nous lancions des confettis sur les ministres du logement et les propriétaires véreux.

Je vous avoue que ce matin, j'étais tentée de venir avec des confettis dans mes poches et de vous en lancer, ici, des poignées à la figure. Car 20 ans plus tard, rien n'a changé, tout a empiré. Des vieilles dames sont expulsées par des fonds vautours. Les loyers explosent. Un salaire ne suffit plus pour se loger dignement. De la Puerta del Sol à Paris, une vague populaire immense se lève en clamant qu'un logement est un droit, pas un actif financier.

Les solutions, nous les répétons depuis 20 ans: encadrer les loyers, construire des logements sociaux, mobiliser les logements vacants, combattre la spéculation. Mais toutes ces mesures, il est grand temps de les appliquer aujourd'hui. Aujourd'hui, plutôt qu'avec des confettis, je vous le dis avec des mots: collègues de droite, Madame von der Leyen, Monsieur le Commissaire, cessez d'engraisser la rente immobilière et faites du logement un droit.

paragraphs.text: Vážený pán predsedajúci, v celej Únii je obrovský problém s bývaním, ale hlavne, že na ubytovanie a prijímanie imigrantov išlo dokopy už viac než 100 miliárd eur. Hlavne, že dávate desiatky miliárd eur do bývania v tzv. marginalizovaných komunitách, pričom len na Slovensku išla do osád viac ako miliarda eur. A výsledok? Žiadny. Premrhané peniaze. Ja sa pýtam, prečo nedáte tieto peniaze na podporu bývania pre všetkých slušných ľudí? Prečo nezoberie tých 800 miliárd eur, ktoré chcete dať teraz na nákupy zbraní a rakiet na vojnu proti Rusku a nepresuniete to do podpory dostupnosti bývania pre všetkých slušných ľudí. Prečo nezatlačíte na banky, aby dávali mladomanželom pri prvej hypotéke nižšie úroky, ako to bolo kedysi v našich krajinách, keď bývali tzv. mladomanželské pôžičky? Prečo dnes nezatlačíte na developerov, aby nedržali byty úmyselne a vedome prázdne kvôli špekuláciám s cenami? Riešenia sú ale to, čo ponúka Únia, je naozaj len ďalšia byrokracia. Ale riešenia sú rázne a potrebné a my sme ich pripravení priniesť.

interventions.speaker_label: Dan Jørgensen, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, are short-term rentals inherently a problem? No. I actually think that it is a great idea. It makes it easier for people to travel and for some people, the income that they can get renting out a room or an apartment some nights can actually be the income that they need to be able to stay where they stay. But we've seen an increase in short-term rentals, especially in some cities in Europe, that has moved away from that original idea and made it a business model, so that what we see is de facto buildings being bought with that sole purpose of having short-term rentals. Short-term rentals that are actually chateau hotels. This has never been the purpose and if cities want to do something about this, because it's driving people out of their municipalities, then of course they should be able to. Today, unfortunately, they are not. They don't have the legal clarity.

Some say is this even a European matter. Well, there's two answers to that question: a bureaucratic one and a political one. The bureaucratic one is, yes, this is about capital, this is about services. So yes, of course, it's internal market. The political answer is that, yes, this is at the top of our citizens' list of concerns: the lack of affordable housing. So obviously we need to deal with this.

Now, with regard to second homes, buildings, apartments, houses that are being bought sometimes as a commodity – instead of buying gold, you buy an apartment and then you hope that it'll increase in value – okay, if you want that in your city, if you want that in your country, if you think this is healthy, keep it. But if you don't, if you think that maybe you want to do something about this, if you think that maybe it's difficult to explain to your citizens that there's a lack of housing, but every third house is empty, then of course you should have the possibility to do something about it.
We don't force cities to do anything. We don't force Member States to do anything. But we provide them with an opportunity and a possibility to fight one of the biggest challenges that they have.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, I'm happy that I was after your first clarification because we can go a bit deeper now – because I think everyone does agree: we are in a massive housing crisis.

Now, what I don't want to do, Mr Commissioner, is to create an alibi for failing national governments on housing policies. I fear that if we take this road that you are proposing now, this is very much a possibility, because when I look at the Affordable Housing Act, in relation to the short-term rentals or the second homes, I have great difficulty finding the affordable in it. It doesn't build a house, it doesn't repurpose an empty building, it doesn't actually do something to increase the supply. It is working on the demand side of things, which I believe and the data shows, even when you look at rent controls and all the other things that people have tried, they have failed to increase supply.

Now, housing is not an EU competence; it's something that is done on local, regional and national levels, and this proposal builds a legal framework that somehow elevates it to this place, which I believe is very, very tricky because regional authorities and local authorities are already making rules about short-term rentals. I mean, in Amsterdam you can do 15 days only from your own home. There is no legal problem there. They can do it themselves. So why do we need to create a legal framework that will inevitably create problems? Because Amsterdam is not the same thing as a village an hour from Amsterdam. Why do we try to create unity where there is none? Also not when it comes to countries in more touristic destinations in the south of Europe.

So, from our perspective, you have a huge opportunity to make building easier: do simplification as you promised. That is what we expect from you and not to create a bureaucratic and legal construct which simply puts the ball on the 11-metre spot to create more polarisation in local communities about housing policies.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Die Wohnpreise sind zu einem großen Problem geworden in Europa; für die Jugend, die kein eigenes Leben starten kann, aber auch für die Mittelschicht, die sich offensichtlich das Leben und die Wohnungen, die sie sich wünscht, nicht mehr leisten kann. Und ein Problem dabei sind eben diese Short-Time-Rental-Modelle, weil sie das Angebot an leistbarem Wohnraum verkürzen. Und wenn das Angebot verkürzt wird, dann steigt der Preis. Und das trifft genau die Mittelschicht, die sich das Leben in den Zentren und in den Städten nicht mehr leisten kann.

Deswegen ist es wichtig, dass mit diesem Affordable Housing Act jetzt eine Rechtsform geschaffen wird, dass die Bürgermeisterinnen und Bürgermeister unserer Städte die Maßnahmen ergreifen können, die sie für richtig halten, um dagegen anzukämpfen. Endlich Freiheit für die Bürgermeister, damit sie gegen diesen Irrlauf des Marktes ankämpfen können! Das ist gut und wichtig. Und genauso müssen wir auch die Spekulation bekämpfen, weil auch die Spekulation den leistbaren Wohnraum und das Angebot an leistbarem Wohnraum bekämpft. Wir Sozialdemokraten, wir stehen für leistbare Wohnbaupolitik in Europa, in den Nationalstaaten und in unseren Städten.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, face à la crise du logement, certains États européens ont déjà fait le choix de donner la priorité à ceux qui ont un lien durable avec leur territoire. À Vienne, l'accès au logement social est conditionné à une durée minimale de résidence. Aux Pays-Bas, les communes peuvent privilégier les habitants ayant un ancrage local. En Pologne, l'accès de certains ressortissants étrangers aux aides au logement dépend de leur statut de séjour.

En France, il y a aujourd'hui près de 3 millions de demandes de logements sociaux. Nous assumons donc d'aller plus loin. Nous voulons inscrire dans notre droit la priorité nationale, afin que les Français soient prioritaires dans l'attribution de logements sociaux. Et s'il faut pour cela modifier notre Constitution, eh bien, nous demanderons aux Français qu'ils se prononcent par référendum.

Et je veux être très claire ici: nous ne laisserons jamais la Commission européenne s'approprier la compétence du logement. Ce domaine doit par essence rester une compétence des États. C'est au peuple français, et non à Bruxelles, de décider à qui doit bénéficier en priorité la solidarité nationale.

paragraphs.text: Domnule președinte, domnule comisar, dragi colegi, criza locuirii este una din cele mai mari probleme cu care se confruntă astăzi tinerii europeni. Prea mulți tineri nu își permit să plece de acasă, să își cumpere prima locuință sau să își întemeieze o familie. De aceea, nu ne confruntăm doar cu o criză a locuirii, ci și cu una demografică. Sunt de acord că avem nevoie de mai multe locuințe accesibile, dar nu pot susține o abordare care încalcă dreptul la proprietate privată și tratează proprietarii ca parte a problemei. O familie care a muncit și și-a cumpărat o a doua locuință, poate pentru copii și o închiriază pentru a-și completa veniturile, nu este dușmanul tânărului care își caută o primă casă.

Mai mult, mă întreb dacă această propunere a Comisiei a ținut cont de recomandările Parlamentului European. Raportul nostru a cerut măsuri concrete pentru creșterea ofertei, accelerarea autorizațiilor, reducerea costurilor de construcție, acces la finanțare și sprijin pentru cei care își cumpără prima locuință. În schimb, astăzi, discuția se concentrează mai mult pe închirierea pe termen scurt, care la nivelul UE reprezintă doar 1,2 % din fondul locativ. Haideți să le spunem cetățenilor adevărul: problema fundamentală este că nu construim suficient. Avem nevoie de mai puțină birocrație, autorizații mai rapide, mai multe construcții și stimulente pentru proprietarii care își pun locuințele pe piață.

Vreau o Europă care îi ajută pe tineri să devină proprietari, nu una care îi face pe proprietari vinovați de criza locuințelor. Poate că dacă vrem mai multe familii și mai mulți copii europeni, trebuie să le oferim tinerilor posibilitatea de a-și construi aici o casă, o familie și un viitor. O Europă care nu își permite să își întemeieze familii, nu își permite nici viitorul.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, met deze wet betaalbaar wonen hebben we de eerste steen gelegd. Maar ik kan hem niet vieren, want het gaat alleen maar over de commerciële huur. Alleen maar over platforms zoals Airbnb. En zelfs dat wordt niet doortastend aangepakt. De steden waar de problemen echt groot zijn, zoals Amsterdam en Barcelona, hebben aan deze aanpak niks. Wat moeten we wél doen? We moeten echte ambitie tonen. We moeten doorbraken realiseren. Kijk naar wat er nu in Nederland gebeurt. Toen onze premier Rob Jetten in een campagne beloofde dat hij 100 000 woningen ging bouwen, zei iedereen dat het niet kon. Volgend jaar gaan we het gewoon wel doen. Het kan wel. Onze minister legt binnen een jaar vijftig voorstellen neer om sneller woningen te realiseren. Wat gaat ze doen? Zorgen dat woningdelen makkelijker is. Zorgen dat er meer vergunningen verleend worden. Zorgen dat er meer vakmensen opgeleid worden. Zo pakken we de echte wooncrisis aan. We moeten aan de slag en Europa moet dat ondersteunen.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Die Würde des Menschen ist unantastbar. Die eigene Wohnung, das Dach über dem Kopf eines Menschen muss es auch sein. Punkt. Die gegenwärtige Wohnungskrise hat sozialen Sprengstoff, gesellschaftlichen Sprengstoff. Und sie hat politischen Sprengstoff, wie die Proteste von Hunderttausenden und die nun angekündigten Neuwahlen in Spanien zeigen. Es zeigen sich die Risse eines Systems, welches nahezu pervertiert, Profitinteressen vor das Wohlergehen der Bürgerinnen und Bürger stellt. In Europa sind die Wohnkosten nicht grundlos seit 2015 im Schnitt um 60 Prozent gestiegen. Und es zeigt, wie schamlos hier Rechtskonservative auch in diesem Hohen Haus Bürgernähe und Verständnis für die Alltagssorgen der Menschen heucheln, um es dann noch den Markt regeln zu lassen. Shame.

Und auch der Kommissionsentwurf ist hier im Kern ein Lobbygeschenk. Schluss mit steigenden Mieten, Schluss mit explodierenden Wohnkosten, Schluss mit Zwangsräumungen! Wir brauchen mehr Spielraum für die Kommunen. Das ist eine dringend notwendige Korrektur. Menschen in Wohnungen und Wohnungen für Menschen. Das muss unsere Leitlinie sein.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, questo è il suono della protesta per il diritto alla casa che attraversa la Spagna. Un simbolo di lotta che speriamo di sentire molto presto nelle strade di tutta Europa, perché nelle nostre città è diventato ormai impossibile vivere.

Gli affitti sono alle stelle, i mutui inaccessibili, le case popolari sono troppo poche e troppe quelle lasciate colpevolmente vuote. Mentre milioni di persone si ammazzano di lavoro per pagare l'affitto o il mutuo, dall'altra parte ci sono pochi privilegiati che possono permettersi di vivere senza lavorare, che affittano le loro proprietà vivendo di rendita.

Ora basta. Basta con il business della casa, basta con la rendita parassitaria. La casa non deve più essere una fonte di guadagno, ma lo spazio sacro attorno a cui costruire le nostre vite. La casa è un diritto, non una merce. Mobilitiamoci, lottiamo, scioperiamo, come in Spagna, come a Berlino, ovunque. Facciamole suonare sempre più forte. Evviva la lotta per la casa!

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Wenn 37 Millionen legale und illegale Einwanderer seit 2015 nach Europa geströmt sind und anschließend 10 Millionen Wohnungen fehlen, ist das eine ganz einfache Rechenaufgabe, die jeder Hilfsschüler sofort lösen kann. Nicht so die Europäische Union. Sie arbeitet sich lieber an Vermietern, Bauherren und Eigentümern ab – ausgerechnet an jenen, die überhaupt noch Wohnraum schaffen. Irre Verordnungen und geplante Eingriffe – der pure Wahnsinn. Dabei ist die Schaffung von Wohnraum ein nationales Recht, und das muss es auch bleiben.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, ο κανονισμός για την οικονομικά προσιτή στέγαση δεν μπορεί να αφορά το πώς θα λειτουργεί καλύτερα η αγορά: η αγορά, η κερδοσκοπία, μας έφτασαν εδώ σήμερα.

Στην Κυψέλη της Αθήνας οι οικογένειες δίνουν μάχη για τα ίδια τους τα σπίτια, μετά τις σοβαρές ζημιές που έγιναν σε πολυκατοικίες από ιδιώτη εργολάβο στα έργα του μετρό. Στην Ελλάδα και σε ολόκληρη την Ευρώπη, πολίτες βρίσκονται αντιμέτωποι με πλειστηριασμούς από ιδιωτικές τράπεζες, servicers και funds, εταιρείες-οχήματα κερδοσκοπίας.

Πρέπει να προστατεύσουμε τον άνθρωπο και το σπίτι του. Και αυτό ακριβώς διεκδικεί μια πανευρωπαϊκή πρωτοβουλία κινημάτων, ενώσεων ενοικιαστών και συνδικάτων που στις 14 Οκτωβρίου έρχεται στις Βρυξέλλες. Προστασία από εξώσεις και πλειστηριασμούς, δημόσια και κοινωνική κατοικία, αξιοποίηση των κενών ακινήτων και πραγματικά όρια στην κερδοσκοπία. Τη φωνή τους μεταφέρω σήμερα εδώ. Η Ευρώπη πρέπει να επιλέξει το δικαίωμα στη στέγη και όχι στην κερδοσκοπία πάνω στη στέγη.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident! Sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar, sorry, aber das war zu wenig. Ich habe zu Beginn der Legislatur begrüßt, dass Ursula von der Leyen die Wohnungsnot auf die Agenda gesetzt hat. Gerade in Großstädten wie in Berlin besorgt das Thema die Menschen sehr. Und wir als Parlament haben zwei Jahre intensiv daran gearbeitet und gute Empfehlungen vorgelegt. Leider ist von diesen in Ihrem Vorschlag nicht viel zu finden. Wir brauchen kein neues EU-Gesetz. Wir brauchen einen Entrümpelungs-Omnibus, der bürokratische Hürden abbaut, Doppelungen und Widersprüche beseitigt und Investitionen erleichtert. Wir brauchen schnellere digitale Genehmigungen und einen Check, ob Baustoffe ausreichend und bezahlbar überhaupt zur Verfügung stehen. Und wir brauchen, wie in der State of the Union angekündigt, einen Pakt mit den Mitgliedstaaten gegen überambitionierte nationale Umsetzungen, beispielsweise der Gebäudeenergieeffizienz-Richtlinie, oder noch besser deren umfassende Überarbeitung.

Sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar! Bisher war das symbolisches Kratzen an der Oberfläche, aber dafür ist die Lage zu ernst. Die Sorge um bezahlbares Wohnen stärkt radikale Kräfte, deren Enteignungsfantasien Gift für jede Investition in den Wohnungsbau sind. Bitte gehen Sie wirklich in die Tiefe des Bauregulatorik-Dschungels, damit wieder mehr Wohnungen und Häuser fertig werden. Lassen Sie uns alle nicht vergessen: Es ist Eigentum, das Sicherheit schafft. Und diesen Traum müssen wir durch echte Kostensenkungen wieder für alle möglich machen.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, España ha dicho basta. La gente ha salido a las calles y no piensa volver hasta que no tengan una vivienda digna. Hablamos de familias que gastan más de la mitad de su sueldo en alquiler, jóvenes que no pueden emanciparse o personas como Maricarmen que son desahuciadas a los 87 años.

Estamos ante una emergencia habitacional no solo en España, sino también en Europa, y por ello se requieren medidas extraordinarias. No hay soluciones mágicas, lo sabemos, pero sí hay dos opciones políticas muy diferentes: intervenir el mercado para proteger el derecho a la vivienda digna o reivindicar la libertad para proteger los fondos buitre.

Los socialistas tenemos muy claro de qué lado de la historia estamos. Desde Europa, comisario, trabajaremos por una Ley de Vivienda Asequible ambiciosa, que aporte a los municipios cobertura legal para limitar los alquileres turísticos y de corta duración y que permita actuar frente a la especulación y poder habilitar viviendas asequibles. Porque, como decía Silvia Pérez Cruz: es indecente, es indecente, gente sin casa, casas sin gente. Partido Popular, ¿en qué lado están? ¿Consideran que la vivienda es un negocio o un derecho más?

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, Brussel heeft ons inmiddels een indrukwekkend pakket aan crises bezorgd: een energiecrisis, een stikstofcrisis, een klimaatcrisis en een enorme asielcrisis. Nu mogen we daar ook nog de huizencrisis aan toevoegen. Uitgerekend mevrouw von der Leyen komt met een EU-masterplan voor betaalbare woningen. Want als er één organisatie bekend staat om betaalbare oplossingen, dan is het de EU wel. Laten we vooral niet kijken naar de gevolgen van stikstofregels die de bouw vertragen. Ook niet naar klimaat- en energieregels die bouwen duurder maken. En al helemaal niet naar de gevolgen van de ongecontroleerde massa-immigratie. Nee, dat zou wel erg ongemakkelijk worden. Het is makkelijker om de vinger te wijzen naar Airbnb. Alsof de huizencrisis is ontstaan omdat een paar huiseigenaren hun woning aan toeristen verhuren. De boodschap van de PVV is duidelijk: stop je te bemoeien met nationale aangelegenheden. Wat Brussel aanraakt, verandert namelijk niet in goud, maar in bureaucratische drek. Het is tijd dat Nederland weer baas wordt in eigen land.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario, ¿qué esperanza le queda a toda una generación que trabaja pero no puede comprarse una casa? En España, hay parejas jóvenes que necesitan sumar dos salarios solo para afrontar el alquiler y los gastos básicos; ahorrar, tener hijos o construir un futuro se convierten en un lujo.

Ahora necesitamos más viviendas disponibles y para construirlas tenemos que apoyar la inversión y fomentar la colaboración público-privada. Sin ellas no vamos a aumentar suficientemente la oferta para hacer la vivienda más asequible. Por eso debemos: agilizar las licencias, fomentar la inversión a la construcción, dar seguridad jurídica a quienes ponen su vivienda en alquiler y también ayudar a quien lo necesita.

Desde ECR pedimos que este plan europeo convierta esas prioridades en hogares que los jóvenes puedan pagar, porque nuestros jóvenes no quieren que les regalemos una vida, quieren que su trabajo les permita construirla.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, the new Eurostat data show that only in three Member States, we see the trend of annual decrease in house prices. Rent prices are still rising like crazy: Romania 41 %, Croatia 22 %. So the crisis is still hitting hard.

In that context, we welcome the Affordable Housing Act, which will target only one segment of the housing crisis: uncontrolled short-term rental policies. Let us give mayors and local authorities the tools they need to restrict the uncontrolled spread of short-term rentals.

However, the methodology to declare areas under housing stress must be simple and efficient, not to be lost in complicated calculation procedures. The restriction measures in lower income Member States – this is really important – must protect small-scale landlords who supplement their insufficient monthly household budget through renting. The problem does not lie within them, but rather with those speculators who hold large numbers of apartments to profit from them. Let's focus on them.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Naprawdę podziwiam bezczelność kasty politycznej. Obiecujecie tanie mieszkania, ale najpierw wystawiacie obywatelom rachunek, a później ogłaszacie, że przychodzicie im z pomocą. Tak naprawdę co się kryje za obietnicą tanich mieszkań? Drugą ręką dokładacie ludziom koszty budowy, ogrzewania, prądu i remontów. Żeby postawić dom, trzeba przejść coraz cięższe procedury. Ktoś za to musi płacić – czasem i pieniądzem. I ten rachunek dostaje rodzina, która chciała swoje własne cztery ściany.

Do tego dochodzi to zaślepienie zieloną polityką. Przecież ETS obciąża produkcję cementu, energii i stali. Koszty uprawnień do emisji nie znikają tylko dlatego, że mówicie, że chodzi o ratowanie klimatu. A gwoździem do trumny będzie ETS 2, który jeszcze bardziej zwiększy koszty.

paragraphs.text: Vážený pán predsedajúci, cenovo dostupné bývanie dnes nie je len problémom ľudí s nízkymi príjmami. Je to existenčná výzva aj pre mladé rodiny a pre ľudí, ktorí napriek tomu, že pracujú, si vlastné bývanie ani nájomné bývanie nemôžu dovoliť. Ja vítam, že po rokoch špekulácií a manipulácií s cenami bytov súkromnými spoločnosťami a rôznymi špekulantmi okolo nájomného bývania prichádza Komisia s návrhom, že túto tému otvára. Ale tento návrh sám o sebe ani nové byty nepostaví a ani cenu bývania, žiaľbohu, nezníži. Aj samotná Komisia priznáva, že jeho vplyv na ceny a dostupnosť bude skôr nepriamy a bude závisieť od opatrení jednotlivých štátov, miest či samospráv. Na Slovensku vláda Roberta Fica rozvíja systém štátom podporovaného bývania a tento rok už vyčlenila ďalšie zdroje na podporu výstavby nájomných bytov. Takéto národné programy by mala Európska komisia podporovať a umožňovať ich rozšírenie. Treba pomôcť členským štátom výrazne zvýšiť ponuku dostupného bývania zrýchlením povoľovania výstavby a mobilizovať verejných a súkromných investícií.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario, construir un hogar es la principal preocupación de millones de europeos. El problema de fondo es estructural: faltan viviendas y se necesitan casi 10 millones para responder a la demanda actual.
Debemos ofrecer oportunidades a las familias y especialmente a los jóvenes. Para ello, la construcción y movilización de inversión pública y privada sin interferencias ni ideologías es fundamental.

Sin embargo, la propuesta de la Comisión vuelve a empezar la casa por el tejado: restringir los alquileres de corta duración y las segundas residencias tal y como lo proponen supone un ataque directo a la propiedad privada. No podemos conformarnos con redistribuir la escasez, que seguirá existiendo si no construimos más. Defendamos la cultura del esfuerzo, del ahorro y de la propiedad. Detrás de muchas viviendas hay familias que han ahorrado durante años e invertido sus recursos para obtener un ingreso extra. No desincentive a quienes aportan oferta al mercado. Hacen falta más viviendas e inversión.

Europa debe aportar simplificando normas y siendo parte de la solución y no a través de supuestas recomendaciones que no resuelven el problema. Frente a la escasez, ampliemos soluciones y facilitemos alternativas.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, Minister, conservatives here say the market will fix the housing crisis. The right to property is all they defend. In Dublin, we see tourists in family homes, families in hotel rooms, children in emergency accommodation, doing homework on fire escapes, young adults stuck in their childhood bedrooms, communities deprived of essential workers – all caused by a heartless mindset that lets profit rule.

Commissioner, I am happy to see, thanks to our political family, that we are taking action with the Affordable Housing Act, giving councils the power to curb short-term lets, putting families back in homes. The EU budget must also deliver under the Irish Presidency. We demand EUR 100 billion for social and affordable housing and to end homelessness. We were promised an EU housing summit before the end of the year. Where is it?

Children in Gardiner Street in Dublin doing their homework on a fire escape have a right to housing. The market has betrayed them. And so have those right-wing politicians who worship at the altar of the market.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, dobbiamo affrontare questo tema con pragmatismo. È da poco entrato in vigore un regolamento europeo sugli affitti brevi, nato per garantire trasparenza e condivisione dei dati. Introdurre nuove restrizioni, prima di valutare gli effetti, sarebbe un errore di metodo.

La politica abitativa deve rimanere una competenza nazionale e territoriale. Il diritto di proprietà è un pilastro della nostra economia. Non possiamo decidere a Bruxelles come i proprietari debbano utilizzare i propri immobili.

Non possiamo attribuire agli affitti brevi e al turismo la responsabilità della crisi abitativa. Per borghi, isole e aree rurali il turismo significa occupazione ed economia reale. Le esigenze di una grande città sono diverse da quelle di una località montana o rurale. Un approccio unico rischia di creare più distorsioni che soluzioni.

La vera priorità è aumentare l'offerta abitativa, intervenendo sulle cause strutturali della crisi, senza penalizzare il turismo, senza centralizzare competenze e senza comprimere il diritto di proprietà.

Le esigenze di una grande città sono diverse da quelle di una località montana o rurale. Un approccio unico rischia di creare più distorsioni che soluzioni.

La vera priorità è aumentare l'offerta abitativa, intervenendo sulle cause strutturali della crisi, senza penalizzare il turismo, senza centralizzare competenze e senza comprimere il diritto di proprietà.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, cuatro de cada diez europeos considera que la falta de vivienda accesible es un problema inmediato. Las clases medias tienen dificultades y muchos jóvenes no pueden independizarse.

Tenemos una oportunidad, por lo tanto, con esta Ley europea de Vivienda Asequible. Pero tenemos que hacerlo bien porque también estamos viendo qué es lo que está ocurriendo en el Estado español. El Gobierno ha aguantado una legislatura sin presupuestos, pero en quince días el foco mediático ha cambiado de Ceuta a los desahucios y de ahí a unas elecciones anticipadas.

Con esto lo único que quiero decir es que tenemos que ser capaces de leer el sentir de la gente y llegar a unos acuerdos de marcos jurídicos mínimos que nos permitan proteger a vulnerables, hacer al pequeño propietario partícipe de la solución sin cargarle con responsabilidades que son de las administraciones, pararle —por supuesto— los pies a fondos buitres, a las prácticas abusivas y a la especulación, regular los alquileres que son de temporada allá donde son un problema real para el acceso a la vivienda, pero también aumentar la oferta y la rehabilitación y hacerlo agilizando, construyendo más y más rápido y a precios razonables.

Estas acciones son complementarias, no son excluyentes. Y quien quiera hacernos ver otra cosa es que está haciendo otro tipo de sumas y restas. Hagámoslo bien, por lo tanto, y alcancemos el acuerdo que es necesario para dar solución a este reto habitacional.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, a Roma 400 persone hanno perso la casa, nell'esperienza di Spin Time, perché il fondo immobiliare che detiene l'immobile l'ha voluto indietro. Il Comune ha provato a comprarlo, ma niente. Nel frattempo, queste persone sono state ricollocate e le liste d'attesa per le case popolari si sono bloccate. E questo perché? Perché non possiamo mica toccare un fondo immobiliare!

Signor Commissario, possiamo dire che il diritto di un fondo immobiliare di fare profitto non è uguale a quello delle persone ad avere una casa? Possiamo dire che l'abitare è un diritto e che il profitto dei miliardari viene dopo, tanto dopo?

Perché controllare gli affitti brevi è doveroso, ma non possiamo farlo con una serie infinita di clausole e non ci può essere solo questo. Come distribuiamo le regole? Ai sindaci che vogliono regolare il mercato, una gabbia di criteri. A chi invece specula, trasformando le case in investimenti finanziari, nessuno strumento vincolante.
La gente letteralmente non può più vivere, e oggi in Spagna è evidente. Possiamo iniziare a difendere i diritti di queste persone e non di chi specula sulle nostre spalle?

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Bostaden är inte en vara, det är en mänsklig rättighet, och bostadsbristen är en av vår tids absolut största frågor. I Madrid har stora demonstrationer startat efter att 87-åriga Maricarmen blev vräkt från sin bostad. När det inte finns några lägenheter med rimliga hyror så begränsas människan i sitt liv. Hon kan inte flytta dit jobben finns eller där studierna finns. Hon kan inte flytta ihop med någon som hon älskar, och inte heller separera från en partner som gör att hon inte mår bra. Det är konsekvenserna av en högerpolitik här i EU, och i mitt land Sverige, som gör att samhället spricker i sömmarna.

Jag vill se ett Europa som sätter människan före marknaden. Men det finns ljusglimtar. I staden Göteborg inför vänsterstyret hyresgarantier som underlättar för människor att få ett förstahandskontrakt.

Demonstrationerna i Madrid ledde till att Maricarmen nu fått flytta tillbaka till sin lägenhet. Politiskt mod och folkligt motstånd ger resultat, och kampen för allas rätt till ett tryggt hem fortsätter.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, la loi «Logement» de l'Union européenne veut prioritairement réguler la location de courte durée touristique, qui ne représente en fait qu'1,2 % des logements en Europe. Inutile de dire qu'elle ne résoudra pas la crise du logement qui sévit dans nombre d'États membres, grevant le pouvoir d'achat des ménages.

Parmi ceux dont le taux d'effort est le plus élevé, il y a les jeunes: étudiants, apprentis, jeunes actifs. En moyenne, en Europe, 10 % des jeunes consacrent plus de 40 % de leurs ressources au logement. L'âge moyen de départ du domicile parental recule.

Une étude sur le logement des jeunes a été publiée cette année par le Parlement européen. Elle propose notamment, et cela relève de l'Union, de mobiliser des investissements pour le logement étudiant, par exemple avec la BEI, InvestEU ou les fonds FEDER, de créer des garanties de dépôt, à l'image de la garantie Visale en France, ou d'intégrer davantage le logement dans les financements Erasmus+.
Alors, ma question est très simple, Monsieur le Commissaire, la Commission a-t-elle commencé à travailler à ces axes d'amélioration en faveur du logement des jeunes?

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Vice-président, Monsieur le Commissaire, il aura fallu du temps, mais nous y sommes enfin. L'Union européenne se saisit concrètement du sujet du logement abordable. Cette proposition législative est un acte majeur par sa seule existence, puisque c'est la première fois qu'il y a une législation sur le sujet. Espérons qu'elle porte ses fruits et qu'elle soit suivie d'autres initiatives tant le défi est immense.

À cet égard, si le logement abordable est une priorité indiscutable, n'oublions pas que le logement social a aussi besoin d'être soutenu. La question d'un meilleur encadrement des locations de courte durée est un premier pas dont nous nous félicitons. Mais gardons à l'esprit que ce nouveau modèle européen ne fonctionnera que s'il met pleinement les collectivités locales au centre du jeu, car ce sont elles qui connaissent finalement le mieux leur territoire. Attention à ne pas imposer trop de critères pour désigner des zones tendues, dont l'effet cumulé pourrait restreindre la capacité des maires à agir efficacement. Attention aux restrictions sur la réglementation des résidences principales. En France, ce qui fonctionne le mieux, nous disent les maires, c'est la règle du maximum de 120 nuitées par an. Alors, ne cassons pas ce qui existe déjà.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, en España en ocho años de Gobierno socialista la vivienda se ha encarecido un 74 % en la compra y 40 % en el alquiler, pero a los fondos de inversión, alfombra roja e incentivos fiscales que niegan a los españoles.

4 millones de extranjeros más en ocho años, 4 millones que han colapsado el mercado de la compra y el alquiler, poniendo fin a las aspiraciones de jóvenes y familias de disponer de una vivienda en propiedad, como tuvieron sus padres y sus abuelos.

La oferta ha sido aniquilada en la escasez, porque ustedes ni construyen ni dejan construir, y se han puesto del lado del okupa, del que no paga y del que asalta la frontera. Es el resultado de secuestrar el suelo para especular desde el poder con el futuro de los españoles, del exceso de burocracia y la fiscalidad abusiva y el abandono de las políticas de vivienda que fueron tan exitosas para una España que fue de propietarios y ahora es de vulnerables.

Pero se puede hacer de otra manera: desregular, remigrar y establecer la prioridad nacional. Solo se trata de ponerse del lado del pueblo español. Ya sé que a ustedes les cuesta, pero solo se trata de eso.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, how we deal with the housing crisis facing European citizens will be the defining moment of our time.
To date, we have been undermining intergenerational solidarity and social cohesion. And if we're not careful, we will fracture society deeply.

We are obsessed with process over progress, Commissioner. We simply have stifled any capability in developing infrastructure across Europe, both in terms of water, electricity, roads and infrastructure that underpins housing.

Honestly, at this stage, we know the rulebook is not allowing us to deliver either through the market or through social and affordable housing by local authorities and governments directly. So we need to have an aggressive look at what is holding us back in terms of the regulations that are impinging on our ability to build homes for citizens.

I do welcome the act. It does look at short-term lets, and it gives greater power to local authorities and mayors to make decisions based on their local circumstances. But, more broadly, we need to ensure that there are no regulations in place that prohibit our ability to build infrastructure that ultimately underpins supply of homes.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, I was in Madrid and it was horrible as a human being to see this 87-year-old woman dragged out of her house. Thousands of people came out – out of solidarity – and thousands of people cannot afford the housing they need, which is a human, European right. It should be a human right.

My problem with the housing plan is that the Commission does not define affordability. And it is as if we do not want it to touch on too many interests. Let me tell you what affordability is: if you need several jobs to sustain a living, that's not affordability. We can find a definition easily: you don't have to have three jobs to be able to live under a roof; you don't have to wait until you're 40 to be able to move out of your parents' home. How can you start a family if you don't even have an apartment?
So, Commissioner, let's act. Let's work hard against speculation, against big investment funds that make it impossible to live, against Airbnbs. Let's make it hard. And give everyone a house.
