paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Szanowny Panie Komisarzu! Chciałabym zacząć od bardzo prostego pytania: czy zapoznał się pan z rekomendacjami Parlamentu Europejskiego dotyczącymi kryzysu mieszkaniowego? Parlament wskazał w nich bardzo konkretne rozwiązania, również dotyczące osób, które dziś są praktycznie wykluczone z rynku mieszkaniowego.

W Unii Europejskiej żyje 90 milionów osób z niepełnosprawnościami, co stanowi prawie 24% dorosłej populacji. Dlatego chciałabym zapytać wprost: czy komisja zamierza przygotować konkretny instrument legislacyjny dotyczący mieszkań wspomaganych i dostępnego mieszkalnictwa, tak aby osoby z niepełnosprawnościami mogły rzeczywiście korzystać z prawa do niezależnego życia? Bo na razie, kiedy mówimy o działaniach legislacyjnych w obszarze mieszkalnictwa, słyszymy wyłącznie o regulowaniu najmu krótkoterminowego.

Co więcej, Komisja stawia kolejne wymogi dotyczące danych i każe nam najpierw udowadniać, że problem rzeczywiście istnieje. Przecież gdyby nie istniał, nie rozmawialibyśmy o nim od ponad dwóch lat. A co z ludźmi, którzy w ogóle nie mają dostępu do rynku mieszkaniowego?

Jest jeszcze jedna rzecz. To, co wybudujemy i wyremontujemy dziś, będzie służyło przez dziesięciolecia. Nie możemy więc przegapić szansy, aby zadbać o wspólne standardy dostępności mieszkań. I nie mówię tylko o osobach z niepełnosprawnościami, bo nie każdy z nas będzie osobą niepełnosprawną, ale każdy z nas będzie osobą starszą, wymagającą wsparcia.

paragraphs.text: Panie Przewodniczący! Kryzys mieszkaniowy dotyka dziś miliony Europejek i Europejczyków. Szczególnie dotyka osoby młode i osoby o niższych dochodach i oczywiście kobiety. Widzimy to wszędzie w Europie. Mieszkania i tak już są dla młodych ludzi nieosiągalnym marzeniem. Ale to, co robią niektórzy deweloperzy, dosłownie i w przenośni wyciąga młodych ludzi na ulicę.

W Madrycie ludzie wyszli na ulice, bo nie mogli pojąć, jak można wyeksmitować 87-letnią kobietę, która mieszkała w mieszkaniu przez siedem dekad. W Poznaniu, w Polsce ludzie wyszli na ulice, bo nie mogą pojąć, jak można wyeksmitować samotną matkę z dzieckiem z mieszkania, w którym mieszkała od urodzenia.

Cieszę się bardzo, że dzięki socjalistom i demokratom mamy komisarza do spraw mieszkalnictwa. I wreszcie w Parlamencie Europejskim rozmawiamy o polityce mieszkaniowej i patrzymy na mieszkanie nie tylko przez pryzmat rynku. Ta regulacja jest pierwszym dobrym krokiem, ale ja czekam na kolejny, na budowę tanich mieszkań.

paragraphs.text: Pirmininke, komisare, būsto įperkamumas nėra vien ekonomikos ar socialinės politikos klausimas. Tai yra ir demografijos klausimas. Jaunos šeimos galimybę turėti nuosavą, tinkamo dydžio būstą įvardina kaip vieną svarbiausių veiksnių sprendžiant, kada kurti šeimą ir kiek vaikų turėti. Eurofound taip pat konstatuoja, kad būsto krizė Europoje atitolina jaunų žmonių savarankišką gyvenimą ir šeimos kūrimą. Tačiau kalbėdami apie būsto prieinamumą, turime sąžiningai įvertinti ir tai, kiek patys reguliavimu didiname naujo būsto kainą. Vienas pavyzdžių – vis griežtėjantys pastatų energetinio efektyvumo reikalavimai. Energijos taupymas yra svarbus tikslas, tačiau kiekvienas papildomas reikalavimas turi būti proporcingas. Jei jau efektyvaus pastato energijos sąnaudas sumažiname dar keliais procentais, bet dėl to reikšmingai padidiname statybos kainą, turime klausti, ar nauda pateisina kainą. Todėl siūlau, kad vertinant naujus reikalavimus būtų privalomai įvertinamas ir jų poveikis būsto įperkamumui.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, le proteste sulla casa sono il segno del fallimento della democrazia liberale, che aveva promesso prosperità e servizi pubblici per tutti e non ha mantenuto le promesse. La casa è il primo anello della catena di sicurezza per ognuno di noi. Se manca quella, ogni altro diritto diventa più fragile.

Piantiamola anche di prendere in giro i ragazzi, dicendo loro di investire sul futuro e di prepararsi, però senza dare loro le basi materiali per cominciare. Va inserita la valutazione di impatto generazionale in ogni provvedimento legislativo, anche a Bruxelles.

Ho sentito colate di ideologia da una parte e dall'altra. Ma qui non è questione di lotta di classe, qui è questione anche di lotta dentro le classi, perché i piccoli proprietari, che hanno due appartamenti e uno lo mettono ad affitto breve per guadagnare qualcosa, non possono essere equiparati alle grandi multinazionali che speculano a livello internazionale. Meno ideologie e più risposte concrete. Alla rabbia si risponde con soluzioni concrete: più offerta di case.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner, Minister, colleagues, Europe has finally recognised that housing is an emergency. It's a crisis. Our own country, our own citizens know this too. So now we need to act like it is. We've shown that where there is a political will, permitting can be accelerated. It's no surprise that for energy and defence projects, Europe has taken the necessary urgent action to cut red tape and shorten approval times. So why not for housing? A home that gets takes years to get through a planning permission system becomes unaffordable. It's also a home that may never, ever be built. We need to see the same urgency for housing: faster permitting, simpler planning rules, greater access to finance, and a construction capacity to actually deliver the homes that every one of us knows we need.

So, Commissioner, I am asking you to be bold. Bring forward the simplification package that was asked for by the EPP and the Housing Committee as soon as possible, set ambitious targets for reducing permitting times, and use every available tool in the European box to make sure that we actually build the millions of houses that we need so desperately for our cities.

paragraphs.text: Sur President, li jkollok dar mhijiex lussu, li jkollok dar hija bażi għal ħajja diċenti. Iżda, għal tul ta' żmien, is-suq tal-proprjetà ma kienx qed jaħdem favur il-familji tagħna.

F'Malta qed naraw kif iż-żieda fix-short lets wasslet għal żieda sostanzjali fil-prezzijiet u għamlitha diffiċli ħafna għal ħafna Maltin biex jaffordjaw id-djar tagħhom. U rridu nkunu ċari: mhux qed nitkellmu dwar familja li għandha kamra żejda u tiddeċiedi li tikriha. Qed nitkellmu dwar investituri kbar li jixtru proprjetajiet li qabel kienu djar tal-familji. Qed nitkellmu wkoll dwar kif pjattaformi bħall-Airbnb u Booking, għandhom jirrispettaw ir-regoli tal-pajjiżi li joperaw fih. L-awtoritajiet lokali għandhom jingħataw ir-riżorsi u l-appoġġ kollu meħtieġ biex ikunu jistgħu jinfurzaw ir-regoli, speċjalment meta jkunu qed jiddiljaw ma' kumpaniji globali tat-teknoloġija.

Biex insolvu din il-problema, irridu mmorru oltre mill-kritika. Irridu nżidu l-provvista u dan huwa eżattament dak li qed jagħmel Gvern Laburista f'Malta, fl-aħħar snin. Bnejna aktar akkomodazzjoni soċjali, żidna l-akkomodazzjoni affordabbli, għenna liż-żgħażagħ tagħna biex ikunu jistgħu jixtru d-djar tagħhom permezz tal- iskema tas-self soċjali u llum qed nagħmlu pass oltre, il-Gvern qed jinvesti wkoll f'xiri ta' proprjetajiet biex jgħin dawk li għandhom bżonn dar permezz tal-iskema tal-equity sharing.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, geschätzte Kollegen! Leistung muss sich wieder lohnen in Europa. Ich glaube, das ist ein Ansatz, den wir hier auch gerne mal verwenden könnten. Und wer arbeitet, muss sich eine Wohnung leisten können. Ich glaube, da sind wir uns alle d'accord hier im Haus. Und es gibt aber immer mehr Menschen, die sich das schlicht nicht leisten können. Und jetzt – und da werden wir schon sehr skeptisch – will Brüssel leistbares Wohnen zur Chefsache machen. Aber eine Wohnung wird nicht deshalb billiger, weil sich eine weitere Behörde darum kümmert. Mehr Wohnungen, schnellere Genehmigungen: Ja! Aber dafür brauchen wir weniger Vorschriften.

Und wir brauchen bezahlbare Energie. Denn wer sich die Energiepreise in Europa und die Benzinpreise anschaut, dem wird klar, dass den Menschen immer weniger Geld im Börsl bleibt. Und Wien ist nicht Graz. Und ein Tiroler Tourismusort ist keine kleine Landgemeinde. Man kann das nicht vergleichen. Was vor Ort gebraucht wird, das können noch immer die Menschen vor Ort am besten entscheiden. Und deshalb sage ich: Lasst die Gemeinden handeln und macht ihnen das Bauen nicht noch schwerer. Für uns heißt das, dass den Menschen am Monatsende mehr zum Leben bleiben muss. Weniger Bürokratie, weniger Kosten, mehr Wohnungen.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, davanti alla crisi abitativa, la scelta dovrebbe essere chiara: dobbiamo costruire più case, non imporre chi può utilizzare quelle che già esistono e chi no. Perché oggi l'Europa ha bisogno di case. La stessa Commissione europea stima che ne servono oltre 2 milioni in più ogni anno fino al 2035.

Eppure, discutiamo di restrizioni alla proprietà e agli affitti brevi, che rappresentano solo 1,2 % del patrimonio abitativo europeo. Siamo chiari: se il problema è la scarsità, la soluzione non può essere vietare. Una famiglia che affitta per qualche settimana la seconda casa in montagna non è un fondo speculativo, e vietare di farlo non crea magicamente un appartamento per uno studente o per una famiglia.

Le case si rendono accessibili costruendo, rigenerando, recuperando gli immobili vuoti e liberando l'offerta dalla burocrazia. Non si risolve la crisi abitativa facendo della proprietà privata il capro espiatorio. Più case, non più divieti. Più offerta, non meno libertà.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar! Ich bin sehr glücklich, dass wir uns über die Wohnungskrise in der Europäischen Union unterhalten, aber wir gehen in die komplett falsche Richtung. Wer möchte, dass mehr Wohnraum in der Europäischen Union existiert, der muss sich um das Bauen kümmern, nicht mehr Regulierung schaffen. Nur mehr gebauter Wohnraum schafft günstigere Wohnungen und ermöglicht jedem, sich letztendlich auch den Traum zu erfüllen, Wohnraum zu schaffen – vielleicht für die Altersvorsorge, weil der Staat auch da verzichtet –, eine Wohnung zu kaufen oder zu bauen, die er vermieten kann.

Das, was wir im letzten Mandat gemacht haben mit ESG und Taxonomie, hat genau dazu geführt, dass Wohnen teurer wurde. Schauen Sie sich doch mal die enorme Bürokratie an, die die Kommission durch ESG geschaffen hat, was das Bauen verteuert. Schauen Sie sich die enormen Zinsaufschläge an, die wir haben, weil in der Taxonomie gewisse Baustoffe letztendlich über andere bevorzugt werden. Das macht das Bauen teurer. Und wenn Sie wollen, dass mehr gebaut wird, dann hören Sie auf mit diesem Regulierungswahn und fangen Sie wieder an, allen Menschen, die das möchten, das Bauen möglich zu machen. Das geht nur durch mehr Wohnraum und nicht durch mehr Regeln.

paragraphs.text: Herr Präsident, Herr Kommissar, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Der sogenannte Affordable Housing Act, er ist nicht nur enttäuschend, er ist eine politische Nebelkerze. Wir haben ein Angebotsproblem. In Europa wird zu wenig gebaut. Und wer ein Angebotsproblem hat, der braucht Lösungen auf der Angebotsseite. Ihr Vorschlag setzt stattdessen auf Kurzzeitvermietungen und verlangt neue Berichte. Mangelverwaltung schafft keinen neuen Wohnraum. Keine einzige Wohnung entsteht durch Ihren Vorschlag.

Dabei haben wir Ihnen im Sonderausschuss zur Wohnraumkrise ja einen klaren Auftrag mitgegeben. Durchforsten Sie den gesamten europäischen Rechtskörper, streichen Sie, was Bauen verhindert. Legen Sie einen Housing-Omnibus vor, und zwar mit einem klaren Ziel: Genehmigungen straffen, Vorgaben pragmatisch fassen, Vergabeverfahren vereinfachen. Das wird jetzt benötigt. Wer will, dass gebaut wird, muss das Bauen erlauben. Herr Kommissar, Sie sind Kommissar für die Menschen in Europa, nicht nur für die spanischen Sozialisten.

paragraphs.text: Senhor Presidente, Senhor Comissário, a poucos deve ter escapado a ironia de estarmos a discutir a habitação acessível logo após recebermos aqui o primeiro‑ministro de Portugal que na semana passada fez aprovar legislação que liberaliza ainda mais o mercado de arrendamento, permite maiores aumentos de renda e facilita os despejos.

A falta de rendas ou a falta de regras já deixou as rendas incomportáveis. A solução não pode ser aumentar a dose do remédio que está a matar o paciente. Foi este caminho que levou a que professores, médicos, enfermeiros e a esmagadora maioria das pessoas não consiga hoje pagar uma casa.

Esta situação não é sustentável nem aceitável. Precisamos de um forte programa, Senhor Comissário, de construção de habitação pública, repito, construção de habitação pública, apoiada por fundos europeus, que coloque casas no mercado a preços acessíveis, para que todos tenham direito a uma vida digna e a construir uma família, sem viverem todos os meses com a angústia de não saberem se conseguirão pagar a renda. Que não nos falte a coragem e a determinação.

paragraphs.text: Signor Presidente, signor Commissario, dinanzi alle crescenti aspettative dei cittadini europei sulla casa, l'Unione europea deve offrire risposte chiare e concrete.

Il nuovo Housing Act, finora, è però lontano da questo obiettivo. Si concentra su un aspetto molto marginale, gli affitti brevi, proponendo modelli già sperimentati con esiti negativi. Per questo oggi vorrei richiamare tutti al buon senso. Ci sono persone che cercano un'abitazione, giovani e famiglie che faticano ad acquistarla e lavoratori che non riescono a sostenere un affitto adeguato.

La risposta deve quindi partire da qui. Costruire più case e recuperare gli edifici inutilizzati, mettendo a sistema patrimonio esistente e nuovi investimenti. Per questa ragione, la delegazione italiana del Partito popolare europeo chiede a lei, Commissario, di rivedere profondamente questa proposta, cercando di semplificare, rigenerando le nostre città e costruendo più case per i nostri cittadini europei.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues, a home is not a luxury nor a financial asset – a home is a right. Yet across Europe, people are losing that right. There are Maricarmens in all our Member States. A home was once affordable on an ordinary salary. But today, for too many people, this is an unreachable dream, because the market has failed us: 1.4 million people in Europe face homelessness, while too many sharks on the market consider houses and apartments not as a home, but as a financial product to only generate profit.

The Affordable Housing Act – a good first step – gives us an opportunity to deliver change by regulating short‑term rentals. But we also need stronger tenants' rights, rent capping, better protection against illegal evictions, and greater investment in social and affordable housing. We must take tackle speculation and harmful tax rules.

Citizens are calling on us to act. We need the courage to put people before profit and make decent, affordable housing a reality for all Europeans. Member States, regions and municipalities must not shy away from their responsibilities.

Ma loomulikult tervitan komisjoni algatust tegeleda Euroopa eluasemekriisiga, sest see probleem puudutab kõige haavatavamaid, aga ka keskklassi ja noori. Samas ei saa Euroopa eluasemepoliitikat kirjutada ühe mõõdupuu järgi. Tallinnas, Madridis ja Pariisis ei ole samad probleemid ning veel vähem on sama olukord suurlinnades ja väiksemates maapiirkondades. Eesti maapiirkondades on küsimus selles, kuidas hoida noori inimesi kohapeal ning kuidas tekiks piisavalt nõudlust uute eluasemete ehitamiseks. Samas pealinnas Tallinnas on mure sageli vastupidine. Uusi kortereid on, kuid hinnad on nii kõrged, et noortel peredel on raske koguda vajalikku sissemakset, kuigi nende sissetulek võimaldaks igakuist laenumakset tasuda. Uusi kortereid on, kuid hinnad on nii kõrged, et noortel peredel on raske koguda vajalikku sissemakset, kuigi nende sissetulek võimaldaks igakuist laenumakset tasuda. Suur osa sissetulekust kulub aga üürile ja see võtab palju aastaid aega, et sellist summat koguda. Arvan, et siin saavad liikmesriigid rohkem appi tulla käenduste ja garantiidega.

paragraphs.text: Herr talman! Kommissionären. Unga kan i dag inte flytta hemifrån. Barnfamiljer trängs och vanliga löntagare har inte råd att bo där jobben finns. Det senare gör det dessutom svårare både för företag och offentlig sektor att rekrytera den personal man behöver. En fungerande bostadsmarknad är därför inte bara en social fråga utan också en förutsättning för jobb och tillväxt.

Och det är riktigt att EU inte kan bygga lägenheter i Stockholm, i Skellefteå eller Borlänge. Det är riktigt att korttidsuthyrning har andra effekter i Barcelona än Avesta, men EU kan och måste hjälpa till att riva de hinder som står i vägen för regioner, städer och medlemsländer att bedriva en aktiv bostadspolitik.

I Sverige har högerregeringen testat att lämna bostadsbyggandet till marknaden, och efter fyra år har vi resultatet: Antalet byggstarter har halverats. Det är inte värdigt. Det är ett svek mot alla dem som saknar en bostad, det är ett svek mot alla dem som arbetar med att bygga våra bostäder. Politiken behöver ta ett ansvar på alla nivåer.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario, este pretendía ser un primer paso en la dirección correcta, pero es solo una decepción. La primera y única propuesta legislativa presentada se centra en regular y en intervenir en el mercado, y abre incluso la puerta a limitar la compra de segundas residencias, medidas que encajan difícilmente con los pilares fundamentales del proyecto europeo y que además, a estas alturas, deberían saberse ineficaces y enormemente contraproducentes.

Mire, por desgracia mi país es el mayor laboratorio de este tipo de políticas de toda la Unión Europea. El Gobierno de Sánchez lleva ocho años a la vanguardia y le voy a dar algunos datos: los precios de la vivienda han aumentado un 74 % y, los alquileres, un 45 %. Sus políticas han expulsado a una de cada tres viviendas del mercado. La edad de emancipación de los jóvenes supera los treinta años. Se ha generado un déficit de 750 000 viviendas y la vivienda ha pasado de ser el problema dieciséis a ser el primero de los ciudadanos. No parece el mejor espejo en el que mirarse. El impulso a este tipo de medidas solo puede responder a prejuicios ideológicos o intereses políticos y electorales.

Señor comisario, céntrense en lo importante, en lo necesario, en lo que les sugirió este Parlamento. Necesitamos movilizar suelo, acelerar las licencias, reducir impuestos, impulsar la innovación y la industrialización, atraer inversiones tanto públicas como privadas y garantizar la seguridad jurídica. Esos deben ser los principales objetivos.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Úr! Senki nem akar 30 évesen koleszos életet élni. Egyszerűen kinövünk belőle. És mégis: ma Magyarországon – és Európában is – a fiatalok egyre gyakrabban kénytelenek egy szobában lakni, mert nem bírják megfizetni a bérleti díjakat, lakásra meg esélyük sincsen.

És hogy miért van ez így? Mert amit ma Európában és Magyarországon ingatlanpiacnak nevezünk, az egy szabadrabláson alapuló, teljesen torz rendszer, ahol milliárdos ingatlanbefektetők gazdagodnak meg, miközben milliók számára kilátástalanná válik az, hogy saját lakáshoz jussanak.

A piacon kellene versenyezniük ezekkel a milliárdos ingatlanbefektetőkkel, spekulánsokkal, akiknek a lakás nem otthon, hanem egy befektetés, amiből meg akarnak gazdagodni. Na, ennek kell Európában véget vetni. Igenis meg kell adóztatni keményen a lakásspekulációt, bérlakásokat kell építeni az önkormányzatok bevonásával. És ha azt mondjuk, a lakhatás alapjog, akkor tegyük hozzá: nem alapjog meggazdagodni mások nyomorán.

paragraphs.text: (Beginn des Redebeitrags bei ausgeschaltetem Mikrofon) ... mir als deutsche Staatsbürgerin eine Vorbemerkung. In unserem Grundgesetz, unserer Verfassung, steht: Eigentum verpflichtet. Sein Gebrauch soll zugleich dem Wohle der Allgemeinheit dienen. Für manche ist es schon Kommunismus oder andere, die reden von Freiheit und meinen aber Rechtlosigkeit. Und wir wissen aus jedem Western, wem Rechtlosigkeit dient. Ich will die Debatte noch einmal zurückholen.

Wir stehen hier, um über diesen Vorschlag zur Kurzzeitvermietung zu diskutieren, weil die Bürgermeister und Bürgermeisterinnen, Linke, Konservative, Liberale, Grüne die Kommission gebeten haben, gesagt haben: Wir brauchen mehr Rechtssicherheit, sonst müssen wir Vertragsverletzungsverfahren fürchten. Und genau dazu dient dieser Vorschlag. Er war nie gemeint, alle Probleme zu lösen. Oder wenn man hier so tut: Wasch mir den Pelz, aber mach mich nicht nass. Wir können nicht diesen konkreten Schritt für die Menschen tun, weil wir eigentlich noch viel größere Schritte gehen müssen. So funktioniert das nicht und das ist auch nicht verantwortlich. Mir kam das eben hier ein bisschen vor manchmal wie eine Zombie-Debatte.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, señor comisario Jørgensen, es evidente, después de un debate tan intenso, que la Ley europea de Vivienda Asequible es profundamente ideológica y marca una línea divisiva entre quienes creen que es un derecho y parte de una aspiración a una vida digna y quienes creen que es sencillamente un bien de mercado sujeto a toda especulación.

Pero entre quienes creen que es un derecho, el Estado es insurreccional. Particularmente cuando, como en España, la distribución de competencias permite a comunidades autónomas, regiones y municipios gobernados por la derecha obstruir cualquier esfuerzo por parte del Gobierno progresista de resolver lo que es esa aspiración.

Pero hay una huelga general en ciernes que no es contra el Gobierno, sino contra la especulación. Y hay algo que la Unión Europea puede hacer contra la especulación de los fondos de inversión —que en España se llaman fondos buitre— y solo la Unión Europea puede hacerlo: introducir medidas de restricción a la libre circulación de capitales para impedir que los fondos de inversión puedan acaparar vivienda encareciendo exponencialmente su precio y expulsando del mercado a la clase trabajadora y a la juventud que aspira.

paragraphs.text: Arvoisa puhemies, Suomen Maaninka ei ole sama kuin Espanjan Marbella. EU-tasolla on tästä huolimatta raivoisa hinku ratkaista joidenkin maiden asuntopulat EU-tason toimilla ja rahoituksella. Suomessa moni pitäjä on ollut muuttotappiokunta jo vuosikymmeniä. Vastaavasti suuret kaupungit ovat vetäneet väestöä magneetin lailla ja asuntojen hinnat ovat nousseet. Tämä suunta on ymmärretty, emmekä ole kaivanneet mitään EU:n asuntovaliokuntia tätä pulmaa ratkomaan. Kansallisvaltiot ratkovat kansalliset ongelmansa omin keinoin.

On täysin mahdollista rakentaa lisää asuntoja ilman EU-tason tukea – uskokaa tai älkää. Suomalaisten asumis- ja rakentamiskulut ovat jo muutenkin kalliita – pakkanen puraisee ja se tekee loven myös suomalaisten lompakkoon. Siihen lompakkoon ei tarvita enää yhtään uutta EU:n puraisemaa lovea.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, κύριε Επίτροπε, η στέγαση αποτελεί θεμελιώδες κοινωνικό δικαίωμα και βασική προϋπόθεση για αξιοπρεπή ζωή, όχι κερδοσκοπικό περιουσιακό στοιχείο ή προνόμιο για λίγους.

Η πράξη για την οικονομική προσιτή στέγαση αποτελεί ένα πρώτο βήμα, αλλά δεν αρκεί. Δεν μπορείτε να ζητάτε από τις τοπικές αρχές να περιμένουν τρία χρόνια πριν παρέμβουν για να αποδείξουν ότι η κρίση έχει ήδη καταστρέψει την αγορά κατοικίας. Ούτε να μετράτε τη στεγαστική πίεση με γενικούς δείκτες που συχνά κρύβουν την πραγματικότητα μικρών νησιών και τουριστικών περιοχών.

Αυτή η κρίση, για να αντιμετωπιστεί, χρειάζεται ευρωπαϊκή χρηματοδότηση, δεσμευτικά μέτρα, πραγματικά εργαλεία για τους δήμους, νομική ασφάλεια, πρόσβαση στα δεδομένα των πλατφορμών. Απαιτείται μόνιμη αύξηση της δημόσιας και κοινωνικής κατοικίας, ένα ευρωπαϊκό πρόγραμμα κατασκευής και ανακαίνισης προσιτών κατοικιών, προστασία της πρώτης κατοικίας, προστασία από εξώσεις και πλειστηριασμούς, και απαιτούνται αποτελεσματικοί μηχανισμοί ρύθμισης των ενοικίων.

paragraphs.text: Κύριε Πρόεδρε, εκατοντάδες χιλιάδες οικογένειες χάνουν τα σπίτια τους. Δίνεται μάχη με διαδηλώσεις και διαμαρτυρίες στην Ισπανία, την Ελλάδα, και η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση ρίχνει κι άλλο λάδι στη φωτιά. Με αυτόν τον κανονισμό, προωθώντας την πολιτική κατοικία-εμπόρευμα, χρηματοδοτείτε επενδύσεις και τα κέρδη των κατασκευαστικών ομίλων με συμπράξεις δημοσίου-ιδιωτικού τομέα και κρατικά ευρωενωσιακά κεφάλαια στο όνομα της ενίσχυσης της προσφοράς.

Αυτή η πολιτική διαιωνίζει την πανάκριβη κατοικία, τη βραχυχρόνια μίσθωση, την εξάρτηση από τον τραπεζικό δανεισμό. Προετοιμάζει τον επόμενο γύρο πλειστηριασμών, παραδίδοντας τα σπίτια του λαού στα κοράκια funds και τραπεζών. Αυτή η πολιτική αύξησε τις τιμές κατοικιών και ενοικίων κατά 61 % σε δέκα χρόνια, όπως και οι πράσινες προδιαγραφές της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης που ανεβάζουν τις τιμές των οικοδομικών υλικών.

Η στέγη είναι κοινωνικό αγαθό, όχι εμπόρευμα, όπως τη θέλουν η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, αστικά κόμματα και κυβερνήσεις. Διεκδικούμε αποκλειστικά κρατικό σχεδιασμό και κατασκευαστικό πρόγραμμα, επανασύσταση του Οργανισμού Εργατικής Κατοικίας, απαγόρευση πλειστηριασμών λαϊκών κατοικιών, αξιοποίηση κενών κατοικιών και ξενοδοχείων για δωρεάν στέγαση των φοιτητών. Μόνο ο λαός σώζει τα σπίτια του λαού.

Κύριε Πρόεδρε, εκατοντάδες χιλιάδες οικογένειες χάνουν τα σπίτια τους. Δίνεται μάχη με διαδηλώσεις και διαμαρτυρίες στην Ισπανία, την Ελλάδα, και η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση ρίχνει κι άλλο λάδι στη φωτιά. Με αυτόν τον κανονισμό, προωθώντας την πολιτική κατοικία-εμπόρευμα, χρηματοδοτείτε επενδύσεις και τα κέρδη των κατασκευαστικών ομίλων με συμπράξεις δημοσίου-ιδιωτικού τομέα και κρατικά ευρωενωσιακά κεφάλαια στο όνομα της ενίσχυσης της προσφοράς.

Αυτή η πολιτική διαιωνίζει την πανάκριβη κατοικία, τη βραχυχρόνια μίσθωση, την εξάρτηση από τον τραπεζικό δανεισμό. Προετοιμάζει τον επόμενο γύρο πλειστηριασμών, παραδίδοντας τα σπίτια του λαού στα κοράκια funds και τραπεζών. Αυτή η πολιτική αύξησε τις τιμές κατοικιών και ενοικίων κατά 61 % σε δέκα χρόνια, όπως και οι πράσινες προδιαγραφές της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης που ανεβάζουν τις τιμές των οικοδομικών υλικών.

Η στέγη είναι κοινωνικό αγαθό, όχι εμπόρευμα, όπως τη θέλουν η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, αστικά κόμματα και κυβερνήσεις. Διεκδικούμε αποκλειστικά κρατικό σχεδιασμό και κατασκευαστικό πρόγραμμα, επανασύσταση του Οργανισμού Εργατικής Κατοικίας, απαγόρευση πλειστηριασμών λαϊκών κατοικιών, αξιοποίηση κενών κατοικιών και ξενοδοχείων για δωρεάν στέγαση των φοιτητών. Μόνο ο λαός σώζει τα σπίτια του λαού.

paragraphs.text: Señor presidente, la vivienda es la mayor fractura social de nuestro tiempo y, como siempre en política, se trata de elegir.

Con esta Ley, Europa se encuentra ante una disyuntiva: elegir entre la impunidad de los fondos buitre o la tranquilidad de las familias, elegir entre la especulación salvaje que expulsa a los jóvenes o el derecho innegociable a un techo.

Se acabó el tiempo de mirar hacia otro lado, hay que poner freno a esta sangría, también desde aquí, también desde la Unión Europea y también asignando fondos de la política de cohesión que sirvan para construir viviendas públicas que equilibren el mercado, para invertir como nunca se ha hecho desde lo público, para recuperar nuestro parque público de vivienda y para proteger a quien lo necesita. Toca elegir entre el negocio de unos pocos o una vida digna para la mayoría.
La vivienda es un derecho y garantizarlo es nuestra responsabilidad.

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, Maricarmen est devenue le symbole de la situation dramatique du logement dans l'Union européenne: une femme de 87 ans expulsée de force de chez elle à la demande d'un fonds d'investissement.

La Commission européenne nous propose aujourd'hui un règlement sur le logement abordable pour lutter contre les locations de courte durée et pour un guichet unique pour accéder aux financements européens. C'est bienvenu, mais vous le savez, Monsieur le Commissaire, il faudra bien d'autres leviers d'action pour réussir à faire face à la crise du logement.

D'abord, il faut des outils pour les États membres et pour les collectivités locales, pour plafonner les loyers dans les zones tendues. Ensuite, il faut des outils pour réquisitionner les logements vacants. Et enfin, il faudra, un jour ou l'autre, créer un fonds européen pour le logement abordable et durable, comme l'est aujourd'hui le Fonds social européen. Sans cela, il n'y aura pas de réponse durable au logement et il y aura d'autres Maricarmen qui seront expulsées par des fonds spéculatifs.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, thank you all for a very good debate. So, although there has been obviously differences of opinions, there has also been a lot of common ground. We seem to agree, most of us, that we do have a housing crisis in Europe and we do need to act.

Now, some of you argue that we are not doing enough. Others argue that we are going too far. To those who think we are not doing enough, I can say I agree and we will do more, but this is an important first step and it will help us solve some of the challenges that we are facing. Short‑term rentals are an increasing problem. It is driving people out of their homes. It is leading to an increase in prices. Same goes for vacant homes. It is in many cities a real challenge, a real problem, and now we give the opportunity to do something about it.

To those who think we are going too far, I have two messages. One is: I doubt your populations and your voters agree with you on that. It is very, very clear that all over Europe our citizens are demanding action. They are seeing how firefighters, teachers, nurses, people with ordinary, normal jobs can no longer live where they serve. This is totally unacceptable and we need to act.

My second answer is: remember, this is a proposal that gives cities, regions, Member States opportunities. We respect to subsidiarity principle. We do not force cities to do something that they do not want to do, but we provide legal certainty. We provide a path, a toolbox, ways to deal with some of these problems.
I look forward to keep discussing this with you and to making this into real legislation that can then hopefully help our citizens and help alleviate the crisis that we are in.

interventions.speaker_label: Roxana Mînzatu, Executive Vice-President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, honourable Members, the European School Alliances are an important pillar of the education package that we are working on and that we will present early November this year.

Towards that objective, I want to thank this House for the very strong interest it has taken on the European Partnerships for School Development, which is really a step towards the work that we are preparing to deliver to our pupils and our teachers across the European Union.

A lot has happened since my colleague, Commissioner Hansen, delivered a statement here on behalf of the European Commission in March 2025, so last year, on European Schools Alliances. Let me just briefly say that yes, we are quite motivated because meanwhile we have seen the PISA 2025 results. We have performed an analysis in the Commission on these results. I say this very often – most of us know it – around one in three of our teenagers, 15-year-olds, is underachieving, so they do not have the basic proficiency in reading and in mathematics. One in four is underperforming in science.

At the same time, when we look at the top performers, this number is also falling in Europe. Now we are seeing this trend with our pupils for the past decade already in Europe. So that tells us that it is not by accident and that we really need to act to reverse this trend.

The CULT Committee in the European Parliament proposed the draft motion on the agenda today to put a strong emphasis on citizenship education and European values. This also underlines the importance of democratic participation, the importance of critical thinking, of resilience to disinformation, and all this from an early age. Citizenship education is what I've always said is one of the five basic skills. With that in mind, I very much welcome this motion.

Earlier this year, we launched the European Partnerships for School Development and the call to support these partnerships with a budget of around EUR 20 million in the first Erasmus+ call for this topic. We already fund 40 projects across almost all EU Member States, which include nearly 400 school authorities and schools. These projects actually have just started their activity on 1 October.

I would give just three examples of these European Partnerships for School Development that we already support. The Hungarian-Estonian Dignity project is making digital learning environments safer and more respectful and teaching young people how to use AI responsibly. This is such a relevant topic nowadays, as we discuss social media and the mental well-being of our children.
The French-German project called Math Link is improving how mathematics is being taught through shared resources and through better support for vulnerable pupils.

The third example that I would give is a Romanian-Greek-Turkish project called EZIT maybe making inclusive teacher teaching of literacy and mathematics practical and scalable through mentoring, through in-house training and through better monitoring.

These projects, as I've said, have just started. What we learn from their implementation will of course inform the preparation of the European Schools Alliances tool, which we will launch with the 2028 Erasmus+ working programme and then, of course, plan to scale up.

The reality is that too many young people in Europe are falling behind in literacy, in mathematics, in science, in digital skills and AI, and in citizenship skills. The alliances are meant to help schools across Europe tackle this underachievement.

They will focus on the most important and, of course, the most urgent gaps and help us scale up what works best across our education systems. That is how I think we efficiently prepare our young people for the age of artificial intelligence everywhere – in our societies, our lives, our economies – for the jobs of not just today, but of tomorrow.

To do this, we need school authorities, and this is an important aspect. School authorities who know the school's challenges best, who work together with school leaders, with teachers, with experts across Europe. Together, they can develop and put into practice concrete actions so that they improve the learning processes in schools.

I want to close with this. The alliances will be built and scaled up with four important principles in mind. First – and this is very important – they must reach pupils and teachers in disadvantaged areas. Second, they must have a geographical balance across our European Union. Third, they must generate a lasting change, a systemic change and improvement in the learning processes. Erasmus is amazing, but we need to capitalise on these experiences and produce a durable change in the learning processes. Fourth, of course, we want simple, agile, easy-to-implement projects, so no administrative burden on schools and on teachers because they already have their work cut out for them.
I thank you and I really look forward to your contributions to this important debate.

paragraphs.text: Mr President, Commissioner and dear colleagues, European competitiveness begins long before people enter the labour market. It begins at school. Today, 46 % of European small and medium-sized enterprises struggle to find workers with the right skills. More than half of EU companies see this shortage as an obstacle to investment. We cannot allow a skills shortage to hold back European growth. This is where European school alliances can turn a European problem into a concrete European solution.

The proposal is to connect schools from different countries through structured networks, enabling teachers to work together, students to benefit from learning that is more open to Europe, and the best teaching practices to be shared and replicated across borders. This is not just about mobility. It is about improving the quality of education and better preparing our young people by giving them strong foundations, digital skills and critical thinking abilities.

Schools in rural, remote or peripheral regions should be able to join the European network and give their students access to experiences and opportunities that are not always within their reach. But we want alliances that are demanding when it comes to results – not bureaucracy – with simple rules and clear criteria for measuring participation and learning outcomes. Vocational education and training (VET) must also be part of this effort. This is how we improve education without leaving anyone behind. If we want more competitive companies tomorrow, we need more connected schools today.

interventions.speaker_label: Sabrina Repp, im Namen der S&D-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Wenn wir über Erasmus+ sprechen, dann denken viele zunächst an Studierende im Ausland. Aber warum sollte Europa eigentlich erst an der Universität beginnen? Ich erinnere mich noch gut an meine Schulzeit. Wir sollten an einem Austausch mit Jugendlichen aus Lettland teilnehmen. Eigentlich wollte ich mitmachen, aber sofort hatte ich Hunderte Zweifel im Kopf. Wo soll die Austauschschülerin bei uns schlafen, weil unsere Wohnung so klein ist? Wie soll sie mit meinen Eltern kommunizieren, die kein Englisch sprechen können? Und können meine Eltern sich später überhaupt den Flug leisten, wenn ich sie besuchen soll?

Genau solche Fragen dürfen nicht darüber entscheiden, wer Europa erleben kann. Deshalb müssen die europäischen Schulallianzen von Anfang an so gestaltet werden, dass wirklich alle teilnehmen können. Schulen brauchen Unterstützung. Familien dürfen nicht auf zusätzlichen Kosten sitzen bleiben. Ob Förderschule, regionale Schule, Berufsschule, Gymnasien, Schulen im ländlichen Raum oder in der Stadt – alle müssen erreicht werden.
Denn Europa darf nicht vom Wohnort oder vom Geldbeutel abhängen. Wer Europa schon jung erlebt, für den bleibt Europa nicht abstrakt. Es bekommt Gesichter, Geschichten und Freundschaften.

interventions.speaker_label: Catherine Griset, au nom du groupe PfE.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, en France, l'alliance toxique des extrêmes mélenchonistes et macronistes a mis l'enseignement à terre. Et vous osez aujourd'hui nous parler d'alliances scolaires européennes et d'éducation à la citoyenneté. Favoriser les échanges entre jeunes Européens, leur permettre de découvrir d'autres langues et d'autres cultures: nous sommes pour. Mais avant de vouloir fabriquer une citoyenneté européenne, commençons par assurer la première mission de l'école: instruire nos enfants.

Après des années de réformes, le niveau scolaire français s'effondre. Et pendant ce temps, des lycées sont saccagés, des enseignants et des élèves blessés, des policiers et des pompiers attaqués. Plus grave encore: certains élus de La France insoumise préfèrent attiser les tensions plutôt que de les condamner, poussant les jeunes à s'exposer aux affrontements et à basculer eux-mêmes dans la violence. Alors oui, «tu casses, tu paies», car l'éducation à la citoyenneté commence par des choses simples: respecter son professeur, respecter son école, respecter les autres et respecter la loi.

L'Europe peut favoriser les échanges entre nos écoles; elle n'a pas à fabriquer une identité européenne destinée à se substituer à nos identités nationales. Nos priorités sont claires: transmettre, relever le niveau, rétablir l'autorité et garantir la sécurité. Voilà du concret.

interventions.speaker_label: Lara Magoni, a nome del gruppo ECR.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, oggi un giovane europeo vive in un mondo sempre più connesso e, allo stesso tempo, può arrivare a quindici anni senza possedere pienamente le competenze fondamentali per comprenderlo. Uno su tre fatica con la matematica, uno su quattro con la lettura. Questa è la vera sfida da affrontare.

Le alleanze delle scuole europee possono essere parte della risposta se servono per uno scopo concreto: far circolare ciò che funziona. Una buona pratica nata in una scuola italiana può aiutare una scuola polacca. Un metodo sviluppato in Finlandia può essere utile a un insegnante portoghese.

Questo è il valore dell'Europa: condividere esperienze, non imporre modelli. Cooperare non significa uniformare. Non abbiamo bisogno di un modello educativo unico o di nuova burocrazia decisa a Bruxelles, ma di scuole capaci di un sostegno concreto agli insegnanti per accompagnare i giovani europei.
Se l'Europa saprà sostenere questo obiettivo, queste alleanze potranno davvero fare la differenza. Più cooperazione, non più uniformità. Più competenze, non più burocrazia.

interventions.speaker_label: Христо Петров, от името на групата Renew.

paragraphs.text: Г-жо Председател, как едно дете да усети какво е Европа? Европейският съюз се усеща, когато едно дете от Пазарджик влезе в класна стая в Испания, когато ученик от Гоце Делчев работи по общ проект с дете от Франция, Полша или Италия, когато учител от Видин заедно с неговия колега от някой германски град не просто четат за добри практики, а работят заедно.

Всяка държава сама определя учебната си програма, но училищата могат да си партнират на база това, в което са най-добри и успешни. Това е идеята на европейските училищни алианси. Всички ние, които се занимаваме с този проект, знаем, че той вече работи повече от успешно на ниво университети, и беше крайно време да го разширим и към училищата. С моя екип работим по тази тема вече две години, преговаряхме, пишехме, спорихме, правихме компромиси, но с някои неща не направихме компромис. Това няма да бъде програма само за големите градове и големите училища. Тя ще бъде достъпна за селата, пограничните райони, професионалните гимназии и спортните училища и училищата по изкуствата, и няма да има бюрокрация.
Аз вярвам, че с European Schools Alliance ние правим една много важна стъпка. Европа ще стане нещо, което много повече деца ще могат да усетят, а не просто да учат за него.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, every morning, across Europe, us parents drop off our kids at school with the same hope: that they will grow up safe, curious and ready for the world. But right now, from Rome to Saxony-Anhalt, far‑right governments – also aided by the conservatives – are trying to turn our classrooms into battlegrounds.

Pushing laws that sort children by their background, they want to teach our kids to look at their neighbours with suspicion. It is a direct attack on our freedom. Schools should be where we learn to coexist, not where we learn to divide.

That is why initiatives like the European School Alliances matter. They bring together students from every background to learn democracy and also respect. As a teacher, I know our duty is to help all kids to thrive, no matter how they look, who they pray to, or where they come from.
Let's learn from our children welcoming anyone onto the playground to build a future where we all belong.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, in Francia studenti e insegnanti stanno protestando per chiedere più risorse, classi meno affollate, edifici scolastici dignitosi e personale sufficiente.

Non è un caso isolato. Mobilitazioni in difesa della scuola pubblica hanno attraversato anche Italia, Spagna e Belgio. In Germania decine di migliaia di studenti sono scesi in piazza contro la possibile reintroduzione della leva obbligatoria e contro la militarizzazione. Proteste diverse, stesso messaggio. I giovani vogliono essere ascoltati sul futuro che stiamo noi costruendo.

Le scelte di bilancio dicono quale Europa vogliamo. Se per il riarmo avete trovato flessibilità e centinaia di miliardi, nessuno venga a dirci che non ci sono risorse per scuole e giovani. La sicurezza dell'Europa non si costruisce solo con le armi, ma anche con cittadini liberi, consapevoli e capaci di pensiero critico.

Le European School Alliances possono essere uno strumento importante, ma devono ridurre le disuguaglianze, non replicarle. Le opportunità non devono finire, ancora una volta, a chi parte avvantaggiato. Noi ci battiamo per una scuola pubblica forte, capace di dare a ogni giovane le stesse opportunità. È da qui, e non dalle armi, che comincia una democrazia più forte.

interventions.speaker_label: Marc Jongen, im Namen der ESN-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Meine Damen und Herren, Frau Kommissarin! Szenen wie aus dem Bürgerkrieg in Frankreich, vermummte Jugendbanden marodieren unter dem Vorwand von Schülerprotesten auf den Straßen. Das ist die Rechnung für Massenmigration und gescheiterte Integration. Und was macht die Kommission? Sie nutzen auch diese selbst mitverantwortete Krise für noch mehr Zentralisierung, diesmal über Schulallianzen.

Aber die EU-Verträge sind klar, über Bildung entscheiden die Mitgliedstaaten. Und darum, Frau Riehl, sie ist ja nicht mehr hier, wenn Sie mit dem CULT-Ausschuss noch weitergehen und demokratische Resilienz und EU-Werte als Pflichtstoff an europäischen Schulen verordnen wollen, dann widersprechen Sie offen dem Subsidiaritätsprinzip. Wir brauchen sicher keine EU-Propaganda für unsere Demokratie in den Klassenzimmern. Das ist gegen die Freiheit gerichtet. Schulen sollen Wissen vermitteln: lesen, rechnen, Naturwissenschaften, Technik. Die Pisa-Ergebnisse zeigen, woran es fehlt. Dazu das antike und christliche Erbe Europas. Darauf zielen unsere Änderungsanträge. Im Übrigen gibt es Schulpartnerschaften längst über Erasmus+. Der geplante Ausbau bedeutet nicht zuletzt neue Bürokratie und neue Kosten. Bildung gehört den Familien und den Nationen. Sie soll von Brüsseler Vorgaben frei bleiben.

interventions.speaker_label: Roxana Mînzatu, Executive Vice-President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, thank you for your contributions.

I have met many teachers and many students whose life is not easy in the teaching profession, in the material conditions that they were facing every day, for whom the experience of Erasmus, whether it was some mobility, whether it was just cooperation, some co-creation with some partners from across the Union, was the biggest motivation to continue to teach, to improve or to learn. The Schools Alliances capitalises on this immense motivation that Erasmus has already brought in our schools, in our universities, in our vocational schools, but only to some, that is true.

The Schools Alliances obviously are never meant and could never be a tool of centralisation or of harmonisation, because what is being taught is a decision of the Member States. But how to share experiences, tools, methods so that mathematics or reading or science or a citizenship skill in a world of AI, of social media, of disinformation, how to improve these methods can be the result of a very good exchange between European partners.

Here I must say, it is obviously not the intention of the Commission that these School Alliances are elitist. As I have mentioned, one of the four conditions is that they are inclusive, that they include schools, pupils, teachers from disadvantaged backgrounds. But at the same time, I will not be able to say that schools from big cities will be excluded out of this tool. Of course, we are building this model of cooperation and this is towards, as I said, the education package in November. But do remember the focus that we want to put: to equip our pupils and to help our teachers to focus on the basic skills. This is the basic element of the direction that we see for the Schools Alliances. The alliance is not just mobility, not just partnership exchange. Yes, it's a very nice cooperation project in the European Union but teachers will have to choose one basic skill and focus on how to improve it. In this world, we need more than ever to equip our young generation with these basic foundations so that they can be relevant in democracies, in the labour market, wherever you may wish, in an age where they compete with technology or they see so much transformation because of technology. This is the intention of the Schools Alliances.

Obviously, I thank you for the contribution. I think also, for the young generation here or that that are listening and watching us, that they will be very interested to see how we deliver with this new tool. And I'm very confident that it will deliver for our pupils and our students all over the European Union.

paragraphs.text: L'ordine del giorno reca il tempo delle interrogazioni alla Commissione sull'attuazione del regolamento sul metano.
Do il benvenuto al Commissario Jørgensen per questo tempo delle interrogazioni.
Il tempo delle interrogazioni verte sul tema: Attuazione del regolamento sul metano.
La durata prevista è di circa 60 minuti.
I deputati avranno a disposizione un minuto per formulare un'interrogazione e due minuti per la risposta.
Per il primo turno di oratori sarà possibile porre una interrogazione supplementare di 30 secondi con due minuti per la risposta.
Vi ricordo che l'eventuale interrogazione supplementare è concessa soltanto se è strettamente correlata all'interrogazione principale e non consiste in una nuova interrogazione.

Chi intende dunque partecipare al dibattito è invitato a registrare fin d'ora la sua richiesta utilizzando la funzione "catch-the-eye" sul dispositivo di voto, dopo aver inserito ovviamente la tessera.

Durante il tempo delle interrogazioni, i deputati interverranno dal proprio scranno. Invito tutti gli oratori a rispettare il tempo di parola assegnato. Sarò costretta a essere abbastanza rigida perché siamo purtroppo in ritardo.
I deputati potrebbero aver bisogno di alcuni minuti per registrare la richiesta. Quindi vi chiedo di farlo al più presto. Iniziamo subito con i primi oratori che ne hanno fatto richiesta.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, Herr Kommissar Jørgensen! Die Methan-Verordnung ist wieder einmal ein typisches Beispiel der vergangenen Legislatur: Gut gemeint, aber mit massiven Auswirkungen auf Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und Energiesicherheit.

Ganz knapp zusammengefasst kann man sagen: Die Voraussetzungen für die gleichwertige Messung und Vermeidung von Methan sind in vielen Ländern, aus denen wir Öl und Gas beziehen, schlicht ab 2027 nicht vorhanden. Stabile Lieferverträge können Unternehmen so nicht rechtssicher aufbauen, weil sie sonst wissentlich gegen die Methan-Verordnung verstoßen.

Wenn wir also über niedrigere Preise sprechen, auch wenn wir die Importe reduzieren wollen, dann wäre unser Vorschlag – ob wir Ihren Proposal prinzipiell unterstützen –, dass wir das schlicht und einfach über Artikel 122 der EU-Verträge über die Notfallmaßnahmen hinaus nicht einfach nur um ein Jahr verlängern, sondern gleich bis 2030 verlängern. Sonst sitzen wir schlicht und einfach nächstes Jahr wieder hier.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Dan Jørgensen, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Mr Ehler and the others who have raised these questions, I look forward to this debate because the Methane Regulation and the implementation of it is indeed a very timely topic. On one hand, we are extremely proud of our regulation in Europe. It makes us frontrunners in the fight against methane emissions. Methane emissions, as you know, are very serious pollutants with regards to climate change and we are setting the standard globally, not only by reducing our own emissions but also by affecting others around the planet.

On the other hand, it is also clear that many Member States have experienced serious challenges in implementing the legislation, especially with regards to the part that has to do with imports. That, of course, also then relates to the ability of the different actors out there on the global markets that are exporting their products to us.

So we have listened. I have listened to that input, and that is why I have decided to ask my services to look into the possibility of postponing the different rules that relate to the import part of this regulation, so as to make sure that Member States and the different relevant actors are indeed able to implement. I would also like to underline that we do not foresee this to be more than one year. On the contrary, I would say that now the obligation is on Member States to make sure that they are ready in one year.

paragraphs.text: Commissioner, I mean, that is well intended, but it is totally unrealistic because you put the burden on the shoulders of Member States. But what you say to Algeria, what you say to the exporters, it is a matter of investments of a certain dimension, it is a matter of time to install that technically.

And we are going to sit here next year, so to pretend it is the Member State to solve that within a year is absolutely unrealistic because we talk about other parts of the world. That will take time and it would be more realistic to say we go until 2030 and we are not going to sit here next year again pretending it is the problem of the Member States.

political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Dan Jørgensen, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: I totally agree with you that this is obviously an issue that also has to be dealt with in the different countries that are right now exporting oil and gas products to us in a way that is not yet in line with this legislation. Fortunately, many of the third countries – so outside of EU countries – that are to fulfil these criteria are doing a lot of progress, and until recently we also thought it was possible for them to fulfil these criteria before 1 January. I think personally that most of them will still be able to do this. Looking at the gas, for instance, a lot of new contracts have been signed just within the last couple of months, clearly indicating to us that this is indeed possible.

However, we are facing a very hard winter and we need to clear any uncertainties on whether or not this legislation could lead to security of supply issues. We do not think it could but, nonetheless, we do not want any uncertainties in a very difficult situation like this. So this is why I propose one year. Some will say it is too much and it wasn't necessary at all. Others will say – as you do, Mr Ehler – that you want a longer time. But I do believe that this is the right compromise.

We also need to make sure that there is a level playing field. And if we postpone this until 2030, not only would we not get the effects that we want with regards to fighting climate change and stopping the emissions of methane, but it would also not be fair to the companies that have actually done a lot of work, made a lot of investments to be able to live up to this legislation from the 1 January already.

paragraphs.text: Comisario, la actual crisis energética no la ha provocado el Reglamento sobre el metano, sino que dependemos de los combustibles fósiles importados. Por tanto, retrasar el Reglamento no va a reducir los precios ni va a generar nuevos suministros. Una vez más la respuesta es acelerar con las energías renovables y reducir esta dependencia, es decir, el Pacto Verde Europeo.

La Comisión —lo ha dicho usted— ha ofrecido flexibilidad sobre las sanciones. El propio Reglamento permite justificar los casos en los que los importadores no consigan obtener toda la información. La Comisión, por cierto, tampoco ha demostrado que las obligaciones que pretende aplazar vayan a provocar una falta de suministro. Por tanto, ¿por qué no utiliza las salvaguardias que ya usted tiene en la mano, resuelve los problemas técnicos pendientes y mantiene la presión para reducir las fugas en lugar de reabrir una legislación que se aprobó hace tan solo dos años?

political_group.label: S&D
political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Dan Jørgensen, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: I very much agree that it is not the Methane Regulation that has led to the crisis that we are in right now. The crisis that we are in right now is often referred to as an energy crisis, but in fact, it would be more precise to say it is a fossil energy crisis.

It is also clear that the combination of several things, first, our decision to get rid of our dependency of Russia – which is one that I hope we all agree was a very wise decision, nonetheless, one that put us under pressure – followed by the crisis in the Middle East and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, has led us to the situation that we are in now.

We are no longer dependent of Russia. We are getting out of that dependency fast and soon we will not be importing any energy from them at all, but we are still importing for, in a normal year, more than EUR 350 billion worth of fossils. So, when the world market price goes up, of course this problem increases. And right now, unfortunately, we are in a situation where we, since the start of the year, have paid more than EUR 100 billion more for our energy than we normally do without getting extra energy, not one single molecule.

So, this is the situation that we stand in the prices of energy. The cost of living has increased for our citizens, it is hurting our competitiveness, there is a lot of uncertainty and then add to that Member States' companies coming to the Commission saying we really need to do something. It is the combination of these factors that has led to me now telling my services to look into the possibility of a one‑year‑long postponement, but of course, not moving away from the overall target and ambition.

Y al final conseguirán tres años, que es lo que no nos podemos permitir. Hay que reducir la dependencia del exterior y aplicar el Pacto Verde Europeo, es decir, más energías renovables.

Piénselo. Piénselo en el colegio. No traigan este aplazamiento, que llevamos dos años y medio de legislatura, que sabemos lo que pasa, que son insaciables, que se quieren cargar todo el Pacto Verde Europeo.
No cometa ese error, comisario.

paragraphs.text: I, of course, share the objective of safeguarding the Green Deal. This is something that the Commission is doing every day. We have also put forward, as you know, many other new proposals within the last year that will help make the Green Deal a reality and even move beyond the grids package, the electrification plan and so forth.

At the same time, we need to be flexible when we are dealing with a transformation of our societies that is as wide-reaching and with consequences as big as the one we are in right now. So when a big majority of Member States in the European Union, many political families in this Chamber, many companies and relevant industry stakeholders come to me and say that they have real worries that this can be a problem for them, and therefore a problem for all of us going into a winter that will be a very tough one – the prices are high now, but I think, unfortunately, that it's almost certain that the prices will be even higher in the winter – then, of course, I have to listen.

We have 47 million people approximately in a normal winter, on average, that are not able to adequately heat their homes. Almost 50 million people. This winter, unfortunately, I fear it's very likely that that number will be higher. So to go into a winter like this with uncertainties, I do not find responsible. And this is why we've put forward this proposal, which I think strikes a very clear balance. There are some in this Chamber that do not want me to touch it at all. There are others that think I should postpone until 2030. What I am proposing is a postponement of one year.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Tisztelt Biztos Úr! Európa energiaellátása már most is bizonytalan. Ezt jól jelzik az energiaárak. A metánkibocsátási rendelet 2024-es hatálybalépése óta a kőolaj ára 35%-kal, a földgázé 14%-kal nőtt. Iparági értékelések szerint az EU-ba importált kőolaj és földgáz túlnyomó része nem felelne meg a rendelet előírásainak. Ezért a teljes körű alkalmazás január 1-jétől újabb jelentős áremelkedéshez vezetne.

Mi, Patrióták, minden platformon jeleztük ezt a Bizottságnak. Ön, Biztos Úr, ennek ellenére még idén júniusban is úgy nyilatkozott, hogy nagyon büszke a metánkibocsátási rendeletre, és nem hajlandó azt elhalasztani. Kérdésem tehát, hogy elismeri-e a Bizottság eddigi álláspontjának tarthatatlanságát a metánrendelet ügyében? Emellett ebből az esetből tanulva tud-e garanciát vállalni arra, hogy az uniós jogszabályok a jövőben nem fogják aláásni az energiaellátás biztonságát, és nem vezetnek magasabb energiaárakhoz?

We have paid more than EUR 100 billion more for our energy sources since February than what we normally do without getting any more energy.

So, the strategy needs to be something that is contrary to what the political family of the gentleman that just posed a question believes in. That is, of course, a green transition – a transition away from fossils into clean energy. So, more renewables as fast as possible, more energy efficiency as fast as possible, stable nuclear supply and in some countries also more nuclear, although that has a little bit longer time frame.
But in no scenario is an increase in import of fossil a part of a solution to get cheaper energy, on the contrary.

paragraphs.text: I have consulted primarily our Member States, but have, of course, been receiving input from a multitude of different actors on the market, both foreign and European. So it is very important for me to say that this postponement of one year rests also on a very clear demand from the Commission's side that we step up on implementation and that that year is used fruitfully, so that in a year we will not stand in the same situation again, because this is a one‑time only postponement of one year that I propose.

Now, obviously this is also a question for co‑legislation, and it has to be discussed both in this House and in the Council, so it's not only up to me and the Commission, but our recommendation is quite clear. We have listened to the concerns. We have proposed a postponement. But, at the same time, we do have to underline that this legislation is one that supports our transition in Europe, and therefore it should be implemented as fast as possible to create a level playing field to reduce emissions and thereby fight climate change, but also for economic reasons.

Methane that is let into the atmosphere is methane that could have been utilised, methane that could have actually been a part of our energy system instead of part of our climate problem. So it is in the interests of everybody to do this as fast as possible. If we look at the most efficient producer countries around the world, you will also see that the ones that are indeed in that category are also the ones that manage to deal with this challenge. Some of them even did it before there was legislation that forced them to it. Why? Because of responsibility to our climate, yes, but certainly also because it is just pure economic common sense to do so.

paragraphs.text: So yes, if you are against this legislation, and if you don't believe that it is necessary for economic or climate reasons, or because you think it's important to have a level playing field, then of course I will not be able to persuade you.

But if you do believe, which the data clearly supports, that it makes economic sense to not emit methane, that is a valuable resource. And we need a level playing field, because there's actually a lot of companies out there that have invested heavily in being able to implement this.

All of these things combined makes it pretty clear that, yes, we do need to do this. We need to do it fast. Now, I would have preferred it to happen 1 January, but because of all of the challenges that I alluded to earlier, we've decided to to listen to those who have come to us and asked us, would it not be a good idea to postpone? And we have said one year. Some wanted to 2030, some wanted three years. We've said one year should be enough.

paragraphs.text: Herr Kommissar! Sie rechtfertigen die Verzögerung der Anwendung der Methanverordnung auf Importe mit Gründen der Energiesicherheit. Doch in Ihrer eigenen Empfehlung von Juni heißt es, dass durch die Bekämpfung von undichten Systemen, Entlüftung und Abfackeln bis zu 200 Milliarden Kubikmeter Gas freigesetzt werden. Die Internationale Energieagentur schätzt ebenfalls, dass weltweit rund 200 Milliarden Kubikmeter durch die Bekämpfung von undichten Systemen et cetera verfügbar gemacht werden könnten, während mehr als 35 Millionen Tonnen Methan aus fossilen Brennstoffen ohne Nettokosten vermieden werden könnten.

Das ist Energieverschwendung, während die Europäerinnen und Europäer mit immer höheren Energiekosten zu kämpfen haben. Warum sollten Haushalte – insbesondere einkommensschwache und energiearme Haushalte – die Kosten für knappes Gas tragen, während es Unternehmen der fossilen Brennstoffindustrie gestattet ist, dieses durch undichte Systeme zu verschwenden? Warum sollten Methanvorschriften nicht durchgesetzt werden, um Verschwendung zu reduzieren, das verfügbare Angebot zu erhöhen und den Druck auf die Energiepreise zu mindern?

paragraphs.text: Monsieur le Commissaire, nous venons de vivre un été extrêmement chaud. La majorité de l'Europe a subi un stress thermique très élevé, et lors des seules vagues de chaleur du mois de juin, c'est plus de 10 000 Européens qui sont morts de ces chaleurs extrêmes. À quoi cela est dû? Cela est dû évidemment au dérèglement climatique. Et ce dérèglement climatique est alimenté par des émissions de méthane. Le méthane est responsable à lui seul d'environ un tiers du dérèglement climatique que nous subissons.

Ce règlement européen sur le méthane est donc un texte majeur de protection de la vie et de la santé de nos citoyens. Son importance est essentielle. Réduire rapidement les émissions de méthane du secteur de l'énergie est l'un des moyens les plus efficaces de freiner le dérèglement climatique, et donc pour protéger la santé et la vie des Européens – cet été 2027 qui arrive, comme ceux qui arrivent ensuite.

Dans ce contexte, le revirement d'Emmanuel Macron sur ce règlement m'inquiète profondément, car il défend non pas l'intérêt des Français, mais les intérêts de Patrick Pouyanné, PDG de Total. Ma question est donc simple: pouvez-vous, Monsieur le Commissaire, vous engager, au nom de la Commission, à défendre pleinement les objectifs fondamentaux de ce règlement pour que la santé des citoyens soit plus importante que le lobby des pétroliers et des gaziers?

Alla crisi in Medio Oriente e alle instabilità geopolitiche si aggiunge un ostacolo regolatorio: il regolamento sul metano. I nuovi requisiti per gli importatori rischiano di aggravare la crisi. Si tratta del 17 % delle nostre disponibilità di carburanti. Questo significa meno capacità industriale, meno occupazione e carburanti più cari. L'Italia e gli Stati membri stanno facendo tutto il possibile per proteggere famiglie e imprese, ma ora anche l'Europa deve fare la propria parte, perché le priorità oggi sono la sicurezza energetica e l'abbassamento dei costi energetici.

paragraphs.text: Many of you are asking the same questions, so therefore, obviously, the answer will also be quite similar. Maybe I can add a few points. One is that this is not a standalone legislation. This is a part of an overall strategy to move away from fossils. It's something that we chose to do a long time ago to fight climate change, but it's also something that we are doing increasingly because of security and because of competitiveness. On security, I think all of us saw, in February 2022, when Russia started their full-scale invasion of Ukraine, just how bad it is for us to be in the pockets of an enemy, which we were, let's be honest. But we managed to move away from that and soon we will no longer have any imports at all from Russia.

But we are still importing way too much energy, fossil energy, from around the planet. And it makes us vulnerable, because it means that when there's a conflict in the Middle East, as there is now, even though we are not even importing that large amounts of energy ourselves from the Middle East, going through the Strait of Hormuz, because it affects the world market, we are then also indirectly affected. Or rather, it's an indirect effect, but it's felt very directly by our citizens and by our companies.

So this is why if you want lower prices, which I'm sure we all do, the strategy can never be to just abolish legislation that will bring down the demand, abolish legislation that will make the production more efficient, abolish legislation that will force, to some extent, our consumers into more sustainable alternatives. It needs to be the opposite. It needs to be looking for solutions that will support this transition.

paragraphs.text: Commissaris, de EU kampt met torenhoge energieprijzen. Europese bedrijven betalen voor aardgas maar liefst 4 tot 5 keer zoveel als hun Amerikaanse concurrenten. Onze energiebevoorrading blijft kwetsbaar en we zijn sterk afhankelijk van ingevoerd gas en lng. paragraphs.text: Well, I totally agree that we need affordable energy, but I don't think that the way to have affordable energy and energy security in the future is to scrap one of our most efficient legislations. This crisis that we're in now is a crisis that will come to an end, of course. But make no mistake, we were also in a crisis in 22, and we can and most probably will face crises in the future.

Our job, in my mind, needs to be to find a way, a strategy to become independent of the world markets, become independent of geopolitical turbulent times so that when shocks hit the world economy, as happened when the Strait of Hormuz was closed, it should not be able to make and have direct implications for the bills of our citizens and our companies.

The only way to do that is get out of our dependencies. That means reducing consumption. That means doing things more rationally. That means not wasting energy, not wasting molecules by flaring them or emitting them to the atmosphere.

I said that you should not be surprised that when you ask the same question, you will also get the same answer. Otherwise, that would actually be a bit strange. paragraphs.text: Panie Komisarzu! W Polsce wschodniej 40 km od granicy z Ukrainą, na Lubelszczyźnie jest kopalnia węgla kamiennego „Bogdanka”. Jedyna nie dotowana przez państwo kopalnia. Kopalnia, która może być wzorem transformacji i powinna być za to premiowana. Na podstawie rozporządzenia metanowego od 2031 roku ograniczenia emisji wyniesie 3 tony na 1000 ton wydobycia węgla. „Bogdanka” już dziś osiąga 0,72 tony, zwiększa swoją efektywność dzięki ogromnemu wysiłkowi pracowników i nakładów finansowych. Jej węgiel trafia również na Ukrainę. Jednocześnie pracownicy potrzebują środków na bezpieczeństwo, inwestycje i transformację.

Panie Komisarzu, transformacja? Absolutnie tak, ale nie kosztem innych bardzo ważnych rzeczy. Artykuł 20 wymaga ciągłego, bezpośredniego pomiaru z bardzo wysoką dokładnością, co jest zrozumiałe. interventions.speaker_label: Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, for too long, our children have been engaging with technologies that were never created with their well-being in mind. Algorithms decide what they see and notifications pull them back in. Platforms compete for every second of their attention.

With the Digital Services Act, we ensured that healthy, safe and secure online environment is more than an objective. It is a law, and it was the first of its kind in the world and with tangible results. Only this year alone, we have adopted 10 preliminary findings on protection of minors online, including on addictive design and on unsafe account settings. However, we have seen that the dangers are growing and new services, features and functionalities have brought new potential harms. That is why we need to ensure safety from the very beginning. We need safety by design and we need to be more strict when it comes to making certain products available.

With the EU Kids Act, we are saying enough is enough. This proposal is very much shaped by the vital work of this House and your calls for further action. In addition, we have also gathered strong evidence, notably through our expert panel convened by President von der Leyen. That is why we have submitted to you a proposal for one set of harmonised rules at EU level – because every child, no matter where they are located, deserves the same high level of protection online. The proposal's key principle is that children's digital experiences must grow with them, in step with their needs and development, fully respecting their rights. The EU Kids Act covers social media, video-sharing platforms, online games, AI companions and chatbots. It proposes proportionate safety-by-design measures and clear prohibitions, along with transparent, agile and effective enforcement.

First, it proposes a gradual and age appropriate approach to social media. The starting point is no autonomous social media accounts before 15. Between 13 and 15, guardians can set up mini accounts that children can use with the supervision of their parents, and with strict time and contact limits. As of 15 years, minors can create accounts on their own without losing protection.

Second, it places safety by design at its core. For all users until 18 years, digital services must meet strict safety-by-design requirements, a clear list of dos and don'ts, such as prohibitions of addictive design, safer settings including prohibiting beauty filters and harmful features increasing social comparisons, safer feeds, effective and easy-to-use tools for guardians, which should be able to set time limits and manage settings. As these tools are often not used by guardians, providers are also required to encourage their rollout, support and agency tools for minors and guardians, and for AI chatbots and companions, no features that mimic personal relationships and foster emotional dependencies.

Third, this act reverses the burden of proof. Let us be clear: it cannot be for the victims to prove that there is harm, but for providers to show that their services are safe for children and compliant with our rules. Before coming into contact with children, services must submit a compliance plan showing how they meet the new rules. And finally, it also adds two crucial elements for the effective protection of our children: age verification and fast enforcement. Online services must verify the age of new users. And this age verification must be privacy-preserving and user-friendly. And this is the standard set by the EU age verification blueprint. To act quickly to protect children, we are also proposing a fast-track enforcement procedure, to conclude within 90 days.

Honourable President, Honourable Members, there is no time to waste when it comes to protecting minors online. That is why we call on you to work to swiftly adopt this proposal, which aims to answer the calls of this House and was shaped by your work and grounded in strong evidence. Enforcement under existing frameworks will continue at the highest speed and with due diligence. I am sure we all agree that the EU Kids Act must become law as soon as possible – because every day counts when it comes to the protection of our children. I look forward to hearing now your views on this.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Commissioner, each generation of parents throughout history will have had their own specific concerns and fears for the well-being and the future of their children. In the past, it might have been about health, safety or enough food to eat, there might have been worries about drugs, crime, about bad influences. Today, for me and for many other parents of young children, the fear is not so much about the dangers of the physical world, but it most certainly is about what happens online.

My children are still too young for social media, but if I look back at the developments over the past ten years, I don't even want to know what the online world will look like by the time my children will start participating in it if we don't intervene now. In the real world, we would never knowingly hand over our children to an addictive environment designed to monitor them, to profile them, to exploit their vulnerabilities and to influence their behaviour for commercial gain. Yet, online, that is precisely what we do.

I don't want to look back in ten years from now and say we saw what was happening, we knew the risks and we did nothing. The EU has a responsibility to act, and we also have the market power to make a difference. It's time to draw a line. Technology must serve our children, not the other way around. And the Kids Act gives us an opportunity to draw that line at the European level. We need enforceable standards that put children's rights and well-being first. We need stronger safeguards, better accountability for platforms, and a digital environment designed with children in mind. And no individual country can tackle this alone. This requires coordinated European action, because our children's safety should not depend on where in Europe they happen to live.
Dear colleagues, the greatest fear of parents have changed over time, but our responsibility has not, so let us together today start by drawing a line together.
