paragraphs.text: Madam President, Vice-President, as a parent, I worry about my child. It is part of them growing up. Nowadays, the effect of online platforms on my daughter worries me the most. It is impossible to bring up children without addictive screens, but for some parents, social media addiction turned into a nightmare of depression and also of self-harm.

Too many families are mourning the loss of a child due to toxic digital products. A staggering 90 % of Europeans want us to regulate social media for our children. Everyone agrees. It shows us how bad things are and that legislation is overdue.

Children are distracted at schools. Their development and mental health is suffering. They lost what it means to be a child free to play without worries and stress. And that is why the Socialists have called for legislation to protect minors online. And we are glad that you listened to European parents that wanted this proposal.

Social media and risky online services are not fit for all ages. We need a minimum age that protects the youngest. Just writing up an age limit is not enough. It needs to be enforced to work in practice. Otherwise we get what we saw in Australia – a paper tiger with plenty of loopholes.

Europe has a chance once again to set a global standard. If we require age verification of users, this should be done in a privacy-conversing way, with zero knowledge protocols and third-party verification. We need to protect the data and the anonymity of Europeans on the internet for all users – children and adults alike.

Protection of minors cannot legitimise surveillance of our personal data. Rather the opposite. This proposal should come hand in hand with an ambitious digital fairness act that will protect all society from the negative impact of big tech business model. Deliberate, addictive design like infinite scrolling, but also dark patterns and unfair dynamic pricing, affect us all.

We need to stop unfair business practices that exploit consumer weaknesses. They have no place on our internal market. As lawmakers, we set the rules on what is acceptable conduct, not the businesses themselves.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! A gyermekek biztonsága és mentális egészsége nem lehet alku tárgya. A digitális világ mindennapjaink része, de vele együtt a képernyőfüggőség, az online zaklatás és a radikalizáció veszélye is. Álláspontunk változatlan: a gyermekek nevelésének elsődleges felelősei a szülők. Európának támogatnia kell őket, a korhatár és a gyermekvédelmi szabályok meghatározása pedig tagállami hatáskör. Az életkor-ellenőrzés a platformok feladata, üzleti érdekeik nem írhatják felül a gyermekek biztonságát. Fel kell lépni a grooming és az online zaklatás ellen, és meg kell akadályozni a gyermekek hozzáférését a pornográf és más káros tartalmakhoz.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, met hun verslavende algoritmes hebben grote socialemediaplatformen het hoofd van onze kinderen overgenomen. We waarschuwen hen voor de risico's van online contacten en we tonen ons bezorgd over de schadelijke impact van sommige videogames. Waarom blijven we dat aanvaarden? Veilig opgroeien is geen luxe, het is een recht. Al decennialang leggen we daarvoor als volwassenen, als politici, maar ook als ouders allerlei regels vast: thuis, op school of in het verkeer. Ik verwelkom dan ook het nieuwe initiatief van de Europese Commissie om dit ook voor de online leefomgeving te doen met de Kids Act. Veel kinderen zitten vandaag gemiddeld 4 tot 6 uur per dag online. Dat is intriest. In de strijd tegen de vaak verwoestende impact van sociale media op kinderen mogen we de ouders niet in de steek laten. We moeten het probleem bij de bron aanpakken, bij de digitale platformen en bij de toezichthouders. Dit is geen achterhoedegevecht tegen de opmars van nieuwe technologie. Dit is een strijd voor de toekomst van onze jeugd.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear Vice President, dear colleagues, 'Please come home to me as soon as possible, my love.' These were the words of an AI chatbot towards a 14-year-old Sewell Setzer, who took his own life a few seconds later. 'I know your mum saw the last one, but you need to seriously think about this... I love you.' And these were the words of a sexual offender towards a 14-year-old girl that he met through Roblox.

So let's not kid ourselves here. Demanding strong AI safeguards for chatbots interacting with our children is not restricting innovation, and blocking unwanted contacts of adults towards minors on social media is not limiting freedom of speech. It's just protecting our children, because, as we've heard, enough is enough. And to all the tech bros listening, we've seen that you can act when you are forced to do so. And now Europe will act too. With our EU KIDS Act, all of us need to make sure that we protect our children before the next message becomes the next tragedy.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, do you know how to make a teenager do something? Tell them they cannot do it. The Commission is proposing a ban on children from social media with the Kids Act, despite data from Australia and expert testimonies from their own panel suggesting that age restrictions have little to no effect. Teenagers can simply lie about their age, use VPNs, use someone else's account or AI-generate an adult ID. And if we want to stop them with mandatory ID checks, we create a whole other problem: putting everyone's privacy at risk.

We all want children to be safe online, but instead of trying to keep them off the internet, why not make the internet safer for everyone? Platforms should be the one to take the responsibility – with safer settings by default, better protection of privacy and transparent neutral algorithms.

And if the Commission really means it, why not broaden the scope of the 15-18 years age category to 15+? How about no toxic social media for all of us, me included – a 33-year-old – you included, everyone?

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, gentile Commissaria Virkkunen, stiamo crescendo purtroppo la prima generazione di bambini che può essere condizionata 24 ore al giorno da ciò che vede su uno schermo. Ansia, dipendenza, modelli irrealistici: tutto questo può avere conseguenze sulla salute mentale dei nostri ragazzi.

Allora, il Kids Act è un patto sicuramente importante, ma le regole da sole non bastano. Purtroppo, gli algoritmi possono costruire gabbie emotive dalle quali un adolescente può non riuscire a uscire. Noi non vogliamo una generazione di zombie davanti a uno schermo. Vogliamo giovani invece capaci di pensare con la propria testa, liberi, critici, se vogliamo anche anticonformisti.

Dobbiamo portare l'educazione digitale nelle scuole. Lo dobbiamo a tutti i ragazzi. Io penso all'esempio di una ragazza che in Italia, proveniva da Asti, a soli dodici anni si è tolta la vita, come denunciano i genitori, proprio per la spirale alimentata dai social. Ecco, lo dobbiamo ai giovani come lei.

Oggi essere analfabeti digitali, tra l'altro, non significa non saper usare uno smartphone, ma significa non accorgerci quando siamo noi a usare lo smartphone o quando è lo smartphone a utilizzare noi. Proteggere i nostri ragazzi significa restituire loro la libertà di alzare gli occhi da uno schermo e riprendersi la propria vita.

interventions.speaker_label: Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, thank you very much for your interventions. The important points you were raising show that there is very strong momentum now and ambition also to move forward quickly.

Like many of you said, during the last years we have seen that the digital environment has been developing very fast, as have business practices. The recommender system of social media, especially, has become more and more personalised, and that is why also now social media has become much more addictive as well. So I hear your calls now for more comprehensive rules that are implemented without delay. We remain fully committed to that.

Our Digital Services Act already requires all platforms to provide a high level of protection. Especially where minors are concerned, a very high level of privacy, security and safety has to be in place. One year ago we already published guidelines for online platforms, but we see that they are implementing them too slowly and that is why we are now making these guidelines binding in our Kids Act proposal.

At the same time, we continue to enforce our DSA – this year alone, 10 preliminary findings against platforms like TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and large pornographic platforms. These cover topics like addictive design for minors and other vulnerable users, as well as unsafe accounts and kids accessing pornography.

Our toolbox also goes further. The Audiovisual Media Services Directive keeps kids safe on video‑sharing platforms, and our AI Act prevents AI systems from exploiting children's vulnerabilities. And we also have the Better internet for kids strategy and Safer Internet Centres. They provide support on the ground. So with the proposal for the EU Kids Act, we are now strengthening our toolbox even further.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, señorías, conectar, compartir, aprender, divertirse. Eso es lo que las redes sociales deberían ofrecer a nuestros menores. Pero esas oportunidades conviven con riesgos que no podemos ignorar: adicción, ciberacoso, contenidos perjudiciales, autolesiones e incluso suicidio.

Las pantallas ocupan un lugar cada vez mayor en nuestras vidas. Un chatbot sustituye el consejo de un adulto. Un algoritmo parece conocerlos mejor que nadie. Y detrás de ese algoritmo, hay quienes buscan retener su atención, sin importar si lo que ven es dañino, ilegal o inadecuado para su edad.

Ante esta realidad, la política tiene que actuar. Por eso celebro que la Comisión Europea haya asumido el reto y que avancemos hacia una propuesta legislativa basada en la evidencia, las recomendaciones de expertos y herramientas concretas de protección.

Nuestro objetivo es claro: no queremos expulsar a los menores de Internet. Queremos que puedan disfrutar de sus oportunidades en un entorno seguro y que la sociedad tenga la garantía de que nuestros menores están protegidos.

Para lograrlo, necesitamos más Europa. La fragmentación no protege mejor a nuestros menores. No necesitamos veintisiete normas distintas, sino una norma común para los veintisiete. Nuestro mercado está abierto a todos los que respeten nuestras condiciones, nuestro mercado, nuestras normas. Y cuando hablamos de menores, nuestra exigencia debe ser máxima.

Señorías, hoy damos un paso para convertir una prioridad política y social en una protección efectiva. Hagámoslo con agilidad, con rigor y con la profundidad que exige ese desafío, porque detrás de esta propuesta hay niños, adolescentes y familias que esperan de nosotros algo más que palabras. Esperan garantías y respuestas.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, cuando hoy le preguntas a un niño con quién habla cuando está triste, uno de cada dos te dirá con un chatbot, con una máquina. Y no es difícil entender por qué.

Para muchos niños y niñas la inteligencia artificial se está convirtiendo en el confidente perfecto, siempre disponible, nunca juzga y siempre te da la razón. Pero aquí está el problema, lo que parece compañía se convierte en esclavitud, porque esa escucha tiene un precio: dependencia emocional, aislamiento y una mente que se acostumbra a no pensar por sí misma. Nuestros hijos no pueden crecer aprendiendo que una máquina es su mejor confidente.

Ante esta realidad saludamos la EU KIDS ACT que obliga a los chatbots y a los compañeros de inteligencia artificial a garantizar los máximos niveles de seguridad y privacidad para menores de dieciocho años y también una edad mínima digital, y prohíbe los diseños adictivos para menores de edad. Hay que regular a nivel europeo y esto va más allá de la IA, también redes sociales y también videojuegos, porque no podemos pedirles a nuestros hijos que aprendan a poner límites mientras las propias tecnologías están diseñadas para no tenerlos.

Así que necesitamos un freno de emergencia para nuestros menores, pero también una Ley de Equidad Digital que combata los diseños adictivos para los adultos. Nos lo piden nuestras familias y también una generación entera.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, avec le KIDS Act, vous fermez les réseaux sociaux aux moins de 15 ans et instaurez une vérification d'âge pour tous. De 13 à 15 ans, un compte tenu par les parents une heure par jour. Pour y rentrer: une vérification certifiée. Macron le voulait, le Conseil constitutionnel a dit non, mais Ursula l'a repris. Aux parents absents, pas d'accès. Aux parents séparés, qui autorise? Bruxelles choisira qui. On a déjà l'article 28 du DSA. Alors, qui veut ces contrôles certifiés? Macron, von der Leyen, qui, pour vendre un narratif aux jeunes, utilisent McFly et Carlito à l'Élysée, ou des jeunes influenceurs pour le discours de SOTEU.

Protéger un mineur, ce n'est pas le contrôle pour tous ni semer la zizanie dans les familles; c'est apprendre à lire ce qu'on lui montre. L'Australie a fermé la porte aux moins de 16 ans: huit jeunes sur dix y sont encore. La Finlande et l'Estonie apprennent à lire un écran, Singapour n'interdit pas. Regardez leur classement PISA.
Vous voulez protéger les mineurs? Nous aussi. Mais alors, commencez par ouvrir une commission d'enquête Epstein et fermez, s'il vous plaît, le site Sexemodel rebaptisé MesLibertines.

paragraphs.text: Г-жо Председател, нашите деца растат в два свята - света, който ние познаваме, но и в един друг свят, свят на светещи екрани, които никога не заспиват. Аз разбирам импулса да затворим напълно вратата към този свят, но това е грешният отговор. Интернет не е стая с една врата, Интернет е като море, а морето не може да се затвори. Но можем да учим децата да плуват и можем да пазим брега.

EU Kids Act иска от всеки да доказва възрастта си на прага на всяка страница. Това не е защита на децата, това е масово наблюдение. Огромни бази с лични данни, край на всяка една анонимност. И всичко това е безсмислено, защото всеки тинейджър знае как да заобиколи тези защити с VPN за броени минути. Когато улиците на един град станат опасни, ние не забраняваме на хората да излизат навън, ние преследваме нарушителите и правим средата безопасна за всички. Същото нещо дължим и на интернет. Да държим отговорни платформите, които пристрастяват децата ни пред екраните, както и да приложим всички закони, които вече имаме. Ние не искаме клетка за децата, а безопасен и свободен свят за тях.

paragraphs.text: Madame la Présidente, Madame la Vice-présidente, chaque semaine, près de 100 jeunes Européens se donnent la mort – 100 jeunes Européens. Et plus les enfants passent de temps sur les réseaux sociaux, plus le risque de suicide augmente. Car sur ces plateformes, le mal-être est décuplé et circule en codes: un drapeau suisse pour "réussir son suicide"; un code-barres pour apprendre à se scarifier. La modération ne fait rien. Les algorithmes, eux, font tout et poussent ces contenus vers les plus fragiles, matin, midi, soir, nuit, les enfermant dans une spirale mortelle.

Mais ce n'est pas une fatalité. Outre-Atlantique, le tournant est historique: Meta et TikTok ont accepté de limiter le temps d'écran des adolescents et de leur couper l'accès la nuit. Pendant ce temps, en Europe, nos enfants ne dorment plus et le DSA, censé les protéger depuis 2023, dort dans un tiroir de la Commission européenne. Il devrait pourtant être le cauchemar des plateformes. Le KIDS Act, que je salue parce qu'il reprend notre rapport de 2025, sera un vrai jalon. Mais il ne s'appliquera pas avant 2028. D'ici là, Madame la Commissaire, qu'attendez-vous? Nous avons voté le DSA au Parlement européen. Appliquez-le pleinement, sanctionnez, allez au-delà des enquêtes préliminaires pour sauver nos enfants du suicide.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, er komen inmiddels wekelijks schokkende onderzoeken uit over onze jongeren. Vandaag nog: 83 % van de meisjes en vrouwen tussen de 12 en 29 jaar voelt zich regelmatig onveilig, zowel online als op straat. Twee weken terug schokte de sterke daling van lhbti-acceptatie onder jongeren, die onder tienerjongens is zelfs gehalveerd, heel Nederland. Ondertussen groeit de vraag van jongeren naar mentale gezondheidszorg. We moeten het onder ogen zien: onlinehaat blijft niet online. De manosfeer en content die zelfbeschadiging verheerlijken blijven niet online. Het heeft echt effect op onze jongeren. Iedere dag dat big tech geld verdient aan roekeloze algoritmes en verslavende apps, vormen zij een regelrecht gevaar voor onze samenleving, onze veiligheid en onze kinderen. We moeten nu ingrijpen. Het verbieden van verslavend ontwerp voor minderjarigen is de eerste stap. Maar ik stel voor dat we die ophef-algoritmes ook volledig verbieden. Laten we alsjeblieft niet doen alsof wij volwassenen wél bestand zijn tegen die manipulatieve trucjes van big tech. Commissaris, ik verwacht dat u stappen neemt om ons allen te beschermen en verslavend ontwerp verbiedt.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, sono molte le cose che possiamo e dobbiamo fare per tutelare i bambini nell'era digitale.

Da ex insegnante credo che l'educazione digitale sessuo-affettiva nelle scuole sia fondamentale. Dobbiamo investire molto di più in questi percorsi. Ma non basta. Servono anche misure di controllo, come l'introduzione di un limite di età per l'utilizzo dei social network a 14 anni, garantendo al tempo stesso il pieno rispetto della privacy.

Numerosi studi scientifici dimostrano quanto sia importante per lo sviluppo psicofisico dei bambini ridurre il tempo trascorso davanti agli schermi e favorire le relazioni, il gioco, lo sport, la lettura.

Ma c'è un problema ancora più urgente che non riguarda soltanto i bambini, ma anche gli adolescenti e gli adulti: il potere tossico delle piattaforme. I social network utilizzano algoritmi progettati per tenerci incollati davanti allo schermo il più a lungo possibile e massimizzare i loro profitti favorendo comportamenti compulsivi e dipendenze. Questo scandalo deve finire. I bambini non devono essere una fonte di profitto.
L'Europa deve avere il coraggio di regolare seriamente le Big Tech e anteporre ai loro sporchi guadagni la salute, i diritti e il benessere dei minori e di tutte le persone.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, first off, parents raise their children and Brussels needs to stay the heck out of it. But it isn't about children's safety at all now, is it? If that were truly the case, you would protect children from sexualised content of gender education, and you would protect them from the disgusting public display of sexual fetishes of the transgender activist community.

No, what you are trying to usher in is yet another instrument to monitor how citizens express themselves online; a means to persecute them. Today, it is just about age verification. Tomorrow, it will be verification of identity. And you've got these plans already in the drawer, haven't you? Eventually, the citizens will wake up in a totalitarian surveillance hellhole – a hellhole which you will then, smirkingly, call our democracy.
Commissioner, withdraw your proposal and deliver to the people what they deserve: freedom from government!

paragraphs.text: Doamnă președintă, doamnă comisar, avem o problemă de abordare, am senzația, pentru că noi discutăm aici despre cum să interzicem adolescenților de 13-15 ani și apoi, cu părinții, să-i supraveghem cu atenție, să mai aibă acces pe rețelele sociale. Dar acești copii sunt inocenți, când intră pe rețelele sociale, nu au nicio vină. De fapt, de vină sunt cei care sunt deja pe rețelele sociale, niște fiare care se ocupă cu trafic de persoane, cu pornografie infantilă și care încearcă să manipuleze acești tineri.

Însă, problema este că acești oameni nu au o identitate asumată. Eu am pe rețele conturi clare, asumate. De ce nu toată lumea are aceste conturi asumate? De ce noi vrem acum să fim interesați de vârstă, dar nu suntem deloc interesați de identitate? Numai cei care vor să facă rău nu își asumă identitatea pe rețele. Și atunci ne putem întreba care este de fapt viitorul acestor rețele? Ele nu au fost construite ca să socializăm (...)

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, Caros Colegas, proteger as crianças no mundo digital começa por preservar o seu direito a crescer, a aprender e a descobrir o mundo para além de um ecrã. Os números demonstram a urgência. Os dados mais recentes da Comissão Europeia mostram que os adolescentes passam, em média, 4 horas e meia por dia na Internet, em dias de semana, e 6 horas por dia ao fim de semana.

Esta realidade claramente exige uma resposta à altura. As crianças devem beneficiar das oportunidades da tecnologia sem que as suas vulnerabilidades sejam exploradas por funcionalidades e por algoritmos. O debate europeu deve procurar este equilíbrio: mais responsabilidade das plataformas, melhores instrumentos para as famílias e um ambiente digital adequado à idade, seguro desde a conceção e centrado na proteção das crianças.

Mas proteger não basta, temos de capacitar e temos de legislar e regular. Precisamos de mais literacia digital, de pensamento crítico, de professores preparados e famílias capazes de acompanhar os jovens. O KIDS Act, articulado com a legislação já existente, será uma ferramenta urgente e fundamental. O objetivo é claro: queremos uma geração que domine a tecnologia e não uma geração dominada pela tecnologia.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Beim Schutz von Kindern reden wir viel über Altersgrenzen, Altersverifikation. Aber welches Problem lösen wir damit? Ein Kind wird ja nicht dadurch sicherer, dass die Plattform sein Alter kennt. Das eigentliche Problem ist ein Geschäftsmodell, das Aufmerksamkeit möglichst lange binden will – durch endloses Scrollen, Benachrichtigungen, personalisierte Empfehlungen und vieles mehr. Das betrifft im Übrigen auch Erwachsene. Die effektive Durchsetzung bestehender Regeln würde allen helfen. Altersverifikation darf nicht zur Beruhigungspille werden. Es wäre fatal, wenn im Hintergrund dieselben ausbeuterischen Systeme einfach weiterlaufen.

Wir brauchen keine Algorithmen und Geschäftsmodelle, die Verletzlichkeit in Profit verwandeln und Aufmerksamkeit als Währung sehen, sondern strukturelle Sicherheit und Privacy by Design. Ein Verbot personalisierter Werbung und manipulativer Designs gerade für Kinder. Was wir nicht brauchen, ist eine digitale Ausweiskontrolle in zahllosen Onlinebereichen.

paragraphs.text: Voorzitter, commissaris, een Europese KIDS-wet is goed bedoeld, maar zoals vaker het geval is, is de weg naar de hel geplaveid met goede bedoelingen. Dit voorstel is daarop geen uitzondering. Een socialmediaverbod is namelijk geen oplossing, want jongeren omzeilen het toch. Maar straks moeten wel alle gebruikers aantonen hoe oud ze zijn. Ook gebruikers van VPN-verbindingen ontkomen daar niet aan. De Commissie tuigt hiermee de infrastructuur op om te weten wie iemand is en schaft effectief het anonieme internet af. Een soort Big Brother-Commissie die alles wat u op het internet doet in het oog houdt. Zo wordt het kind met het badwater weggegooid en vervolgens als excuus gebruikt om onze onlineprivacy af te schaffen. Opvoeden is de taak van ouders, zeker niet van deze Commissie. Kinderen verdienen bescherming, geen Europese voogd.

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, sono le undici di sera e un bambino di dodici anni scorre video nella sua cameretta. Non decide lui cosa vedere. Decide un algoritmo, progettato per non farlo staccare. I genitori in cucina credono che stia dormendo. Bene, questa è la sfida che ci attende.

Guardiamo allora con favore alla proposta della Commissione, perché il Kids Act introduce strumenti importanti: limiti di età, verifica dell'età e sicurezza fin dalla progettazione. Le piattaforme devono fare la loro parte. Le istituzioni devono garantire un quadro di protezione efficace, ma soprattutto le famiglie devono essere messe nelle condizioni di svolgere pienamente il loro ruolo educativo.

Non possiamo lasciare sole le famiglie davanti alla complessità di un ambiente digitale. La protezione dei minori richiede regole chiare e responsabilità condivise. Allora non dimentichiamo che i genitori sono i principali responsabili nell'accompagnare i propri figli verso un uso responsabile e consapevole delle tecnologie digitali.

Infine, ricordiamo che non dobbiamo scegliere tra protezione e libertà. Dobbiamo costruire un ambiente digitale nel quale i nostri figli possano crescere, imparare ed esercitare i propri diritti in sicurezza.

Le piattaforme devono fare la loro parte. Le istituzioni devono garantire un quadro di protezione efficace, ma soprattutto le famiglie devono essere messe nelle condizioni di svolgere pienamente il loro ruolo educativo.

Non possiamo lasciare sole le famiglie davanti alla complessità di un ambiente digitale. La protezione dei minori richiede regole chiare e responsabilità condivise. Allora non dimentichiamo che i genitori sono i principali responsabili nell'accompagnare i propri figli verso un uso responsabile e consapevole delle tecnologie digitali.

Infine, ricordiamo che non dobbiamo scegliere tra protezione e libertà. Dobbiamo costruire un ambiente digitale nel quale i nostri figli possano crescere, imparare ed esercitare i propri diritti in sicurezza.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Kinder schützen, ohne Familien zu bevormunden: Das muss doch unser Ziel sein. Und deshalb geht der Kids Act an vielen Stellen in die falsche Richtung. Der Staat ist kein Elternteil. Brüssel sollte Familien nicht die Bildschirmzeit ihrer Kinder vorschreiben. Und erst recht nicht dürfen wir alle Bürger zwingen, sich im Internet ständig auszuweisen. Kinderschutz darf nicht als Vorwand für Überwachung missbraucht werden.

Stattdessen müssen wir dort ansetzen, wo die Probleme wirklich entstehen: bei den Plattformen. Denn auch Kinder haben ein Recht auf Informationen und auf gesellschaftliche Teilhabe. Deshalb müssen wir Plattformen in die Pflicht nehmen, sichere und altersgerechte Angebote zu schaffen. Süchtig machende Algorithmen, Kostenfallen oder kontaktiert werden durch fremde Erwachsene – dort müssen wir ansetzen. Denn das Internet ist mehr als TikTok-Doomscrolling. Es ist Bildung, es ist Kommunikation, es ist gesellschaftliche Teilhabe.

Deshalb lassen Sie mich das auf den Punkt bringen: Plattformen regulieren, statt Familien zu kontrollieren. Kinder befähigen, statt sie auszusperren. Und mehr Medienkompetenz statt staatlicher Bildschirmzeit.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, Senhora Deputada Hahn, é evidente o poder que as multinacionais do setor digital alcançaram e a capacidade que têm não apenas de influenciar, mas de condicionar o desenvolvimento das crianças. E o interesse comercial dessas multinacionais é antagónico com o interesse no desenvolvimento equilibrado e são das crianças. E a pergunta que lhe faço é a de saber se, na sua perspetiva, na perspetiva dos liberais, é possível proteger as crianças sem enfrentar essas multinacionais que têm esse poder no setor digital? E se aos Estados deve apenas caber a responsabilidade pela regulação ou se é preciso ir mais longe para termos efetivamente medidas eficazes na proteção das crianças no mundo digital?

paragraphs.text: Ich habe mich gefragt, ob Sie mir zugehört haben, lieber Kollege. Denn ich habe sehr klar gesagt, dass wir Plattformen in die Verantwortung nehmen müssen. Ich bin 1989 geboren. Ich kann mich noch erinnern an die Vorhänge in den Videotheken, wo ich als Kind nicht dahinter gekommen bin. Und genauso müssen wir auch darüber reden: Was für Regeln brauchen wir im digitalen Raum, im digitalen Miteinander, dass Kinder sicher und geschützt sind? Aber die Logik kann nicht sein, Kinder auszusperren, sondern sichere Online-Räume für sie zu schaffen, und da sind die Plattformen eben in der Verantwortung.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin! Frau Kommissarin! Natürlich brauchen Kinder mehr Schutz, auch im Internet. Aber Schutz allein macht ja noch kein sicheres Internet oder mündige Erwachsene und deswegen ist es wichtig, dass wir diesen Anlass jetzt nutzen, das alles umfassend zu betrachten. Viele Erwachsene fallen auch auf Falschinformationen rein oder werden süchtig. Ich bin gar nicht komplett dagegen, dass 14-Jährige auch betreut werden von ihren Erwachsenen. Aber ich bin sicher, dass es auch viele 14-Jährige gibt, die ihre Eltern im Internet besser betreuen könnten, als wenn sie da allein unterwegs sind.

Ich glaube, dass wir eigentlich drei Punkte brauchen. Das Erste ist Schutz. Ja, das kann altersgerechte Zugänge bedeuten, aber es muss eben auch Datenschutz und Privatsphäre für Kinderbetreuung bedeuten. Ansonsten haben wir neue Gefahren und weniger Schutz. Zweitens: Ich glaube, dass wir nicht nur Kinder, auch Erwachsene viel besser befähigen müssen, Informationen zu hinterfragen, Mechanismen und Algorithmen etc. zu verstehen. Und drittens brauchen wir Plattformen, die wirklich auch endlich in die Verantwortung genommen werden. Es ist Schluss mit der Appeasement-Politik, hoffe ich jetzt auch langsam. Guter Kinderschutz schützt Kinder ja nicht nur vor Social Media, sondern sorgt dafür, dass das Internet wieder für alle sicherer wird und nicht eine Maschine zur Massenmanipulation von Tech Bros bleibt.

paragraphs.text: Κυρία Πρόεδρε, όταν ανατρέχω στα παιδικά μου χρόνια θυμάμαι μία εντελώς διαφορετική καθημερινότητα, όπου το παιχνίδι, η παρέα, η επικοινωνία είχαν κυρίαρχο, πρωταγωνιστικό ρόλο. Σίγουρα δεν είχαμε μία οθόνη όπου καθ' όλη τη διάρκεια της ημέρας θα διεκδικούσε την προσοχή και το ενδιαφέρον μας.

Σήμερα, δυστυχώς, η εικόνα είναι διαφορετική. Βλέπουμε παιδιά, όλο και μικρότερης ηλικίας, με ένα κινητό στο χέρι, να μεγαλώνουν μέσα σε έναν ψηφιακό κόσμο που πολλές φορές δεν έχει σχεδιαστεί για να τα προστατεύσει, αλλά για να αποσπά την προσοχή τους όσο περισσότερο γίνεται. Και γι' αυτό δεν μπορούμε να ρίχνουμε την ευθύνη μόνο στα παιδιά.

Η ευθύνη είναι δική μας, και κυρίως των ίδιων των πλατφορμών, αλλά ένα ηλικιακό όριο από μόνο του δεν αρκεί. Χρειαζόμαστε ουσιαστικούς κανόνες απέναντι στις εθιστικές πρακτικές, πραγματικούς ελέγχους, ασφαλή σχεδιασμό και αποτελεσματική προστασία των ανηλίκων με σεβασμό στα προσωπικά τους δεδομένα.

Χρειαζόμαστε όμως και κάτι ακόμα: περισσότερες ευκαιρίες για τα παιδιά να σηκώσουν το βλέμμα από την οθόνη, να παίξουν, να αθληθούν, να δημιουργήσουν, να συναντηθούν πραγματικά μεταξύ τους. Γιατί το ζητούμενο δεν είναι να βγάλουμε τα παιδιά από τον ψηφιακό κόσμο, είναι να μην επιτρέψουμε στον ψηφιακό κόσμο να τους στερήσει την παιδική τους ηλικία.

paragraphs.text: Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Most már látjuk, hogy a túlzott socialmedia-használat nem csak függőséget és szorongást okozhat, hanem a lesújtó PISA-eredmények alapján már a gyerekek tanulmányi teljesítményére is hatással lehet. Úgyhogy most már tényleg lépnünk kell. Az internetnek számos előnye van, de nem a gyerekekre tervezték. A cél az online tér biztonságossá tétele, és megtanítani a gyerekeket a felelős használatra. A probléma kezelésére átfogó eszköztárra van szükség: oktatásra, tudatosításra, a meglévő jogszabályok hatékony végrehajtására és a jogi hézagok orvoslására. Erre az utóbbira az EU Kids Act egy fontos eszköz lesz.

Örülök, hogy a Bizottság sok helyen tükrözi a Parlament álláspontját, például egy egységes európai socialmedia-korhatárról, a profilalkotáson alapuló hírfolyamok visszaszorításáról, a biztonságos tervezésről és arról is, hogy kitér az AI chatbotokra és a videojátékokra is. De ne feledkezzünk meg a videojátékokban megjelenő szerencsejátékszerű elemekről sem, például loot box-okról, amire a Bizottság jelenlegi tervezete nem tér ki. Ha a kaszinóba nem mehetnek be a gyerekek a való világban, akkor az online térben miért engednénk be őket oda? A Kids Act tervezet egy jó alap arra, hogy biztonságossá tegyük az online teret a gyerekeknek, és segítsük őket, hogy magabiztosan igazodjanak el benne.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signora Vicepresidente Virkkunen, ho ascoltato il suo intervento. È proprio una rivoluzione quella che sta avvenendo in queste Aule del Parlamento europeo e credo sia importante sottolinearlo.

Ormai abbiamo capito che la responsabilità non può ricadere sui genitori. Sono le piattaforme che devono cambiare il loro atteggiamento, la loro architettura, il modo stesso in cui costruiscono gli spazi digitali abitati dai più giovani. Dobbiamo rispettare dei principi e delle regole, per esempio la protezione dei dati e la salute dei minori.

Purtroppo, le cronache dei giornali di tutta Europa sono piene di storie come quella della giovane Rossella, dodicenne suicida. Allora, per esempio, penso al quindicenne morto folgorato su un traliccio mentre partecipava a una sfida sui social e abbiamo visto più volte piattaforme come TikTok e Meta finire davanti ai tribunali.

Ecco perché il Kids Act è così importante, perché rappresenta una svolta. È questo il cambio di paradigma che aspettavamo: prima viene la sicurezza dei ragazzi e solo dopo il profitto delle piattaforme.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, paní komisařko, kolegyně, kolegové, děti dnes vyrůstají v digitálním světě. Ano. Naším cílem by nemělo být je z něj úplně izolovat, to zkrátka ani není možné, ale spíše naučit je se v něm bezpečně pohybovat. Potřebujeme nastavit jasná pravidla pro platformy. Neměli bychom přehlížet návykové prvky, jako je nekonečné scrollování nebo obsah, který je navržený tak, aby u něj děti zůstaly co nejdéle. Já osobně nemám problém ani s tím, aby byl přístup dětí k sociálním sítím omezený. Ale regulace jako taková sama o sobě nestačí. Potřebujeme se zaměřit na digitální vzdělávání, a to nejen dětí, ale i rodičů. Rodiče musí vědět, jaká rizika na jejich děti v on-line světě čekají a jak s nimi o těchto rizicích mluvit. A děti zase musí samy umět rozpoznat manipulaci, kyberšikanu, závadný obsah a vědět, jak se zachovat v případě, že se s těmito nebezpečnými praktikami setkají. Prostě musí kriticky myslet. My sice můžeme nastavovat pravidla a dbát na to, aby je platformy dodržovaly, ale bezpečí našich dětí to na sto procent nezaručí. Za bezpečí našich dětí totiž zodpovídáme my všichni. Chraňme děti, ale zároveň je připravme na svět, ve kterém budou žít, protože jedině tak zajistíme odolnost nadcházejících generací.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Odgórne zakazy nie będą skuteczne. Przecież świat, w którym wychowujemy dzieci, nigdy nie będzie już wolny, niestety, od algorytmów i sztucznej inteligencji. A więc musimy przygotować dzieci do życia w cyfrowej rzeczywistości. Dzieci potrzebują dorosłych, którzy wyznaczają jasne granice, oraz szkół, uczących uważności i cyfrowych kompetencji. Odporność psychiczna i dyscyplina kształtują się w domu i w szkole.

I przypominam Komisji, że edukacja to wyłączna sprawa państw członkowskich. Dzieci nie mogą stać się zakładnikami Pani kolejnego eksperymentu politycznego, bo on niestety w żaden sposób nie rozwiązuje problemu, tylko przesuwa go w czasie. paragraphs.text: Madam President, I am glad that the Commission is finally catching up on what we, parents, have known for years: that leaving our kids to fend for themselves against addictive digital platforms is a massive mistake. The EU KIDS Act can be a real breakthrough – with one clear standard all across Europe, we can finally stop platforms from treating our children as raw data.

But protecting children isn't and must not be just about bans. We need digital literacy and education so that technology becomes a safe place for growth. The internet can and also should be a safe place for true freedom, for creativity and for connection. But right now, Big Tech does the exact opposite: personalised, polarised, keeping us hooked – that's how they poison our public square and break our democracies. The algorithms breaking our kids mental health are the same ones that are manipulating actually us, the grown ups. We need rules that protect all of us, so our public square belongs to citizens and not to algorithms.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, colleagues, Commissioner, imagine sending a child into a playground with broken swings, sharp edges and predators at the gate, and then telling the child, just be more careful. We would never accept it, yet online, we do exactly that right now. We tell children, look, block, scroll away, protect yourself.

We can't put the whole burden on the child, nor their parents. We must fix the playground, not the child. Behind every screen is a child, curious, trusting, growing. And right now, we are depriving them from their youth.

Europe has tools. Enforce the Digital Service Act and AI Act, demand safer and transparent algorithms and age‑appropriate design, put an age limit on the use of platforms. And when billion‑euro platforms fail our children, there must be real consequences. Enforcement is important. Our laws cannot continue being words on paper.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, paní komisařko, kolegyně, kolegové, ochrana dětí v digitálním světě není otázkou pravice nebo levice. Platformy působí napříč hranicemi, a proto společný evropský postup v tomto případě dává smysl. Škodlivé algoritmy, návykový design a grooming musíme řešit a platformy musí nést skutečnou odpovědnost. Ale dítě nejlépe chrání informovaný rodič, dobrá škola, jeho vlastní odolnost a kritické myšlení. Rodiny, školy a členské státy proto musí mít dostatek prostoru konat. Při tvorbě evropských pravidel bychom však měli dodržet tři zásady. Rodiče musí zůstat klíčovými partnery. Ověření věku musí chránit soukromí a nesmí vést k plošné identifikaci uživatelů. A pravidla proti škodlivému obsahu musí být přesná, aby se nikdy nestala nástrojem cenzury. Chraňme děti před skutečnými riziky digitálního světa, ale chraňme zároveň jejich soukromí a svobodu.

paragraphs.text: Paní předsedající, dámy a pánové, ruku na srdce: Kdybychom si každou vteřinu uvědomovali, co všechno číhá na naše děti v on-line světě, pustili bychom je tam? Vypili bychom si v klidu kávu, zatímco ony koukají na něco na TikToku? Nemyslím si. Naše děti chráníme odmala, když montujeme autosedačky nebo ukládáme prací prášky tam, kam ony nedosáhnou. Jako máma vím, že naše děti nečelí jen nevhodnému obsahu nebo kyberšikaně. Čelí platformám navrženým tak, aby co nejdéle udržely jejich pozornost, využívaly jejich zranitelnosti a vytvářely jim návykové chování. A to mě docela děsí. Ano, nastal čas na přísnější pravidla pro platformy. Pravidla, která naše děti i nás ochrání. Mám ale jedno velké „ale“. Budu sledovat každý návrh Komise a všechny detaily. Jsem pro ochranu dětí. Jsem pro odpovědnost platforem za algoritmy, ale nechci další plošný Chat Control ani databáze se skeny obličejů našich dětí, které by soukromé firmy vytvářely kvůli ověřování věku a které by mohly potom skončit v nelegálním obchodu. Proti tomu budu vždy bojovat.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Frau Kommissarin, ich habe das Gefühl, wir machen in Europa immer wieder den gleichen Fehler: Wir sind supergut darin, über Regulierungen zu diskutieren. Es ist doch nicht so, dass wir keine Regeln im digitalen Bereich haben, die DSGVO, den DSA. Aber wir sind wahnsinnig langsam, das tatsächlich auch einmal umzusetzen. Selbst in Donald Trumps Amerika haben Bundesstaaten mittlerweile Meta verklagt, eine Strafe erwirkt und Regeln durchgesetzt, die wir hier jetzt noch mit neuer Regulierung diskutieren. Wir schaffen immer wieder die nächste Regulierung. Ich bin nicht dagegen, Kids besser im Internet zu schützen, aber es greift doch auch in Wahrheit zu kurz. Die negativen Auswirkungen von Social Media sind nicht nur bei Kindern da. Und wir müssen endlich anfangen, unsere bestehenden Regeln auch effizienter gegen Big Tech durchzusetzen.

Und gleichzeitig bestehen auch Gefahren: Die Privatsphäre, das freie Internet – Altersverifikation bietet ein Risiko für Anonymität und Privatsphäre. Und weiterhin droht die Chatkontrolle, das Überwachen all unserer Chats. Kümmern Sie sich darum, dass wir das freie Europa und das Internet verteidigen.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, we live in a world where parents are aware that if a kid is let out at night in a park, the park might pose problems. It can be a dangerous place. But at the same time, in the evening, a child has full access to the phone, to an internet world which can be even more dangerous.
We have chatbots that look like Disney characters. Behind them, there are criminals trying to take advantage of a child. This is not science fiction. This is what is happening in the world today.
Only half of children across Europe say they feel safe online. It is about cyberbullying, grooming, harmful content, addictive design. It is a wild west with not enough sheriffs on duty.

So, we must act now. Otherwise, we are going to lose a generation that cannot think straight because they have seen atrocities on the internet. We need to get this right and I think we can. We just need to work on it together.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, geschätzte Damen und Herren! Fast 80 Prozent der Jugendlichen zwischen 12 und 15 Jahren informieren sich über das Weltgeschehen über soziale Netzwerke. Das wollen wir doch, oder? Uns gefallen doch hoffentlich allen interessierte junge Menschen. Und ja, dann kann es auch durchaus sein, dass durch diesen freien Informationsfluss nun auch überall in Europa die Zustimmung zu rechten Parteien unter jungen Menschen steigt. Da ist es schon verständlich, dass die etablierten Parteien Angst bekommen, und sogar Angst vor Social Media. Diese Netzwerke sind schließlich viel schwieriger zu kontrollieren als ein öffentlicher Rundfunk oder von staatlichen Förderungen abhängige Mainstream-Medien.

Trotz unzähliger Zensurversuche in Form von DSA und DMA schaffen Sie es nicht, dieser Entwicklung Herr zu werden. Deswegen wird jetzt zum neuen Angriff aufgerufen, und zwar unter dem Deckmantel des Kinderschutzes. Der Kids Act heißt im Endeffekt einfach: keine alternativen Nachrichtenkanäle mehr für junge Erstwähler. Man geht zurück zu den kontrollierten Mainstream-Medien. Ich stimme nicht zu, den Kinderschutz für solche offensichtlich parteistrategischen Maßnahmen herzunehmen. Von mir gibt es nur ein Ja zu echtem Kinderschutz, Ja zur Ermächtigung der Eltern, Nein zu Zensur und Medienkontrolle.

paragraphs.text: Senhora Presidente, este é um tema da maior importância, o da relação das crianças com o mundo digital. As crianças não são adultos em miniatura. São seres humanos que estão ainda num processo de desenvolvimento mental, biológico, cultural e, como tal, os conceitos de liberdade e de responsabilidade que se aplicam aos adultos, evidentemente, não se podem aplicar às crianças, e é por isso que se exige a adopção de legislação com algum caráter proibitivo neste domínio.

Nós estudámos a proposta de Regulamento KIDS apresentada pela Comissão no mês passado e o futuro Regulamento da Equidade Digital, porque entendemos que vão num bom sentido, no sentido de proteção das crianças com aplicação de regras comuns no espaço europeu.

Sabemos que a lei não é suficiente e que as escolas têm aqui um papel absolutamente fundamental a desempenhar. Aliás, os resultados do relatório PISA 2025 confirmam isso mesmo. Há uma tendência negativa que se verificou na última década. Na OCDE, as capacidades no domínio da leitura caíram 28 pontos e, em matemática, 22, entre 2015 e 2025. Um em cada cinco alunos de 15 anos não domina hoje as chamadas competências básicas, contra 16 % em 2020, em matéria séria...

paragraphs.text: Danke, Frau Präsidentin Schaldemose! Vor allem für Ihren Initiativbericht, der ja die Basis für den Kids Act bildet. Ja, Frau Vizepräsidentin, wir können. Die Zeit ist mehr als reif dafür.

Stress, Angst, Schlafprobleme, Einsamkeit: Unsere Kinder sind heute Online-Geschäftsmodellen ausgesetzt, die auf maximale Aufmerksamkeit setzen und durch endloses Scrollen, süchtig machende und sehr schädliche Inhalte die Gesundheit unserer Kinder beeinträchtigen. Daher ist ein EU-weites Mindestalter für soziale Medien unverzichtbar, und es ist schlichtweg nicht zumutbar, dass die Verantwortung allein bei den Eltern liegen soll, die ja selbst sehr oft Ziele von Algorithmen sind. Ja, da braucht es ein Bündel von umfassenden Maßnahmen für eine gesunde digitale Gesellschaft für alle. Deshalb brauchen wir eine konsequente Umsetzung des DSA und auch eine rasche Beschlussfassung des Digital Fairness Act.

paragraphs.text: Fru talman! Alltför många barn och unga mår dåligt på grund av sociala medier i dag. De fastnar i ett skärmberoende, har svårt att stänga av, svårt med skolan och vänskaper – riktiga vänskaper – blir färre. Detta är inte barnens fel, de här tjänsterna är inte utformade för barn. Tvärtom är de utformade för att maximera skärmtid och för att skapa beroenden.

När det gäller det verkliga livet, offline, skulle detta aldrig vara okej. Vi skulle sätta gränser för det vi vet är farligt, precis som vi har gjort när det gäller gränser för tobak, alkohol och att köra bil. Samma sak måste rimligtvis gälla online.
Barn ska självklart kunna fortsätta vara på nätet, men med ett rimligt skydd, såsom till exempel ett säkerhetsbälte.

Jag är glad över att EU-kommissionen har kommit fram med ett förslag som nu ligger på vårt bord, där en tydlig åldersgräns är en del, förbud mot de allra värsta funktionerna är något annat, till exempel oändligt skrollande och riktad reklam till barn. Sådant här ska vi inte ha i EU.
Barnens bästa måste alltid gå före. De är trots allt vår framtid.

paragraphs.text: Catch-the-eye procedure

interventions.text: Catch-the-eye procedure

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I have four lovely children at home. They're growing up now, but they were still small when social media became part of their lives. They were trying to figure it out, and if I'm really honest with you, so was I. At the time, I was a cabinet minister; I was working hard in government. We all know the story, but platforms were working just as hard to try to get my kids' attention. Like many parents, I didn't really fully understand the implications or the perils, and that is why this is so personal to me now.

The EU KIDS Act is our chance to give the next generation of children the protection they deserve – private accounts by default, age checks that respect privacy and action against addictive design. We have to work with children, with parents and families, listen to their experiences and make sure that they help us to shape this act. Children should be free to learn, to connect, to create online engagements without being manipulated by platforms, bullied, or kept scrolling just for somebody else's profit.
So please God, when my children have their children, when we do our job of work here, the online world will be a safe and enjoyable place for all of them to enjoy.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, Paula tenía 13 años cuando un adulto, diez años mayor que ella, la contactó a través de las redes sociales. Se ganó su confianza, quedó con ella, abusó de ella y, después, subió las imágenes a la red.

De estos hay muchos casos. Es un ejemplo desgarrador que nos recuerda la importancia de regular, porque el problema no es solamente a qué edad se entra, sino qué se encuentran cuando entran, quién puede contactarles y qué contenidos les recomienda el algoritmo. Por eso es necesario prohibir los diseños adictivos, esos que están generando impacto en la salud mental, en el desarrollo cognitivo, en la atención, en los resultados educativos... Es absolutamente importante perseguir los algoritmos que exponen contenidos ilegales y nocivos y que los responsables de las plataformas se responsabilicen de esta realidad.

Por eso, Estados miembros como España han intentado regular y, ahora, la Comisión debe dar un paso al frente situando la responsabilidad en las plataformas y no en las familias, y preguntándole a esa derecha que se opone a esta regulación ¿cuál es su solución para proteger a los menores?

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! W dzisiejszej debacie na temat środków ochrony i wsparcia dzieci w świecie cyfrowym chciałem zwrócić uwagę na zjawisko deepfake'ów. To jest zjawisko, które jest bardzo rozpowszechnione w mediach społecznościowych, gdzie wykorzystuje się bardzo często wizerunki osób publicznych, znanych w Polsce, na przykład prezydenta Rzeczpospolitej Karola Nawrockiego czy też jego małżonki po to, żeby wprowadzać w błąd odbiorców, często właśnie dzieci.

Deepfaki dzisiaj stanowią jedno z największych zagrożeń w mediach społecznościowych, ponieważ wprowadzają w błąd nieletnich odbiorców internetu. Dlatego też warto zwrócić szczególną uwagę Komisji Europejskiej na wprowadzanie skutecznych mechanizmów walki z deepfake'ami, ponieważ w moim kraju, w Polsce nawet najwięksi przedsiębiorcy, których wizerunek jest wykorzystywany, nie są w stanie sobie poradzić – na podstawie środków prawnych – z deepfake'ami, które są produkowane przez Metę na Facebooku.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner Virkkunen, we all agree that we must make children safe online. We are all concerned about the very alarming risks that we are discovering with the passing of time. Most of us agree on a number of solutions that haven't really been tried yet, like limiting infinite scrolling, digital curfews – namely in schools, and digital literacy for parents. How many parents across Europe really know about the parental controls online?

The question is, why are we moving with a social media ban when there is already evidence that it is neither effective nor safe? In Australia, 7 in 10 children report that it is easy to circumvent the ban, which actually makes them less safe online because they're unsupervised navigating online with all the risks that we know of. More than 400 specialists at the top of their field have written open letters calling for lawmakers and policymakers to pay attention to the risks of a social media ban.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I stand with Jane Doe, and I am sick and tired of men telling us they will be our protectors, because protectors of whom? There was a group chat of 57 men, and there was not one protector to be found. There was the university board of Cornell, and there was not one protector to be found. If it weren't for abusive men, we wouldn't need protection.

I'm talking about this because this abusive men are also shaping our digital worlds. Every day there's new technologies coming up: we have Meta glasses filming women; we have spyware apps that can track the whereabouts of women, that can track their messages, their cameras; we have nudify apps and in this House, 50 Members were targeted by deepfakes. And it's not just us. It's also young girls who fall victim more and more.
Tech companies compromise the safety of women and girls for profit, and they should be held accountable. From app stores to platforms to AI systems, abusing women can never be a business model.

Οι εταιρείες πρέπει να λογοδοτούν για τον τρόπο που οι αλγόριθμοί τους εκθέτουν τα παιδιά σε επιβλαβές περιεχόμενο και διαφημίσεις, και αν δεν μπορούν να αποδείξουν ότι οι υπηρεσίες τους είναι ασφαλείς, δεν θα πρέπει να τους επιτρέπεται να τις παρέχουν.

Για να αντιμετωπίσουμε αυτές τις πρακτικές, απαιτείται να συμπληρωθεί η πράξη για τα παιδιά από μία φιλόδοξη πράξη για την ψηφιακή δικαιοσύνη, να υιοθετηθούν άμεσα δεσμευτικοί κανόνες κατά του εθιστικού και παραπλανητικού σχεδιασμού, να θεσπιστούν ανεξάρτητοι έλεγχοι και αυστηρές κυρώσεις, να υιοθετηθεί ένα ευρωπαϊκό σχέδιο δράσης για την ψυχική υγεία που θα αντιμετωπίζει τον αντίκτυπο των ψηφιακών τεχνολογιών στους νέους και να ενισχυθεί η εκπαίδευση των παιδιών, για να μπορούν και να αναγνωρίζουν και να αντιμετωπίζουν τους διαδικτυακούς κινδύνους.

Ως πατέρας εφήβων σάς μεταφέρω την απεγνωσμένη κραυγή των γονιών απέναντι σε φοβερούς κινδύνους εθισμού, ψυχικής και συναισθηματικής υγείας και χειραγώγησης, που όλα έχουν στόχο τα παιδιά μας και άλλες δικές τους επιδιώξεις.

Και γιατί είναι ευθύνη δική μας να προστατεύσουμε τα παιδιά μας; Γιατί είναι ανήλικα και γιατί οι κίνδυνοι είναι υπαρκτοί. Γι' αυτό και πρωτοστατώ προσωπικά στην απαγόρευση, με οριζόντια θέσπιση ορίου ηλικίας και ταυτόχρονα ανάληψη δράσης από την Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση για υποχρεωτική προσαρμογή των αλγορίθμων από τις διαδικτυακές πλατφόρμες. Οποιαδήποτε ανοχή για τους γονείς ή κηδεμόνες να προσαρμόζουν το ηλικιακό όριο αναλόγως, τους καθιστά ευάλωτους.

interventions.speaker_label: Henna Virkkunen, Executive Vice-President of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, thank you very much for your interventions. It was very good to listen to the different views expressed today here. I think that today's debate has shown the determination of this House to make the online world a safer place for everybody, but especially for children and the generations to come.

Many of you underlined how important a part of our everyday life the digital world is nowadays, and I very much agree on that. So it is also important to remember all the time – and this is part of our Kids Act – that children also have the right to be connected with friends. They also have the right to have access to information. And that is why we haven't proposed anything like a blanket ban on digital services. But we have proposed here gradual access to really ensure that the content that the kids have access to is age‑appropriate.

We are also prohibiting harmful practices, and here we are speaking, for example, about very excessive screen time, which is very much connected to the addictive design of the services. We are also looking at the kind of content that is recommended for children and also who can see their content, who can be in contact with them. We have to look at these kinds of harmful functionalities and features when we speak about safety by design.

Global and European attention has very much been focused on the age limits. It's an important part of our proposal, and I think it is also very important that we are also able to show that we have an age verification tool also, that you can verify your age without giving your personal data for online platforms. We know that not everyone has had this. So those who have been imposing age limits in other countries outside Europe, they haven't had an age verification tool. It has been a big loophole, but we have one.

I would like to underline that a very important part of our Kids Act is exactly what many of you were calling for: safety by design – all digital services that minors are using, they have to be safe by design. And this is going further, not only covering social media platforms, but also video games and AI chatbots and companions. We have a tailor‑made list for those services laying down the dos and don'ts – what kind of practices there shouldn't be and what there should be – to be included in these features to make sure that they are safe by design.

A very big part of this proposal is really that now we are turning this around, that the social media platforms really have to show beforehand that they are complying with our rules, because now we have a very clear and precise list of the practices which should and shouldn't take place when minors are using those services.

Some of you asked why it's taking so much time to enforce the DSA. When we speak about the DSA, it's horizontal legislation covering all digital services. We have to respect the legal procedure when we are enforcing the rules. So we have to gather evidence, we have to gather information, we also have to have a strong legal basis, and we also have to respect due process. And it's taking time. But now we have very precise rules when it comes to protection of minors and we are complementing our DSA. We continue, of course, to enforce the DSA all the time, but when it comes to the protection of minors, we have very precise rules. They have to come beforehand and show with the compliance plan how they are changing the design of their service.

We are also launching here this fast process for enforcement only in 90 days, because we have also a clear list now that we can check to see if the practices are in place or not. Thank you very much to everybody for the very good contributions to this discussion.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

paragraphs.text: Madam President, dear colleagues, 1 billion euros every day – that was Europe's trade deficit with China last year, and this gap is growing even further. In her State of the Union speech, President von der Leyen told us that words are good, but deeds are better. She was right. For too long we have opened our market without getting the same access in China, for too long we have accepted unfair competition while European companies paid the price, and for too long we have watched China test the limits of international law. Tomorrow, this Parliament can send a clear message: no more dumping, no more spying, and fair competition.

But colleagues, this report is not only about China; it is about us and the role Europe wants to play in the world. Let me ask you one simple question: who are we? Do we open our market of 450 million consumers to cheap Chinese products while China denies our companies the same access? Do we sanction Russia for its war against Ukraine and then look away when Chinese companies help Moscow sustain its war machine? Do we stand for democracy and human rights, but stay silent when Uyghurs and Tibetans suffer? In a world increasingly shaped by Washington or Beijing, does Europe simply choose sides? How do we stand up for our own interests?

Europe wants cooperation with China; we want a strong partnership; we want dialogue and we want to work together wherever we can, but not at any cost. First, our economy. We want fair competition and reciprocity. When China dumps cheap goods on our market, we must use our trade tools, and when China turns our dependence on critical raw materials into a weapon, we must reduce that dependence.

The momentum is growing: France and Germany are now calling for action on the economic imbalances with China. Commissioner, your colleague, Commissioner Šefčovič, will travel to Beijing on Thursday. Kaja Kallas will meet with Wang Yi, and next week European leaders will discuss China at the European Council. They should all carry the same message: no dumping, no spying, no silence. Europe has economic power; it's time we use it.

Second, our security. We will not tolerate Chinese espionage targeting our companies or institutions and our critical infrastructure, and we must be clear on Taiwan: Europe stands by its one-China policy and the status quo in the Taiwan Strait. Peace and stability there are a direct European interest. Third, our values. Partnership cannot mean silence – not on the Uyghurs, not on Tibet and not on Hong Kong. Let me be clear: we do not seek confrontation with China, but we seek a real partnership. That requires reciprocity, respect and trust. As long as those are missing, China remains not only a partner and a competitor, but also a systemic rival.

It has been hard. I want to thank you all. And I look at all the colleagues, Michael, Nacho, everybody who worked very hard on this report. It has been a long journey and we did not always agree, but we did what people expect from politicians – to keep on talking, keep on negotiating and looking for a very good compromise. So tomorrow, let us give our Commission, our Member States and our High Representative the backing to act. At the beginning I asked you, who are we? Tomorrow we get to answer it. Let us show China and above all ourselves what Europe is capable of. Europe has the power. Now Europe must have the political will to use it.

Vicepresidente

PRESIDENZA: ANTONELLA SBERNA

Vicepresidente

interventions.speaker_label: Michael McGrath, Member of the Commission.

paragraphs.text: Madam President, honourable Members, thank you sincerely to the rapporteur, Hilde Vautmans, and all of the Members who contributed to the Parliament's report on EU‑China relations.

Your report accurately captures the complexity of EU‑China relations and it clearly shows the importance of these relations for Europe's security and prosperity. At a time of global challenges, continued dialogue and practical cooperation between the European Union and China are more essential than ever.

Honourable Members, our trade relationship with China is one of the most significant in the world, but it has become heavily unbalanced. Our trade deficit has reached EUR 1 billion a day. This is unsustainable. China's economic progress is not the problem and we welcome competition. But when industrial overcapacity and market distortions threaten Europe's industrial base, European jobs and strategic economic sectors in Europe, we have no choice but to act.

That is why we are currently engaging with China to rebalance our economic and trade relations. As I speak, Commissioner Šefčovič is about to travel to Beijing for the Trade and Investment Consultations with his Chinese counterpart. We are firmly committed to dialogue and finding negotiated solutions, but this dialogue must deliver concrete results.

At the same time, we continue to pursue a European economic security agenda to de‑risk and to diversify our economy. To do this, to avoid deindustrialisation in the industrial heartlands of Europe, we must use all available tools.

And honourable Members when we engage in China, we must engage on what matters to Europe too. China is enabling Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine. Between 80 and 90 % of sensitive dual‑use goods and advanced technology items reach Russia from or through China. These items sustain Russia's military industrial base and therefore present an existential threat to Europe's security. In all our engagements with China – yours and ours – we must keep urging China to halt any support that strengthens Russia's military capacities.

The report rightly addresses the serious human rights situation in China. As a defender of the rules‑based international order, which China is part of, we have a duty to call on China to comply with its obligations under international law, and to respect and protect human rights in the country. This means raising our concerns over systemic human rights violations in Xinjiang, Tibet and Hong Kong, as well as the treatment of human rights defenders across China.

Honourable Members to conclude, managing our relationship with China requires both a values‑based and interest‑driven approach. We must be clear‑eyed about the risks and also the challenges. We must be ready to push back when needed, and we must remain open to engage and to cooperate whenever we can. I look forward to your contributions and to having an opportunity to respond later on in the debate.

interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the PPE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Commissioner, I think that our relationship with China has to be based on some pillars: firmness, transparency, reciprocity, engagement – as you have said. And I think that the report with the recommendations on EU-China political relations takes stock of that and also shows the way to follow in order to have a candid approach to the relations with China. We can no longer afford to be treated as a kind of a weak partner.

We have to recognise that China is behaving in a way that is putting in danger our interests, not only in the trade and commerce sector, but in security and defence. If China wants to be a superpower, it has to help to keep peace, security and stability as part of being a superpower. And it is not abiding by this principle. Sustaining Russia in the war in Ukraine is something we have to raise every time we meet them.

Also, the human rights situation in China has not improved – on the contrary in the last years. And it has disappeared somehow from our agenda in the last years, to be honest. We have to bring to the top of the agenda in order to remind them that Europe is not only a space of commerce and trade, but also a space of human rights, freedom and liberty. In addition to this, we have to remember that no aggression, no unilateral change of the status quo in Taiwan will be accepted by the European Union. We abide by the one‑China policy, and we will not admit any kind of change through coercion or force.
And finally, we ourselves have to do our own homework in order to be more competitive, to engage with China critically, and to deal with them as the systemic rival that they are.

We can no longer afford to be treated as a kind of a weak partner.

We have to recognise that China is behaving in a way that is putting in danger our interests, not only in the trade and commerce sector, but in security and defence. If China wants to be a superpower, it has to help to keep peace, security and stability as part of being a superpower. And it is not abiding by this principle. Sustaining Russia in the war in Ukraine is something we have to raise every time we meet them.

Also, the human rights situation in China has not improved – on the contrary in the last years. And it has disappeared somehow from our agenda in the last years, to be honest. We have to bring to the top of the agenda in order to remind them that Europe is not only a space of commerce and trade, but also a space of human rights, freedom and liberty. In addition to this, we have to remember that no aggression, no unilateral change of the status quo in Taiwan will be accepted by the European Union. We abide by the one‑China policy, and we will not admit any kind of change through coercion or force.

And finally, we ourselves have to do our own homework in order to be more competitive, to engage with China critically, and to deal with them as the systemic rival that they are.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

interventions.speaker_label: Lucia Annunziata, on behalf of the S&D Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the S&D Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, I see there Hilde Vautmans, with whom I have worked for almost a year on this. I think you say something very important: this vote tomorrow is going to say not only something about China but also something about us.

The theme about China is 'What is the best approach?'. And this is what we'll see tomorrow in the vote. There are two ways: one is the confrontational approach that can condemn China to be our systemic rival forever – I speak to Pascal, who supported this idea, and in fact it is the position of the centre right; the other possibility is an articulate approach, taking an extremely strong stance on three points – human rights, the lack of democracy and military expansion, meaning Taiwan.

To the open dialogue on the real issue that now is devastating for us – the imbalanced trade relationship that causes the EU a loss of EUR 1 billion every day, as Hilde Vautmans said before me – I am in favour of the second approach, as has been very clear during this year of negotiation.
Big game is developing the rapprochement between China and the US and if the EU is left out, it is going to be condemned to be a minor player.

political_group.name: Group of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats in the European Parliament

interventions.speaker_label: Juan Carlos Girauta Vidal, en nombre del Grupo PfE.

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, una de las pocas cosas salvables de la anterior legislatura fue el reconocimiento de una realidad: China no es nuestra amiga, sino un riesgo estratégico para Europa. Esa toma de conciencia plasmada por este Parlamento en sus informes debe defenderse de los intentos de socavarla procedentes de Pekín.

Miren a España: mientras Europa intenta cerrar la puerta a la influencia china, el obsolescente presidente Sánchez la ha abierto de par en par y el expresidente Zapatero, amigo de la joyería gratis, aparece una y otra vez en contratos, intermediaciones, dinero e investigaciones vinculadas a intereses chinos.

Los hechos se amontonan. Hemos visto a Zapatero reunido con empresarios chinos en plena tramitación del rescate de la aerolínea Plus Ultra a Huawei; a Huawei contratando a la empresa de las hijas de Zapatero. Hemos visto millones de euros recibidos por el expresidente y sociedades de capital chino apareciendo en el rastro del dinero. Hemos visto a Sánchez multiplicando sus visitas y servilismo a Xi Jinping y, finalmente, al Gobierno socialista abriendo a Huawei las puertas de un sistema tan sensible como las escuchas judiciales. Nada menos.

Pese a que Bruselas viene advirtiendo del riesgo de injerencia extranjera, ¿hasta donde habrán permitido que la voluntad de Pekín penetre en las instituciones y sectores estratégicos? ¿Cuándo dejarán los socialistas españoles de actuar como el caballo de Troya del Partido Comunista Chino?

interventions.speaker_label: Mariusz Kamiński, w imieniu grupy ECR.

paragraphs.text: Pani Przewodnicząca! Debatując dziś na temat relacji między Unią a Chinami, musimy zawsze pamiętać, jaka jest rzeczywista natura tego państwa. Chiny to komunistyczna, totalitarna dyktatura, stanowiąca zagrożenie dla wolnego świata. Sprowadzenie relacji z Chinami do pragmatycznych stosunków gospodarczych jest nie tylko cynizmem, ale nieodpowiedzialną głupotą. Chiny zalewają dziś Europę tanimi, dotowanymi przez państwo towarami, niszcząc europejski przemysł i miejsca pracy. Chińskie technologie wprowadzane do infrastruktury krytycznej stanowią zagrożenie dla naszego bezpieczeństwa. Komunistyczne Chiny wspierają rosyjską agresją na Ukrainie i zapowiadają użycie siły w celu podporządkowania sobie demokratycznego Tajwanu.

Chińskie więzienia wypełnione są tysiącami więźniów politycznych. Symbolicznie wymienię nazwiska kilku bohaterów walki o wolność: Jimmy'ego Laia, skazanego na 20 lat za obronę praw mieszkańców Hongkongu, ujgurskiego profesora Ilhama Tohtiego i tybetańskiego Panczenlamę. Komunistyczny aparat państwowy prowadzi politykę przymusowej asymilacji mniejszości narodowych, niszcząc ich wielowiekową tożsamość i kulturę.

Dlatego też domagamy się, aby Chiny respektowały Kartę Narodów Zjednoczonych, Powszechną Deklarację Praw Człowieka i zasady Światowej Organizacji Handlu. Na poszanowaniu tych zasad muszą opierać się nasze relacje z Pekinem.

interventions.speaker_label: Engin Eroglu, im Namen der Renew-Fraktion.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, sehr geehrter Herr Kommissar! Wir haben heute einen sehr, sehr wichtigen Bericht zu beschließen, der über die Zukunft der Europäischen Union und vielleicht sogar das ganze Jahrhundert entscheiden wird und auch wegweisend sein wird. Das Europäische Parlament hat 2025 wieder angefangen, eigene Beziehungen zur Volksrepublik China aufzubauen, nach vielen Jahren des Stillstands. Ich bin mit sehr vielen Delegationen nach China gereist. Wir haben sehr, sehr viele Kollegen, die eigene Kompetenzen aufgebaut haben. Aber was ist das Ergebnis aus diesen vielen Gesprächen?

Wir sehen einen Gipfel auch mit der Kommission letztes Jahr, Costa und Frau von der Leyen in China. Großer Gipfel, tolle Bilder, kein Resultat. Alle unsere Delegationsreisen, die nach China geführt haben, haben kein Resultat ergeben. Und jetzt müssen wir einen Bericht schreiben, und der Bericht zeichnet ein Bild ab: China wird mehr und mehr ein systemischer Rivale. Nicht weil wir es wollen, weil China innen- und außenpolitisch diese Entscheidungen trifft. Deswegen müssen wir diesen Bericht so abschließen, wie wir ihn machen. Und, Herr Kommissar, ganz, ganz wichtig: Wenn wir handlungsfähig werden wollen, müssen wir wettbewerbsfähiger werden. China kennt nur die Sprache der Stärke und nicht die Sprache der Diplomatie.

interventions.speaker_label: Ville Niinistö, on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: on behalf of the Verts/ALE Group

paragraphs.text: Madam President, Europe needs a clear and united China policy, neither naive dependence nor disengagement. We must cooperate with China where global challenges demand it, especially on issues like climate and biodiversity, but cooperation cannot mean ignoring growing strategic dependencies, unfair economic practices or threats to our security, human rights or democracy.

We also know that China poses a long-term threat to democracies if their path to power is not controlled. China's material support to Russia's military industrial complex is already an issue of particular seriousness. Where Chinese entities enable Russia's war of aggression, Europe must be prepared to respond with targeted, restrictive measures.

Human rights must remain at the centre of our relationship, not be traded away for economic interests. We must also make sure that the green transition strengthens European resilience and strategic autonomy. On Taiwan, we must defend peace, reject coercion and oppose any unilateral change to the status quo.
Europe should engage China from a position of unity, values and resilience, and this report is a good basis for that.

interventions.speaker_label: Danilo Della Valle, a nome del gruppo The Left.
interventions.speaker_role_in_transcript: a nome del gruppo The Left

paragraphs.text: Signora Presidente, signor Commissario, questa relazione è per me un'occasione persa, l'ennesima, perché si poteva scegliere la via del dialogo, della cooperazione, del mutuo interesse e invece si è scelto di compiere un suicidio, avallando il volere del padrone statunitense Trump. Devono essere arrivate le chiamate da Washington anche per congratularsi perché negli Stati Uniti non avrebbero potuto scriverla meglio questa relazione.

Avete deciso di varcare tutte le linee rosse che Pechino aveva, arrivando a chiedere addirittura una presenza navale ed esercitazioni congiunte nell'Indo-Pacifico. Non vi basta la guerra per procura in Europa? Vogliamo mandare i nostri ragazzi a combattere anche fino a Taiwan magari?

Le esportazioni dell'Unione europea verso la Cina valgono circa 200 miliardi di euro l'anno ed esiste un potenziale di crescita enorme. Eppure, siete pronti a sacrificare anche il rapporto con un partner commerciale strategico, mandando all'aria ogni prospettiva di cooperazione con la nuova Via della Seta e fingendo di ignorare che i dazi di Trump costano al PIL dell'Europa circa 50 miliardi l'anno.

Voi mi sa che la pace non la volete, perché questa relazione lo dimostra. Non solo non la volete, ma non la cercate minimamente. Anche nell'ultimo incontro con Trump, il Presidente Xi ha ribadito che Stati Uniti e Cina devono cooperare, che uno scontro porterà solo svantaggi a entrambi e che si può e si deve evitare la trappola di Tucidide.

Pensate di essere trattati alla pari dagli Stati Uniti, ma alla fine hanno deciso di relegarvi al ruolo di abitanti dell'isola di Melo. Siete persino orgogliosi di poter dimostrare alla potenza dominante la vostra subalternità, a costo di fare poi gli utili idioti di fronte alla storia che avanza.
Ancora una volta credo che con questa relazione si è fatta la scelta sbagliata.

interventions.speaker_label: Станислав Стоянов, от името на групата ESN.

paragraphs.text: Г-жо Председател, икономическите проблеми на Европейския съюз се задълбочават. Решаването им изисква повече прагматизъм и предвидими взаимоизгодни отношения с водещите световни икономически сили, а такива отношения изискват доверие. То се изгражда с диалог и сътрудничество, а не с етикети като „системен съперник“.

Търговският дефицит на Европейския съюз с Китай вече надхвърля един милиард евро на ден и продължава да расте. Няма да го намалим с нови ограничения върху вноса и икономическо затваряне. Така това все повече напомня икономическата логика на късния Съветски съюз. Китай има право сам да определя своя модел на развитие, както и ние имаме право да защитаваме собствените си интереси. Вместо да идеологизираме отношенията, нека инвестираме в конкурентоспособност, нови логистични връзки през Черно море и Централна Азия и повече възможности за европейския бизнес да достига световните пазари.
Време е за прагматизъм. Европейският съюз трябва да спре да играе ролята на световен ментор и да започне да защитава икономическите си интереси.

paragraphs.text: Frau Präsidentin, meine sehr geehrten Damen und Herren! Wie Kommissionspräsidentin Ursula von der Leyen es vor drei Wochen genau hier im Parlament formuliert hat: Die Beziehungen zwischen der Europäischen Union und China, sie stehen an einem kritischen Punkt. Chinesische Überkapazitäten, staatliche Subventionen und ungleiche Wettbewerbsbedingungen setzen unsere Unternehmen unter Druck. Gleichzeitig stellen Abhängigkeiten bei kritischen Rohstoffen und Schlüsseltechnologien erhebliche Risiken dar.

Es gilt daher, unsere Lieferketten breiter aufzustellen und für einen fairen Wettbewerb zu sorgen, damit wir als Europäer wirtschaftlich handlungsfähig bleiben und uns nicht erpressbar machen lassen. Darüber hinaus muss China seiner internationalen Verantwortung als ständiges Mitglied des Sicherheitsrates der Vereinten Nationen gerecht werden. Peking muss seinen Einfluss auf den Kreml nutzen, um auf ein Ende des Angriffskrieges gegen die Ukraine hinzuwirken.
Ich wünsche Kommissar Šefčovič viel Erfolg bei seinen wichtigen Gesprächen diese Woche in Peking. Und Hilde Vautmans möchte ich danken für die enormen Bemühungen, diesen Bericht vorzulegen.

political_group.label: PPE
political_group.name: Group of the European People's Party (Christian Democrats)

paragraphs.text: Señora presidenta, nos abstuvimos en la Comisión AFET a pesar de una alineación completa en materia de derechos humanos, protección de nuestra industria y crítica en cuanto a la relación de China con Rusia en relación con Ucrania, pero aún pensamos que hay mucho desarrollo de los aspectos críticos y confrontacionales del papel y menos desarrollo —solo algunas menciones dispersas— de los aspectos de la relación futura, del engagement del que nos hablaba la Comisión —como, por cierto, hacen los Gobiernos europeos de todos los colores con sus semanales peregrinaciones a Pekín—.

Yo creo que es bueno que este Parlamento no parezca estar en otra galaxia política diferente a la de la Comisión, el Consejo y los Estados miembros en lo que respecta a China, y también creo que hay que evitar —como saben los negociadores y como llevamos diciendo un año— aparecer solo como meros ejecutores de la política china de los Estados Unidos. Trump ya está en una página con China distinta de la que, algunas veces, se ve aquí en este ambiente —yo creo que algunos diputados quieren hacernos más trumpistas con China que el propio Trump—.
